events.enhanced_description: On April 7, 2010, Kyrgyz President Kurmanbek Bakiyev fled the country amid fierce anti-government riots in the capital, Bishkek. His departure marked a significant turning point in Kyrgyzstan's political landscape, leading to a change in government.
events.name: Kyrgyz President Kurmanbek Bakiyev flees the country

events.enhanced_description: On April 10, 2010, Polish President Lech Kaczyński was among 96 people killed when their airplane crashed near Smolensk, Russia. The tragedy shocked Poland and led to a national period of mourning, as well as investigations into the causes of the crash.
events.name: The President of Poland dies in a plane crash

events.enhanced_description: On April 14, 2010, volcanic ash from eruptions beneath Mount Eyjafjallajökull in Iceland began to disrupt air traffic across northern and western Europe. The ash cloud led to the cancellation of thousands of flights, affecting millions of travelers and highlighting the impact of natural disasters on modern transportation.
events.name: Volcanic ash disrupts air traffic across Europe

events.enhanced_description: On April 20, 2010, the Deepwater Horizon oil drilling platform exploded in the Gulf of Mexico, killing 11 workers and leading to one of the largest environmental disasters in history. The resulting oil spill had devastating effects on marine life and prompted widespread criticism of BP and offshore drilling practices.
events.name: The Deepwater Horizon oil drilling platform explodes

events.enhanced_description: On April 27, 2010, Standard & Poor's downgraded Greece's sovereign credit rating to junk status, just four days after the activation of a €45 billion EU–IMF bailout. This decision triggered a significant decline in global stock markets and the euro's value, exacerbating the European sovereign debt crisis.
events.name: Standard & Poor's downgrades Greece's sovereign credit rating to junk

events.enhanced_description: Expo 2010, the World Expo hosted in Shanghai, China, opened on May 1, 2010, and ran until October 31, 2010. It was the largest Expo in history, attracting over 70 million visitors and showcasing innovations from around the world under the theme 'Better City, Better Life.'
events.name: Expo 2010 is held in Shanghai, China

events.enhanced_description: In May 2010, five paintings worth approximately €100 million were stolen from the Musée d'Art Moderne de la Ville de Paris. This high-profile art theft included works by renowned artists such as Picasso and Matisse, raising concerns about security in museums.
events.name: Five paintings stolen from Musée d'Art Moderne de la Ville de Paris

events.enhanced_description: On May 2, 2010, the Eurozone and the International Monetary Fund agreed to a €110 billion bailout package for Greece, aimed at stabilizing the country's economy amidst a severe debt crisis. The agreement included stringent austerity measures that sparked widespread protests across the nation.
events.name: Eurozone and IMF agree to a bailout package for Greece

events.enhanced_description: On May 4, 2010, Pablo Picasso's painting 'Nude, Green Leaves and Bust' was sold at auction in New York for a record-breaking $106.5 million, setting a new world record for the most expensive artwork sold at auction at that time. This sale highlighted the growing market for high-value art.

locations.name: New York City, New York, United States

events.name: Nude, Green Leaves and Bust by Pablo Picasso sells in New York

events.enhanced_description: The United Kingdom general election held on May 6, 2010, resulted in a hung parliament, with the Conservative Party winning the most seats but falling short of an outright majority. This led to negotiations between the Conservatives and the Liberal Democrats to form a coalition government, marking a significant shift in British politics.
events.name: 2010 United Kingdom general election results in a hung parliament

events.enhanced_description: The Flash Crash occurred on May 6, 2010, when the U.S. stock market experienced a sudden and severe drop, losing nearly a trillion dollars in market value within 36 minutes. This unprecedented event was triggered by a series of automated trading programs in a feedback loop.
events.name: Flash Crash

events.enhanced_description: On May 7, 2010, Chile officially became the 31st member of the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD), marking a significant milestone in its economic development and commitment to international standards of governance and economic policy.
events.name: Chile becomes the 31st member of the OECD

events.enhanced_description: The Philippine presidential election held on May 10, 2010, resulted in the election of Benigno Aquino III as President. His victory was seen as a mandate for reform and anti-corruption measures in the Philippines, following a campaign focused on transparency and good governance.
events.name: 2010 Philippine presidential election

events.enhanced_description: On May 12, 2010, following the hung parliament from the May 6 general election, the Conservative Party and the Liberal Democrats reached an agreement to form a coalition government. This marked the first coalition government in the UK since World War II, with David Cameron as Prime Minister and Nick Clegg as Deputy Prime Minister.
events.name: Coalition government formed in the UK

events.enhanced_description: On May 19, 2010, protests in Bangkok, Thailand, culminated in a violent military crackdown that resulted in the deaths of 91 people and injuries to over 2,100 others. The protests were part of a larger political struggle in Thailand, reflecting deep divisions within the country.
events.name: Protests in Bangkok end with military crackdown

events.enhanced_description: On May 20, 2010, scientists announced the creation of a functional synthetic genome, a groundbreaking achievement in synthetic biology. This milestone was led by J. Craig Venter and his team, who successfully synthesized a bacterial genome and transplanted it into a host cell, marking a significant advancement in genetic engineering.
events.name: Scientists create a functional synthetic genome

events.enhanced_description: On May 22, 2010, Air India Express Flight 812 overshot the runway while landing at Mangalore International Airport, resulting in the crash that killed 158 of the 166 people on board. This tragic incident highlighted concerns regarding aviation safety in India.
events.name: Air India Express Flight 812 crash

events.enhanced_description: On May 22, 2010, Inter Milan defeated Bayern München 2-0 in the UEFA Champions League Final held at Santiago Bernabéu Stadium in Madrid, Spain. This victory marked Inter's first Champions League title since 2009 and completed a historic treble for the club.
events.name: Inter Milan wins Champions League Final

events.enhanced_description: On May 28, 2010, a coordinated attack on two Ahmadiyya mosques in Lahore, Pakistan, resulted in the deaths of 94 people during Friday prayers. This tragic event highlighted the ongoing persecution faced by the Ahmadiyya community in Pakistan.
events.name: Ahmadiyya mosques massacre in Lahore

events.enhanced_description: The Eurovision Song Contest 2010 took place in Oslo, Norway, on May 29, 2010, where German entrant Lena Meyer-Landrut won with her song 'Satellite.' This victory marked Germany's second win in the history of the contest and was celebrated across the country.

image.caption: The Eurovision Song Contest 2010 hosts at Telenor Arena during rehearsals.
image.date_qualification: Rehearsal image from the contest, rather than the final itself; image date is 2010-05-29.
image.rights_statement: LicenseShortName: CC BY-SA 3.0; UsageTerms: Creative Commons Attribution-Share Alike 3.0; Copyrighted: True

events.name: Eurovision Song Contest 2010

events.enhanced_description: On May 31, 2010, Israeli Navy forces raided a flotilla of ships attempting to break the Gaza blockade, resulting in a violent clash that left nine activists dead. This incident sparked international outrage and heightened tensions in the region.
events.name: Gaza flotilla raid

events.enhanced_description: On June 9, 2010, the Chicago Blackhawks won the Stanley Cup, defeating the Philadelphia Flyers 4-3 in Game 6 of the finals. This victory marked the Blackhawks' first championship since 1961, ending a 49-year title drought.

image.caption: Chicago skyline displaying Blackhawks victory messages on buildings, viewed from Grant Park.
image.date_qualification: 2010-06-10; the night after the championship, not a photograph of the game or trophy presentation.
image.rights_statement: LicenseShortName: CC BY-SA 4.0; UsageTerms: Creative Commons Attribution-Share Alike 4.0; Copyrighted: True

events.name: Chicago Blackhawks win Stanley Cup

events.enhanced_description: In June 2010, ethnic riots erupted in Osh, Kyrgyzstan, primarily between the Kyrgyz and Uzbek communities, leading to significant violence and loss of life. The riots resulted in hundreds of deaths and thousands of injuries, exacerbating ethnic tensions in the region.
events.name: Ethnic riots in Kyrgyzstan

events.enhanced_description: On June 24, 2010, Julia Gillard was elected unopposed as the leader of the Australian Labor Party and subsequently sworn in as the first female Prime Minister of Australia, following the resignation of Kevin Rudd. Her leadership marked a significant milestone in Australian politics.

image.caption: Group portrait of Australian and U.S. officials, including Prime Minister Julia Gillard, after a meeting in Perth.
image.credit: U.S. Department of State from United States — Australian Foreign Minister Smith, Secretary Panetta, Australian Prime Minister Gillard, Secretary Clinton, and Australian Foreign Minister Carr Pose for a Photo
image.date_qualification: A 2012 group portrait, more than two years after Gillard became prime minister; it is contextual to her premiership, not a photograph of her appointment or swearing-in.
image.rights_statement: LicenseShortName: Public domain; UsageTerms: Public domain; Copyrighted: False

events.name: Julia Gillard becomes Prime Minister of Australia

events.enhanced_description: On July 4, 2010, T.J. Joseph, a teacher in Kerala, was assaulted by extremists over an alleged insult to Prophet Mohammed. This incident raised concerns about religious intolerance and freedom of expression in India.
events.name: 2010 assault in Kerala

events.enhanced_description: On July 8, 2010, the Solar Impulse completed its first 24-hour flight powered solely by solar energy, demonstrating the potential of renewable energy in aviation. This landmark achievement was a significant step towards sustainable flight technology.
events.name: First 24-hour flight by a solar-powered plane

events.enhanced_description: In July 2010, a major police operation took place in Tyne and Wear, England, to apprehend a suspect involved in serious crimes. The manhunt drew significant media attention and highlighted issues of public safety.
events.name: 2010 Northumbria Police manhunt

events.enhanced_description: On July 9, 2010, a suicide bombing in Mohmand District, Pakistan, targeted security forces, resulting in numerous casualties. This attack was part of the ongoing conflict involving militant groups in the region.
events.name: Mohmand Agency attack

events.enhanced_description: On July 11, 2010, Spain won the 2010 FIFA World Cup, defeating the Netherlands 1-0 in the final held at Soccer City Stadium in Johannesburg. This victory marked Spain's first World Cup title, solidifying their status as a dominant force in international football.

locations.name: Soccer City Stadium, Johannesburg, Gauteng, South Africa

events.name: 2010 FIFA World Cup Final

events.enhanced_description: On July 13, 2010, Microsoft officially ended extended support for Windows 2000, marking the conclusion of its lifecycle. This decision reflected the company's shift towards newer operating systems and the growing importance of security updates.
events.name: End of extended support for Windows 2000

events.enhanced_description: On July 16, 2010, co-developers Kevin Systrom and Mike Krieger made the first test posts on Instagram in San Francisco. This marked the beginning of a social media platform that would revolutionize photo sharing and social networking.
events.name: First Instagram posts

events.enhanced_description: On July 21, 2010, Slovenia became the 32nd member of the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD). This membership signified Slovenia's commitment to economic cooperation and development with other member countries.
events.name: Slovenia joins OECD

events.enhanced_description: On July 23, 2010, the British-Irish boyband One Direction was formed during the reality show The X Factor in London. The group quickly rose to fame, becoming one of the best-selling music acts in history.

image.caption: One Direction performing at the Scottish Exhibition and Conference Centre in Glasgow.
image.date_qualification: Concert performance during the Take Me Home Tour; this is not an image of the band’s formation. Image date: 2013-02-27.
image.rights_statement: LicenseShortName: CC BY-SA 2.0; UsageTerms: Creative Commons Attribution-Share Alike 2.0; Copyrighted: True

events.name: Formation of One Direction

events.enhanced_description: On July 25, 2010, WikiLeaks published over 90,000 classified military documents detailing the United States' involvement in the War in Afghanistan from 2004 to 2010. This leak raised significant concerns about transparency and accountability in military operations.
events.name: WikiLeaks releases Afghanistan war logs

events.enhanced_description: On July 28, 2010, Airblue Flight 202 crashed near Islamabad, Pakistan, resulting in the deaths of all 152 people on board. The incident raised serious concerns about aviation safety in the region.

image.caption: Portrait of Airblue Airbus A321-200, registration AP-BJB.
image.date_qualification: Photographed 2010-06-24, before the crash on 28 July 2010; this is an aircraft portrait, not a photograph of the crash.
image.rights_statement: LicenseShortName: CC BY-SA 4.0; UsageTerms: Creative Commons Attribution-Share Alike 4.0; Copyrighted: True

events.name: Airblue Flight 202 crash

events.enhanced_description: Beginning on July 29, 2010, heavy monsoon rains caused widespread flooding in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan, leading to over 1,600 deaths and displacing more than a million people. The floods were among the worst in Pakistan's history.
events.name: Flooding in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa

events.enhanced_description: Since 2010, Japan has faced a growing social issue regarding the elderly, with many individuals listed on family registers whose actual status could not be confirmed. This phenomenon raises concerns about elder care and social welfare in an aging society.
events.name: whereabouts of the elderly

events.enhanced_description: On August 6, 2010, a massacre of aid workers occurred in Badakhshan Province, Afghanistan, highlighting the dangers faced by humanitarian workers in conflict zones. The incident drew international condemnation and raised awareness about security issues in Afghanistan.
events.name: 2010 Badakhshan massacre

events.enhanced_description: On August 10, 2010, the World Health Organization declared the H1N1 influenza pandemic officially over, stating that global flu activity had returned to typical seasonal patterns. This marked the end of a significant public health crisis.

image.caption: Map showing reported confirmed H1N1 cases.
image.date_qualification: Dated 2009-05-09; this is earlier than the 2010-08-10 declaration and is not an image of that event.
image.rights_statement: LicenseShortName: Public domain; UsageTerms: Public domain; Copyrighted: False

events.name: WHO declares H1N1 pandemic over

events.enhanced_description: On August 16, 2010, AIRES Flight 8250, a Boeing 737-700, crashed on landing at San Andrés, Colombia. Fortunately, there were no fatalities, but the incident raised concerns about aviation safety in the region.

locations.name: San Andrés, San Andrés and Providencia, Colombia

events.name: AIRES Flight 8250 crash

events.enhanced_description: On August 21, 2010, the Australian federal election resulted in the re-election of Julia Gillard's Labor government, narrowly defeating the Liberal/National Coalition led by Tony Abbott. This election was significant in shaping Australia's political landscape.
events.name: 2010 Australian federal election

events.enhanced_description: On August 23, 2010, the Manila hostage crisis unfolded near the Quirino Grandstand, resulting in the deaths of nine people, including the perpetrator, and injuring nine others. The incident drew international attention and criticism of the Philippine police response.

locations.name: Quirino Grandstand, Manila, Metro Manila, Philippines

events.name: Manila hostage crisis

events.enhanced_description: Beginning on September 1, 2010, a series of bombings in Lahore, Pakistan, targeted religious gatherings and resulted in numerous casualties. These attacks underscored the ongoing sectarian violence and terrorism in the region.
events.name: September 2010 Lahore bombings

events.enhanced_description: On September 4, 2010, a 7.1 magnitude earthquake struck Christchurch, New Zealand, causing extensive damage but no direct fatalities. This event was the first in a series of earthquakes that would devastate the region over the following years.
events.name: Christchurch earthquake

events.enhanced_description: On September 7, 2010, a prison break orchestrated by Boko Haram in Bauchi State, Nigeria, resulted in the escape of numerous inmates. This incident highlighted the growing influence of militant groups in the region and the challenges of maintaining security.
events.name: Bauchi prison break

events.enhanced_description: On September 7, 2010, Israel became the 33rd member of the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD). This membership underscored Israel's commitment to economic cooperation and development on a global scale.
events.name: Israel joins OECD

events.enhanced_description: On September 19, 2010, a series of bomb attacks in Baghdad resulted in significant casualties, reflecting the ongoing violence and instability in Iraq. These attacks were part of a broader pattern of insurgent activity in the country.
events.name: 19 September 2010 Baghdad bombings

events.enhanced_description: On September 22, 2010, the hacktivist group Anonymous initiated Operation Payback, a coordinated cyberattack against multiple corporations and politicians in response to the banning of file-sharing websites. This operation highlighted the growing influence of digital activism.
events.name: Operation Payback initiated by Anonymous

events.enhanced_description: On October 3, 2010, Germany made its final reparation payment related to World War I, concluding a long-standing obligation that had significant economic implications for the country. This event marked the end of a chapter in post-war reparations.
events.name: Germany makes final reparation payment for World War I

events.enhanced_description: From October 3 to October 14, 2010, the 2010 Commonwealth Games were held in Delhi, India. The event brought together athletes from across the Commonwealth and was marked by both celebration and controversy regarding preparations.
events.name: 2010 Commonwealth Games

events.enhanced_description: On October 6, 2010, Instagram was launched, quickly becoming a popular social media platform for photo sharing. Its innovative features and user-friendly interface transformed the way people interacted with photography online.
events.name: Launch of Instagram

events.enhanced_description: On October 10, 2010, the Netherlands Antilles were officially dissolved, leading to a reconfiguration of the islands' political status. This change marked a significant shift in the governance of the Caribbean region.
events.name: Dissolution of the Netherlands Antilles

events.enhanced_description: On October 11, 2010, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu announced he would extend a settlement freeze if the Palestinian leadership recognized Israel as a Jewish state. The proposal was quickly rejected by Palestinian leaders, highlighting ongoing tensions in the region.

image.caption: Cropped portrait of Benjamin Netanyahu.
image.credit: Avi Ohayon — Government Press Office of Israel
image.date_qualification: The image is dated 2023-02-01, more than twelve years after the event; it is used only as a portrait of the central figure.
image.rights_statement: LicenseShortName: CC BY-SA 3.0; UsageTerms: Creative Commons Attribution-Share Alike 3.0; Copyrighted: True

events.name: Netanyahu's settlement freeze offer

events.enhanced_description: On October 12, 2010, a controversial episode titled 'Homoilta' aired on Finland's Yle TV2, leading to the resignation of nearly 50,000 Finns from the Evangelical Lutheran Church. This event sparked significant debate about LGBTQ+ rights and church policies in Finland.
events.name: Controversial Homoilta episode in Finland

events.enhanced_description: On October 22, 2010, the International Space Station (ISS) surpassed the record for the longest continuous human occupation of space, having been continuously inhabited since November 2, 2000. This milestone highlighted the collaborative efforts of multiple space agencies and marked a significant achievement in human space exploration.
events.name: The International Space Station surpasses the record for the longest continuous human occupation of space

events.enhanced_description: On October 23, 2010, finance ministers of the G-20 met in Seoul and agreed to reform the International Monetary Fund (IMF), deciding to shift 6% of the voting shares to developing nations and emerging markets. This agreement aimed to enhance the representation of these nations in global economic governance.
events.name: G-20 finance ministers agree to reform the International Monetary Fund

events.enhanced_description: On October 25, 2010, a devastating earthquake followed by a tsunami struck off the coast of Sumatra, Indonesia, resulting in the deaths of over 400 people and leaving hundreds missing. The disaster highlighted the region's vulnerability to seismic activity and the need for improved disaster preparedness.
events.name: Earthquake and tsunami off the coast of Sumatra, Indonesia

events.enhanced_description: On October 26, 2010, repeated eruptions of Mount Merapi in Central Java, Indonesia, resulted in pyroclastic flows that killed 353 people and forced hundreds of thousands to evacuate. The eruptions were among the most deadly in recent history, emphasizing the risks posed by active volcanoes.

image.caption: False-color ASTER satellite image showing pyroclastic-flow deposits and ash plume around Mount Merapi.
image.date_qualification: Depicts conditions on 2010-11-15, during the ongoing eruption period; it is an aftermath/impact image, not a photograph of the initial 2010-10-26 eruption.
image.rights_statement: LicenseShortName: Public domain; UsageTerms: Public domain; Copyrighted: False

events.name: Eruptions of Mount Merapi volcano

events.enhanced_description: On October 28, 2010, Dilma Rousseff was elected as the first female president of Brazil, marking a significant milestone in the country's political history. Her election represented a breakthrough for women in leadership roles in Brazil and Latin America.
events.name: Dilma Rousseff is elected as Brazil's first female president

events.enhanced_description: On October 31, 2010, the death of Luis Andres Colmenares in Colombia sparked widespread media coverage and public outcry. The circumstances surrounding his death raised questions about justice and accountability in the country.
events.name: death of Luis Andres Colmenares

events.enhanced_description: On October 31, 2010, Expo 2010 concluded in Shanghai, China, after showcasing innovations and cultural exchanges from around the world. The event attracted millions of visitors and highlighted Shanghai's role as a global city.
events.name: Expo 2010 concludes in Shanghai, China

events.enhanced_description: On November 2, 2010, the United States held midterm elections during President Barack Obama's first term, resulting in significant Republican gains in Congress. This shift ended the Democrats' unified control of both the House and Senate.
events.name: 2010 United States elections

events.enhanced_description: On November 4, 2010, Aero Caribbean Flight 883 tragically crashed in central Cuba, resulting in the deaths of all 68 people on board. The incident raised concerns about aviation safety in the region.
events.name: Aero Caribbean Flight 883 crashes

events.enhanced_description: On November 5, 2010, the Turkish Evrim Ağıcı organization was founded, focusing on promoting evolutionary biology and combating creationism in Turkey. This organization represents a significant step in the advocacy for science education in the region.
events.name: The Turkish Evrim Ağıcı organization is founded

events.enhanced_description: On November 11, 2010, the G-20 summit was held in Seoul, South Korea, marking the first time a non-G8 nation hosted the event. The summit focused on global economic recovery and reforming international financial institutions.
events.name: G-20 summit held in Seoul, South Korea

events.enhanced_description: On November 13, 2010, Aung San Suu Kyi, the prominent Burmese opposition leader, was released from house arrest after nearly 15 years of confinement. Her release was celebrated globally and marked a pivotal moment in Myanmar's political landscape.
events.name: Aung San Suu Kyi is released from house arrest

events.enhanced_description: On November 14, 2010, Sebastian Vettel made history by becoming the youngest Formula 1 World Champion at the age of 23. His victory was the culmination of a thrilling four-way championship battle.
events.name: Sebastian Vettel becomes the youngest F1 Champion

events.enhanced_description: On November 17, 2010, researchers at CERN successfully trapped 38 antihydrogen atoms for a brief moment, marking a groundbreaking achievement in the study of antimatter. This experiment opened new avenues for understanding fundamental physics.
events.name: Researchers at CERN trap antihydrogen atoms

events.enhanced_description: On November 20, 2010, participants of the NATO Lisbon summit issued the Lisbon Summit Declaration, outlining the alliance's strategic direction and reaffirming its commitment to collective defense. This summit was crucial in shaping NATO's future policies.
events.name: NATO Lisbon summit issues the Lisbon Summit Declaration

events.enhanced_description: On November 21, 2010, Eurozone countries agreed to a rescue package for Ireland in response to the country's financial crisis. This agreement was part of broader efforts to stabilize the Eurozone during a period of economic uncertainty.
events.name: Eurozone countries agree to a rescue package for Ireland

events.enhanced_description: On November 23, 2010, North Korea shelled Yeonpyeong Island, prompting a military response from South Korea. This incident escalated tensions on the Korean Peninsula and drew widespread international condemnation.
events.name: North Korea shells Yeonpyeong Island

events.enhanced_description: On November 28, 2010, WikiLeaks released over 250,000 American diplomatic cables, including many marked as 'secret' or 'confidential'. This unprecedented leak sparked global discussions about transparency and government accountability.
events.name: WikiLeaks releases American diplomatic cables

events.enhanced_description: On November 29, 2010, the European Union agreed to an €85 billion rescue package for Ireland, aimed at stabilizing the country's economy during a financial crisis. This deal involved contributions from the International Monetary Fund and bilateral loans.
events.name: European Union agrees to a rescue deal for Ireland

events.enhanced_description: In December 2010, Comet Hale-Bopp was rediscovered approximately 30.7 AU away from the Sun, marking a significant moment for astronomers. The comet had previously been observed in 1997, and its reappearance sparked interest in ongoing celestial observations.
events.name: Comet Hale-Bopp found again

events.enhanced_description: On December 7, 2010, a terrorist bombing in Varanasi, India, targeted a crowded area, resulting in numerous casualties. This attack underscored the ongoing threat of terrorism in India and the challenges of maintaining public safety.
events.name: 2010 Varanasi bombing

events.enhanced_description: On December 9, 2010, Estonia officially became the 34th member of the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD). This membership marked a significant step in Estonia's integration into the global economy.
events.name: Estonia becomes the 34th member of the OECD

events.enhanced_description: On December 10, 2010, the 2010 United Nations Climate Change Conference was held in Cancún, Mexico, formally known as COP 16. The conference aimed to address global climate change and build upon previous agreements to reduce greenhouse gas emissions.
events.name: 2010 United Nations Climate Change Conference

events.enhanced_description: On December 17, 2010, the attempted suicide of Mohamed Bouazizi, a street vendor in Sidi Bouzid, Tunisia, sparked the Tunisian Revolution and ignited the wider Arab Spring across the Arab world. His act of protest against police corruption and ill-treatment resonated with many, leading to widespread protests.
events.name: Mohamed Bouazizi's attempted suicide triggers the Tunisian Revolution

events.enhanced_description: On December 21, 2010, a total lunar eclipse occurred on the same day as the Northern winter solstice and Southern summer solstice, marking the first such event since 1638. This rare astronomical event captivated skywatchers around the world.
events.name: Total lunar eclipse on winter solstice

events.enhanced_description: In 2011, the case of Ali Aarrass, a Moroccan-Belgian citizen imprisoned in Morocco on terrorism charges, drew international attention and raised concerns about human rights and due process in the country.
events.name: Ali Aarrass affair

events.enhanced_description: In 2011, the Šamajim festival in Třeboň, Czech Republic, celebrated Jewish culture, showcasing music, art, and traditions. This event aimed to promote cultural understanding and appreciation of Jewish heritage.
events.name: Šamajim 2011

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2011, Estonia officially adopted the Euro as its currency, becoming the 17th member of the Eurozone. This significant economic shift marked Estonia's integration into the European Union's monetary system, reflecting its commitment to European economic stability.
events.name: Estonia officially adopts the Euro currency and becomes the 17th Eurozone country

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2011, a bomb exploded outside a church in Alexandria, Egypt, as Coptic Christians were leaving a New Year service, killing 23 people. This attack highlighted the ongoing sectarian tensions in Egypt and raised concerns about the safety of religious minorities.
events.name: Bombing of Coptic Christians in Alexandria

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2011, a Kolavia-operated aircraft caught fire while taxiing out for take-off in Moscow, resulting in three fatalities and 43 injuries, including four critical cases. This incident raised concerns about aviation safety protocols.
events.name: Kolavia aircraft fire incident

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2011, the song 'A Little Love' by Fiona Fung was released to the public in the Philippines. This release contributed to the cultural landscape of Filipino music and showcased Fung's artistic contributions.
events.name: Release of 'A Little Love' by Fiona Fung

events.enhanced_description: In response to escalating civil unrest, King Hamad bin Isa Al Khalifa declared a three-month state of emergency in Bahrain. This declaration was accompanied by the deployment of troops from the Gulf Cooperation Council to restore order amidst widespread protests.
events.name: Hamad bin Isa Al Khalifa declares a state of emergency in Bahrain

events.enhanced_description: Protests erupted across Syria, demanding democratic reforms and the resignation of President Bashar al-Assad, particularly following the violent suppression of a protest in Daraa. The government's brutal response marked the beginning of the Syrian Civil War, which would last for over a decade.
events.name: Protests in Syria

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2011, the United Nations declared a famine in southern Somalia, marking the first such declaration in over 30 years. The famine was a result of prolonged drought, conflict, and rising food prices, leading to a humanitarian crisis affecting millions.
events.name: Famine declared in southern Somalia

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2011, Mauno Koivisto became the oldest living President of Finland, surpassing Kaarlo Juho Ståhlberg. This milestone reflects the long and impactful political career of Koivisto, who served as President from 1982 to 1994.
events.name: Mauno Koivisto becomes oldest living President of Finland

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2011, a tragic collision occurred between two high-speed trains in Wenzhou, China, resulting in the deaths of 40 people and injuries to 192 others. The incident raised serious concerns about the safety and management of China's rapidly expanding high-speed rail network.
events.name: Wenzhou train collision

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2011, a tragic incident occurred at the Muskingum County Animal Farm in Zanesville, Ohio, where dozens of exotic animals were released from their enclosures. Local law enforcement was forced to hunt and kill 48 animals, including 18 tigers and 17 lions, to protect public safety.
events.name: Zanesville Animal Escape

events.enhanced_description: In 2011, the Basque separatist militant organization ETA announced an end to its 43-year campaign of political violence, which had resulted in over 800 deaths since its inception in 1968. This declaration marked a significant moment in Spain's efforts to achieve peace in the Basque region.
events.name: ETA Ends Campaign

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2011, Michael D. Higgins was elected as the President of Ireland, marking a significant moment in Irish politics. His presidency is noted for its focus on social justice and cultural issues.
events.name: Election of Michael D. Higgins

events.enhanced_description: In 2011, UNESCO admitted Palestine as a member state following a vote that saw 107 member states in favor and 14 against. This decision was significant in the context of Palestinian statehood and international recognition.
events.name: UNESCO Admits Palestine

events.enhanced_description: In 2011, Takaud Savings and Pensions B.S.C., a provider of savings and pension services, was founded in Bahrain. This establishment marked a significant development in the financial services sector in the region.
events.name: Takaud Savings and Pensions Founded

events.enhanced_description: On January 4, 2011, Mohamed Bouazizi, a street vendor in Sidi Bouzid, Tunisia, died from injuries sustained after setting himself on fire in protest against police corruption and ill-treatment. His tragic act ignited widespread protests across Tunisia and inspired the broader Arab Spring movement.

locations.name: Sidi Bouzid, Sidi Bouzid Governorate, Tunisia

events.name: Death of Mohamed Bouazizi

events.enhanced_description: On January 5, 2011, the internet vigilante group Anonymous initiated a series of Denial of Service (DoS) attacks against government websites in Syria, Tunisia, Bahrain, Egypt, Libya, and Jordan. This action was a response to the ongoing Arab Spring protests, showcasing the intersection of technology and activism.
events.name: Anonymous launches DoS attacks

events.enhanced_description: On January 9, 2011, Iran Air Flight 277 crashed near Orumiyeh, Iran, resulting in the tragic loss of 78 lives. The incident highlighted ongoing concerns regarding aviation safety in the region.
events.name: Iran Air Flight 277 crash

events.enhanced_description: On January 14, 2011, after a month of escalating protests against his regime, Tunisian President Zine El Abidine Ben Ali fled to Saudi Arabia, marking the collapse of his 23-year rule. This event was pivotal in the Arab Spring, inspiring uprisings across the Arab world.
events.name: Fall of the Tunisian government

events.enhanced_description: On January 15, 2011, the results of the South Sudanese independence referendum were announced, with an overwhelming majority voting in favor of independence. This pivotal moment set the stage for the formal establishment of South Sudan as a sovereign nation in July 2011.

image.caption: Map of Southern Sudan, recolored green for a referendum infobox.

events.enhanced_description: On January 24, 2011, a bombing at Domodedovo International Airport in Moscow resulted in the deaths of 37 people and injuries to over 180 others. This tragic event underscored ongoing security concerns in Russia and the threat of terrorism.
events.name: Domodedovo International Airport bombing

events.enhanced_description: On January 25, 2011, the 2011 Egyptian revolution began, marking a significant moment in the Arab Spring. Citizens took to the streets demanding the resignation of President Hosni Mubarak, leading to widespread protests and civil unrest.
events.name: Beginning of the 2011 Egyptian revolution

events.enhanced_description: On January 27, 2011, astronomers documented H1504+65, a white dwarf star located in the Ursa Minor constellation, noted for having the hottest known surface temperature in the universe at 200,000 K. This discovery contributed to the understanding of stellar evolution and extreme astrophysical phenomena.

events.enhanced_description: On January 28, 2011, the 'Friday of Anger' marked a pivotal day in the Egyptian revolution, where protestors clashed with security forces, resulting in over 600 deaths. This day became a symbol of the struggle against the regime of President Hosni Mubarak.
events.name: Friday of Anger

events.enhanced_description: On February 11, 2011, Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak resigned after 18 days of mass protests demanding his ouster. His departure marked a significant turning point in the Egyptian revolution and the broader Arab Spring.
events.name: Resignation of Hosni Mubarak

events.enhanced_description: On February 15, 2011, the First Libyan Civil War began as protests erupted against the regime of Muammar Gaddafi. This conflict would lead to significant political upheaval and humanitarian crises in Libya.
events.name: Start of the First Libyan Civil War

events.enhanced_description: On February 16, 2011, a series of explosions occurred at an ammunition depot in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania, resulting in significant casualties and damage. The explosions were attributed to negligence and poor safety standards in the storage of munitions.
events.name: 2011 Dar es Salaam explosions

events.enhanced_description: On February 17, 2011, protesters in Bahrain referred to this day as 'Bloody Thursday' due to violent clashes with security forces during their national uprising. The event marked a significant escalation in the protests demanding political reform and greater freedoms.
events.name: Bahrain Bloody Thursday

events.enhanced_description: On March 6, 2011, the civil uprising phase of the Syrian Civil War was triggered when 15 youths were arrested in Daraa for graffiti denouncing President Bashar al-Assad's regime. This event marked the beginning of a protracted and devastating conflict.
events.name: Beginning of the Syrian Civil War

events.enhanced_description: On March 11, 2011, a 9.1-magnitude earthquake struck off the coast of Japan, triggering a massive tsunami that resulted in the deaths of 19,759 people and left thousands missing. The disaster also caused significant damage to the Fukushima Daiichi Nuclear Power Plant, leading to a nuclear crisis.

events.enhanced_description: On March 14, 2011, uncertainty surrounding Libyan oil production due to the ongoing civil unrest caused crude oil prices to spike by 20% over a two-week period. This surge contributed to the global energy crisis of 2011.
events.name: Rise in crude oil prices due to Libyan crisis

events.enhanced_description: On March 15, 2011, Egypt's Ministry of Interior announced the dissolution of the State Security Investigations Service, a notorious agency accused of human rights abuses. This decision was part of the broader reforms following the revolution and reflected the demands of the protestors.
events.name: Dissolution of State Security Investigations Service in Egypt

events.enhanced_description: On March 17, 2011, the United Nations Security Council voted 10-0 to establish a no-fly zone over Libya in response to the government's violent crackdown on civilians. This resolution paved the way for international military intervention.
events.name: UN Security Council votes for no-fly zone over Libya

events.enhanced_description: On March 19, 2011, military intervention in Libya began following the UN Security Council's authorization under Resolution 1973. French fighter jets conducted reconnaissance flights over Libya, marking the start of international military operations against Muammar Gaddafi's forces.
events.name: Military intervention in Libya begins

events.enhanced_description: On April 2, 2011, the final match of the 2011 Cricket World Cup was held in Mumbai, India, where India triumphed over Sri Lanka to claim the championship. This event was a significant moment in cricket history, celebrated by millions across the subcontinent.
events.name: 2011 Cricket World Cup Final

events.enhanced_description: The Israel Defense Forces successfully intercepted a BM-21 Grad missile launched from Gaza using the Iron Dome missile defense system. This event marked a significant milestone as it was the first successful interception of a short-range missile.
events.name: Iron Dome intercepts missile from Gaza

events.enhanced_description: Former Ivorian President Laurent Gbagbo was arrested in his home in Abidjan by supporters of elected President Alassane Ouattara, with assistance from French forces. This event effectively marked the conclusion of the 2010-2011 Ivorian crisis and civil war.
events.name: Arrest of Laurent Gbagbo

events.enhanced_description: In response to rampant abuses by local drug cartels, the town of Cherán in Michoacán was taken over by vigilantes. This new governance focused on crime reduction and environmental preservation, marking a significant shift in local power dynamics.
events.name: Vigilante takeover in Cherán

events.enhanced_description: The 2011 PlayStation Network outage began, resulting in one of the largest data breaches in history, compromising personal data from 77 million accounts. The outage lasted for 23 days, significantly impacting users and the gaming industry.
events.name: PlayStation Network outage

events.enhanced_description: The Dupont de Ligonnès case emerged on April 21, 2011, when the bodies of a family were discovered in Nantes, France, leading to an extensive investigation into the disappearance of the father, Xavier Dupont de Ligonnès. The case remains unsolved and has garnered significant media attention.
events.name: Dupont de Ligonnès murders and disappearance

events.enhanced_description: The 2011 Guantanamo Bay files leak occurred, with WikiLeaks and other organizations publishing 779 classified documents regarding detainees held at Guantanamo Bay. The documents revealed that many detainees were held without trial, including innocent citizens from Afghanistan and Pakistan.
events.name: Guantanamo Bay files leak

events.enhanced_description: The wedding of Prince William, Duke of Cambridge, and Catherine Middleton took place at Westminster Abbey in London, attracting an estimated two billion viewers worldwide. This royal event was celebrated for its grandeur and significance in British culture.
events.name: Wedding of Prince William and Catherine Middleton

events.enhanced_description: U.S. President Barack Obama announced the death of Osama bin Laden, the founder and leader of Al-Qaeda, during a military operation in Abbottabad, Pakistan. This event marked a significant moment in the fight against terrorism and U.S. foreign policy.
events.name: Announcement of Osama bin Laden's death

events.enhanced_description: On May 2, 2011, Osama bin Laden, the founder of al-Qaeda and mastermind behind the September 11 attacks, was killed in a U.S. Navy SEAL operation at his compound in Abbottabad, Pakistan. This event marked a significant moment in the U.S. War on Terror and was met with widespread reactions globally.
events.name: Death of Osama bin Laden

events.name: Eurovision Song Contest 2011

events.enhanced_description: A 5.1 magnitude earthquake struck southern Spain, resulting in the deaths of 9 individuals and injuring over 400. This natural disaster highlighted the region's vulnerability to seismic activity.

events.enhanced_description: The European Union agreed to a €78 billion rescue deal for Portugal, aimed at stabilizing the country's economy during the Eurozone crisis. The bailout was to be financed through the European Financial Stabilisation Mechanism, the European Financial Stability Facility, and the International Monetary Fund.
events.name: EU rescue deal for Portugal

events.enhanced_description: Grímsvötn, Iceland's most active volcano, erupted, causing significant disruptions to air travel across Northwestern Europe. The eruption led to widespread cancellations and delays, affecting thousands of travelers.

events.enhanced_description: An EF5 tornado struck Joplin, Missouri, resulting in 158 fatalities and injuring over 1,150 people. This devastating tornado was one of the deadliest in U.S. history, causing extensive damage to the city.
events.name: Joplin tornado

events.enhanced_description: Former Bosnian Serb Army commander Ratko Mladić, wanted for genocide and war crimes, was arrested in Serbia. His capture was a significant development in the pursuit of justice for war crimes committed during the Bosnian War.
events.name: Arrest of Ratko Mladić

events.enhanced_description: Chile's Puyehue volcano erupted, leading to widespread air traffic cancellations across South America, New Zealand, and Australia. The eruption forced the evacuation of over 3,000 people, highlighting the impact of volcanic activity on human safety and travel.
events.name: Puyehue volcano eruption

events.enhanced_description: Twitch.tv, a video game-focused live streaming service, was launched as a spinoff from Justin.tv. This platform would go on to revolutionize the gaming industry and online content creation.
events.name: Launch of Twitch

events.enhanced_description: A riot broke out in Vancouver, British Columbia, following the Boston Bruins' victory over the Vancouver Canucks in game seven of the 2011 Stanley Cup Finals. The unrest resulted in significant property damage and highlighted the passionate nature of sports fandom.
events.name: Vancouver riot

events.enhanced_description: Former Winter Hill Gang leader James 'Whitey' Bulger was arrested in Santa Monica, California, following an anonymous tip. His capture marked a significant moment in the long pursuit of one of America's most wanted fugitives.
events.name: Arrest of James Bulger

events.enhanced_description: The 2011 FIFA Women's World Cup took place in Germany, culminating in Japan's victory over the United States in the final match. This tournament showcased the growing popularity and competitiveness of women's soccer on the global stage.
events.name: FIFA Women's World Cup 2011

events.enhanced_description: The Food and Agriculture Organization announced the global eradication of rinderpest, a cattle plague that had caused significant agricultural losses. This achievement marked a milestone in veterinary science and animal health.
events.name: Eradication of rinderpest

events.enhanced_description: The International Olympic Committee awarded PyeongChang the right to host the 2018 Winter Olympics. This decision was a significant achievement for South Korea, showcasing its capability to host major international sporting events.

events.name: Neptune completes its first orbit since discovery

events.enhanced_description: On July 14, 2011, South Sudan was officially admitted as the 193rd member of the United Nations, following its declaration of independence from Sudan on July 9, 2011. events.enhanced_description: On July 14, 2011, two frontal systems caused significant snowfall in south-central Chile, leading to thousands of people being isolated due to blocked roads and disrupted services. The heavy snowfalls highlighted the vulnerability of the region to extreme weather events.

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2011, Goran Hadžić was detained in Serbia, becoming the last of 161 individuals indicted by the International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia for war crimes committed during the Yugoslav Wars. His arrest marked a significant moment in the pursuit of justice for the atrocities of the conflict.
events.name: Goran Hadžić detained in Serbia

events.enhanced_description: On July 21, 2011, Space Shuttle Atlantis successfully landed at Kennedy Space Center, concluding the STS-135 mission and marking the end of NASA's Space Shuttle program. This event represented a significant transition in human spaceflight as NASA shifted its focus to new exploration initiatives.

events.enhanced_description: On July 22, 2011, Anders Behring Breivik carried out a devastating attack in Norway, first detonating a bomb in Oslo that killed eight people, followed by a mass shooting at a Workers' Youth League camp on the island of Utøya, resulting in 69 additional fatalities. This tragic event shocked the nation and raised questions about security and extremism.
events.name: Norway attacks by Anders Behring Breivik

events.enhanced_description: On July 23, 2011, renowned singer Amy Winehouse was found dead at her home in London due to alcohol poisoning, at the age of 27. Her untimely death highlighted the struggles of addiction and mental health in the music industry.
events.name: Amy Winehouse dies in London

events.enhanced_description: On July 31, 2011, Thailand faced severe flooding that affected over 12.8 million people, with damages estimated at 1,440 billion baht (approximately US$45 billion). The floods submerged many areas, leading to significant loss of life and economic disruption.
events.name: Severe flooding in Thailand

events.enhanced_description: In August 2011, Savannah Dietrich, a teenager from Louisville, Kentucky, became a public figure after she publicly identified her rapists, defying a court order. Her case sparked a national conversation about sexual assault, victim rights, and the legal system.
events.name: Sexual assault of Savannah Dietrich

events.enhanced_description: In August 2011, stock exchanges worldwide experienced heavy losses driven by fears of contagion from the European sovereign debt crisis and the credit rating downgrade resulting from the United States debt-ceiling crisis. This period of financial instability had significant implications for global markets.
events.name: Global stock market losses due to debt crisis

events.enhanced_description: On August 5, 2011, the United States experienced a historic downgrade of its credit rating by Standard & Poor's from AAA to AA+, reflecting concerns over the government's fiscal policies and debt levels. This event had significant implications for the global economy.
events.name: United States federal government credit-rating downgrade

events.enhanced_description: On August 5, 2011, NASA announced that its Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter had captured photographic evidence suggesting the presence of possible liquid water on Mars during warm seasons. This discovery fueled further interest in the potential for life on the Red Planet.
events.name: NASA Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter findings

events.enhanced_description: On August 8, 2011, a letter bomb exploded at Monterrey Tech, a prestigious university in Mexico, injuring several individuals. This incident highlighted the ongoing violence and threats posed by organized crime in the region.
events.name: Monterrey Tech bombing

events.enhanced_description: On August 20, 2011, First Air Flight 6560, a Boeing 737-210C, crashed while approaching Resolute Bay Airport in Nunavut, Canada, resulting in the deaths of 12 out of the 15 occupants onboard. The incident raised concerns about aviation safety in remote areas.
events.name: First Air Flight 6560 crash

events.enhanced_description: On August 20, 2011, Libyan rebels successfully took control of the capital city, Tripoli, effectively overthrowing the government of Muammar Gaddafi. This event marked a pivotal moment in the Libyan Civil War and the broader Arab Spring movement.
events.name: Libyan rebels take control of Tripoli

events.enhanced_description: On August 24, 2011, authorities in Ukraine arrested several individuals in connection with an alleged terrorist plot in Boryspil, near Kyiv. This case underscored ongoing security concerns in the region amidst rising tensions.
events.name: Vasylkiv terrorists case

events.enhanced_description: On August 26, 2011, a bombing at the United Nations office in Abuja, Nigeria, resulted in multiple casualties and injuries. The attack was attributed to the militant group Boko Haram, marking a significant escalation in their violent campaign.
events.name: 2011 Abuja United Nations bombing

events.enhanced_description: On September 5, 2011, India and Bangladesh signed a historic pact to resolve their 40-year border demarcation dispute. This agreement aimed to enhance bilateral relations and improve security along the border.
events.name: India and Bangladesh border pact

events.enhanced_description: On September 10, 2011, the MV Spice Islander I sank off the coast of Zanzibar, carrying at least 800 people. The tragedy resulted in the deaths of 240 individuals, raising concerns about maritime safety regulations in the region.
events.name: MV Spice Islander I sinking

events.enhanced_description: On September 12, 2011, a petrol pipeline explosion in Nairobi resulted in approximately 100 fatalities. The disaster highlighted the dangers associated with urban infrastructure and the need for improved safety measures.
events.name: Petrol pipeline explosion in Nairobi

events.enhanced_description: On September 16, 2011, Snapchat was launched, introducing a new way for users to share photos and videos that disappear after being viewed. This innovative platform quickly gained popularity and transformed social media communication.
events.name: Snapchat launched

events.enhanced_description: On September 17, 2011, the Occupy Wall Street protests began in New York City, representing a grassroots movement against economic inequality and corporate influence in politics. The protests quickly spread to over 80 countries, becoming a global phenomenon.

locations.name: New York City, New York, United States

events.name: Occupy Wall Street protests begin

events.enhanced_description: On September 19, 2011, the United Nations launched a $357 million appeal for victims of the 2011 Sindh floods in Pakistan, which resulted in 436 deaths and widespread devastation. The appeal aimed to provide humanitarian assistance to those affected by the disaster.
events.name: UN appeal for Sindh flood victims

events.enhanced_description: On September 25, 2011, a suicide bomber attacked a crowded area in Karbala, Iraq, resulting in numerous deaths and injuries. This attack was part of a broader pattern of sectarian violence in the region.
events.name: 2011 Karbala bombing

events.enhanced_description: In October 2011, severe flooding along the Mekong River in Cambodia resulted in a tragic death toll of 207 people. The floods were exacerbated by heavy rainfall and the overflow of the river, leading to widespread destruction and displacement of communities.
events.name: Flooding of Cambodia's Mekong River

events.enhanced_description: On October 18, 2011, a significant prisoner exchange took place between Israel and Hamas, resulting in the release of Israeli soldier Gilad Shalit after five years in captivity. In exchange, Israel released 1,027 Palestinian and Israeli-Arab prisoners, including many convicted of serious offenses.
events.name: Gilad Shalit prisoner exchange

events.enhanced_description: On October 20, 2011, Libyan leader Muammar Gaddafi was killed in his hometown of Sirte during the Libyan Civil War. His death marked a significant turning point in the conflict, leading to the National Transitional Council gaining control of the city and effectively ending Gaddafi's 42-year rule.
events.name: Death of Muammar Gaddafi

events.enhanced_description: On October 23, 2011, the 2011 Rugby World Cup concluded in New Zealand, with the host nation emerging victorious. This event was a significant highlight in the world of rugby and showcased New Zealand's rich sporting culture.
events.name: 2011 Rugby World Cup held in New Zealand

events.enhanced_description: On October 27, 2011, following an emergency meeting in Brussels, the European Union announced a comprehensive agreement to address the European sovereign debt crisis. The measures included a 50% writedown of Greek bonds, recapitalization of European banks, and an increase in the bailout fund to €1 trillion.
events.name: EU Agreement on Sovereign Debt Crisis

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2011, the effects of a large snowstorm that struck the northeastern United States were still being felt, with widespread power outages and travel disruptions. This storm was notable for its early timing in the winter season.
events.name: Northeastern US Snowstorm

events.enhanced_description: On October 31, 2011, the United Nations designated this date as the symbolic point at which the global population reached seven billion. This milestone highlighted significant demographic changes and challenges facing the world.
events.name: UN Global Population Milestone

events.enhanced_description: On November 9, 2011, the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) conducted the first nationwide test of the Emergency Alert System in the United States. This test aimed to assess the effectiveness of the system in disseminating emergency information to the public.
events.name: Emergency Alert System Test

events.enhanced_description: On November 26, 2011, NASA launched the Mars Science Laboratory rover Curiosity from the Kennedy Space Center in Florida. This mission aimed to explore the Martian surface and assess its habitability, marking a significant advancement in space exploration.
events.name: Launch of Mars Curiosity Rover

events.enhanced_description: On November 30, 2011, the United Kingdom severed diplomatic relations with Iran and expelled Iranian diplomats following an attack on the British embassy in Tehran. This incident marked a significant deterioration in UK-Iran relations.
events.name: UK-Iran Diplomatic Relations Severed

events.enhanced_description: On December 6, 2011, suicide bombings targeted Shia Muslim worshippers in Kabul and Mazar-i-Sharif during Ashura, resulting in significant casualties. These attacks were part of ongoing sectarian violence in Afghanistan.
events.name: 2011 Afghanistan Ashura bombings

events.enhanced_description: On December 15, 2011, the United States formally declared an end to the Iraq War, concluding nearly nine years of military engagement. This announcement marked a pivotal moment in U.S. foreign policy and the ongoing challenges in Iraq.
events.name: End of the Iraq War

events.enhanced_description: On December 16, 2011, Tropical Storm Washi caused devastating flash floods in the Philippines, resulting in 1,268 fatalities and leaving 85 people officially listed as missing. The storm highlighted the vulnerability of the region to extreme weather events.
events.name: Tropical Storm Washi

events.enhanced_description: On December 17, 2011, North Korean leader Kim Jong-il died from a heart attack or stroke while traveling to a field guidance. His death marked a significant transition in North Korean leadership and raised concerns about the future direction of the country.
events.name: Death of Kim Jong-il

events.enhanced_description: On December 19, 2011, Liechtenstein became the 26th member state of the Schengen Area, allowing for passport-free travel across many European countries. This accession was a significant step in enhancing regional cooperation and mobility.
events.name: Liechtenstein Joins Schengen Area

events.enhanced_description: On December 29, 2011, Samoa and Tokelau moved from east to west of the International Date Line, effectively skipping December 30. This change was made to better align their time zones with major trading partners, reflecting the dynamic nature of global commerce.
events.name: Samoa and Tokelau Change Time Zones

events.enhanced_description: Boudougate refers to a political scandal in Argentina involving Vice President Amado Boudou and the printing house Ciccone Calcografica, which surfaced in 2012. The scandal raised questions about corruption and political accountability in the Argentine government.
events.name: Boudougate

events.enhanced_description: In 2012, the tragic case of a woman in Ireland who died after being denied an abortion sparked widespread outrage and debate over the country's restrictive abortion laws. This incident became a pivotal moment in the movement for reproductive rights in Ireland.
events.name: Ireland: a woman dies after being prevented from having an abortion

events.enhanced_description: In 2012, President Cristina Fernández de Kirchner's government passed a law to renationalize YPF, Argentina's largest oil company, which had been privatized in the 1990s. This move aimed to regain control over the country's natural resources and was met with both support and opposition.
events.name: Renationalization of YPF

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2012, a magnitude 6.7 earthquake strikes Negros Island in the Philippines, resulting in the deaths of 112 people. The earthquake causes significant damage to infrastructure and highlights the region's vulnerability to seismic activity.
events.name: Earthquake in Negros, Philippines

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2012, Vladimir Putin is elected President of Russia, marking his return to the presidency after serving as Prime Minister. His election is met with widespread protests and allegations of electoral fraud, reflecting the growing discontent among the Russian populace.
events.name: Vladimir Putin elected President of Russia

events.enhanced_description: In 2012, Pakistan emerges victorious in the Asia Cup cricket tournament, showcasing its cricketing prowess in the region. This win is celebrated by fans and highlights the competitive nature of cricket in South Asia.
events.name: Pakistan wins the 2012 Asia Cup

events.enhanced_description: In 2012, CERN announced the discovery of a new particle consistent with the Higgs boson, a fundamental component of the Standard Model of particle physics. This discovery was a monumental achievement in understanding the universe's fundamental structure.
events.name: Discovery of the Higgs boson

events.enhanced_description: In 2012, Sport Club Corinthians Paulista won the Copa Libertadores by defeating Boca Juniors in the final. This victory marked a significant achievement for the club, securing their first title in this prestigious South American tournament.
events.name: Copa Libertadores 2012

events.enhanced_description: North Korea conducted a satellite launch, marking a significant milestone in its space exploration efforts. This event was part of the country's broader ambitions in aerospace technology.

events.enhanced_description: The Cicada 3301 internet hunt, a mysterious and complex series of puzzles, begins on January 4, 2012. It attracted the attention of cryptographers and puzzle enthusiasts worldwide, seeking to uncover the identity of the organization behind it and the purpose of the challenge.
events.name: The Cicada 3301 internet hunt begins

events.enhanced_description: On January 6, 2012, a suicide bombing occurred in Al-Maydan, a neighborhood in Damascus, Syria, resulting in numerous casualties. This attack was part of the ongoing violence during the Syrian civil war.

events.enhanced_description: On January 12, 2012, peaceful protests erupt in Târgu Mureș, Romania, as citizens express solidarity with medical professionals and demand the resignation of President Traian Băsescu. This local demonstration quickly escalates into a nationwide movement, highlighting widespread discontent with the government.
events.name: Peaceful protests begin in Târgu Mureș, Romania

events.enhanced_description: On January 13, 2012, the Costa Concordia, a passenger cruise ship, runs aground off the coast of Giglio Island, Italy, resulting in the tragic deaths of 32 individuals. The incident raises significant concerns regarding maritime safety and the conduct of the ship's captain, Francesco Schettino.
events.name: Costa Concordia disaster

events.enhanced_description: On January 17, 2012, a terrorist attack occurred in the Afar region of Ethiopia, targeting tourists at Erta Ale, a volcanic site. The attack raised concerns about security for foreign visitors in the region.
events.name: 2012 Afar region tourist attack

events.enhanced_description: On January 23, 2012, the European Union imposes an embargo on Iran in response to its ongoing uranium enrichment activities, escalating tensions between Iran and Western nations. This decision reflects the EU's commitment to addressing concerns over nuclear proliferation.
events.name: EU adopts embargo against Iran

events.enhanced_description: On February 1, 2012, a violent riot erupts at the Port Said Stadium in Egypt when local fans of Al Masry attack supporters of the Cairo-based Al Ahly SC. The chaos leads to 74 fatalities and hundreds of injuries, marking one of the deadliest incidents in football history.
events.name: Port Said Stadium riot

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2012, Queen Elizabeth II's Diamond Jubilee celebrations begin, marking 60 years of her reign over the United Kingdom. The jubilee is celebrated with various events throughout the year, culminating in a series of nationwide festivities.
events.name: Queen Elizabeth II's Diamond Jubilee

events.enhanced_description: On February 19, 2012, Iran announces the suspension of oil exports to Britain and France as a direct response to sanctions imposed by the European Union and the United States. This move reflects Iran's defiance against international pressure regarding its nuclear program.
events.name: Iran suspends oil exports to Britain and France

events.enhanced_description: On February 21, 2012, Eurozone finance ministers reach a consensus on a second bailout package for Greece, amounting to €130 billion, aimed at stabilizing the country's economy amidst a severe debt crisis. This agreement is crucial for Greece's financial recovery.
events.name: Eurozone finance ministers agree on Greek bailout

events.enhanced_description: On February 27, 2012, Yemeni President Ali Abdullah Saleh formally transfers power to Vice President Abdrabbuh Mansur Hadi after a year of mass protests against his rule. This transition marks the end of Saleh's 33-year presidency and a significant step in Yemen's political reform.
events.name: Ali Abdullah Saleh transfers power to Abdrabbuh Mansur Hadi

events.enhanced_description: On February 28, 2012, a terrorist attack took place in Yecheng, Xinjiang, China, highlighting ongoing ethnic tensions and violence in the region. The incident was part of a broader pattern of unrest involving the Uyghur population.

events.enhanced_description: On February 28, 2012, a massacre occurred in Kohistan District, Pakistan, targeting Shia Muslims in a sectarian attack. This incident highlighted the ongoing violence and discrimination faced by minority groups in the region.
events.name: February 2012 Kohistan Shia Massacre

events.enhanced_description: On March 1, 2012, Sauli Niinistö is inaugurated as the 12th President of Finland. His presidency marks a continuation of Finland's stable political landscape and commitment to social welfare.
events.name: Sauli Niinistö inaugurated as President of Finland

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2012, a series of explosions at a munitions dump in Brazzaville, the capital of the Republic of the Congo, results in at least 250 deaths. The disaster raises concerns about safety protocols regarding military munitions storage.
events.name: Explosions in Brazzaville, Republic of the Congo

events.enhanced_description: On March 5, 2012, the viral documentary film Kony 2012 is released on YouTube, aiming to raise awareness about the atrocities committed by Ugandan warlord Joseph Kony. The film quickly gains international attention and sparks a global movement.
events.name: Air date of Kony 2012

events.enhanced_description: On March 12, 2012, a tragic coach accident occurs in the Sierre Tunnel in Switzerland, resulting in the deaths of 28 people, including 22 children. The incident raises questions about road safety and the conditions of travel for school groups.
events.name: Sierre Tunnel coach crash

events.enhanced_description: On March 13, 2012, after 246 years of publication, the Encyclopædia Britannica announces it will discontinue its print edition. This decision marks a significant shift in the publishing industry, reflecting the rise of digital media.
events.name: Encyclopædia Britannica discontinues print edition

events.enhanced_description: On March 15, 2012, Bo Xilai, the Communist Party chief of Chongqing, is removed from his position amid a scandal involving the murder of British businessman Neil Heywood. This event marks a significant political shift in China and raises questions about corruption within the party.
events.name: Bo Xilai removed from post

events.enhanced_description: On May 24, 2021, a coup d'état in Mali resulted in the removal of interim president Bah Ndaw and acting prime minister Moctar Ouane, restoring military rule. This led to Mali's suspension from the Economic Community of West African States and the African Union, alongside France halting its military operations in the country.
events.name: Coup d'état in Mali

events.enhanced_description: On April 6, 2012, the National Movement for the Liberation of Azawad unilaterally declares the independence of Azawad from Mali. This declaration follows a series of conflicts and highlights the ongoing struggles for autonomy in the region.
events.name: Declaration of independence of Azawad

events.enhanced_description: On April 10, 2012, a bombing targeted a group of Bahraini policemen in Eker, resulting in casualties. This attack was part of the ongoing unrest and violence in Bahrain following the Arab Spring.
events.name: Eker bombing

events.enhanced_description: On April 11, 2012, a magnitude 8.6 earthquake strikes off the coast of Aceh, Indonesia, triggering a small tsunami. The earthquake raises fears of a larger disaster, reminiscent of the 2004 tsunami that devastated the region.

image.caption: People evacuate a Kolkata office building after mild tremors associated with the 2012 Indian Ocean earthquakes.

events.name: Earthquake strikes Indonesia

events.enhanced_description: On April 12, 2012, mutinous soldiers in Guinea-Bissau stage a coup d'état, taking control of the capital city, Bissau. They arrest interim President Raimundo Pereira and leading presidential candidate Carlos Gomes Júnior, further destabilizing the nation.
events.name: Coup d'état in Guinea-Bissau

events.enhanced_description: The Kwangmyŏngsŏng-3, an Earth observation satellite launched by North Korea, exploded shortly after its launch on April 13, 2012. This event was significant as it coincided with the centenary of Kim Il Sung's birth, and it drew international condemnation for violating United Nations Security Council resolutions.
events.name: Kwangmyŏngsŏng-3 satellite explosion

events.enhanced_description: On April 20, 2012, Bhoja Air Flight 213 crashed near Rawalpindi, Pakistan, resulting in the tragic loss of all 127 passengers and crew on board. The crash raised serious concerns about aviation safety in Pakistan.
events.name: Bhoja Air Flight 213 crash

events.enhanced_description: In April 2012, astronomers observed PS1-10jh, a supernova that provided valuable insights into stellar explosions and the universe's expansion. This discovery contributed to the field of astrophysics and our understanding of cosmic phenomena.
events.name: PS1-10jh

events.enhanced_description: The state funeral for former Malawian President Bingu Wa Mutharika took place on April 23, 2012, marking a significant moment in Malawi's political history. The event was attended by various dignitaries and highlighted the legacy of Mutharika's presidency.
events.name: State funeral of Bingu Wa Mutharika

events.enhanced_description: On April 25, 2012, former Liberian President Charles Taylor was found guilty by the Special Court for Sierra Leone on 11 counts of aiding and abetting war crimes and crimes against humanity during the Sierra Leone Civil War. This landmark ruling underscored the accountability of political leaders for war crimes.
events.name: Charles Taylor war crimes verdict

events.enhanced_description: On April 27, 2012, a series of bombings occurred in Damascus, Syria, during the ongoing civil war, resulting in numerous casualties. These attacks underscored the escalating violence and chaos in the country.
events.name: April 2012 Damascus bombings

events.enhanced_description: On April 30, 2012, a car bombing in Idlib, Syria, resulted in significant casualties amidst the civil war. This incident illustrated the ongoing violence and instability affecting the region.
events.name: April 2012 Idlib bombings

events.enhanced_description: On May 2, 2012, a pastel version of Edvard Munch's iconic painting 'The Scream' was sold at auction in New York City for a record-breaking $120 million. This sale highlighted the increasing value of modern art in the global market.
events.name: The Scream auction

events.enhanced_description: On May 3, 2012, two suicide bombers detonated explosive-filled cars in Makhachkala, Russia, resulting in numerous casualties. This attack was part of the ongoing violence in the North Caucasus region.
events.name: 2012 Makhachkala attack

events.enhanced_description: On January 25, 2015, legislative elections were held in Greece, resulting in the SYRIZA party, led by Alexis Tsipras, emerging as the largest party with 149 out of 300 seats. This election was pivotal in shaping Greece's economic policies and political landscape.
events.name: Greek legislative elections

events.enhanced_description: The 2012 World Expo took place in Yeosu, South Korea, starting on May 12, 2012. The theme of the expo was 'The Living Ocean and Coast,' showcasing innovations in marine science and sustainability.
events.name: 2012 World Expo

events.enhanced_description: On May 19, 2012, Chelsea Football Club won the 2011-12 UEFA Champions League by defeating Bayern Munich in the final held in Munich, Germany. This victory marked Chelsea's first Champions League title in the club's history.

image.caption: Chelsea players celebrate with the Champions League trophy during the club’s victory parade.
