image.date_qualification: Photograph of Chelsea’s parade on the day after the final, not the match itself.
image.rights_statement: LicenseShortName: CC BY 2.0; UsageTerms: Creative Commons Attribution 2.0; Copyrighted: True

events.name: Chelsea wins UEFA Champions League

events.enhanced_description: On May 22, 2012, the Tokyo Skytree, the tallest self-supporting tower in the world at 634 meters, was opened to the public. This architectural marvel serves as a broadcasting tower and a popular tourist destination.
events.name: Tokyo Skytree opening

events.enhanced_description: On May 26, 2012, the Eurovision Song Contest 2012 took place in Baku, Azerbaijan, where Swedish singer Loreen won with her song 'Euphoria.' This event showcased a diverse array of musical talent from across Europe.
events.name: Eurovision Song Contest 2012

events.enhanced_description: On June 3, 2012, Dana Air Flight 0992 crashed while approaching Lagos, Nigeria, due to dual-engine failure, resulting in the deaths of all 153 people on board and six individuals on the ground. This incident raised serious concerns about airline safety in Nigeria.
events.name: Dana Air Flight 0992 crash

events.enhanced_description: On June 6, 2012, Claire Holland was murdered in Bristol, England, in a case that drew significant media attention. The investigation into her death highlighted issues of violence against women in the UK.
events.name: Murder of Claire Holland

events.enhanced_description: On June 6, 2012, the first cases of the Middle East respiratory syndrome coronavirus (MERS-CoV) were identified, marking the beginning of a significant public health concern that would affect many countries in the following years.
events.name: MERS outbreak identification

events.enhanced_description: On June 7, 2012, Morley and Dianella in Perth, Western Australia, experienced a rare tornado, marking a once-in-a-decade weather event for the region. The tornado caused damage but fortunately resulted in no fatalities.
events.name: Perth tornado

events.enhanced_description: On June 8, 2012, UEFA Euro 2012 kicked off in Warsaw, Poland, with the opening match between Poland and Greece, which ended in a 1-1 draw. This tournament was co-hosted by Poland and Ukraine, showcasing top European football talent.
events.name: UEFA Euro 2012 opening match

events.enhanced_description: On June 16, 2012, a tragic stage collapse occurred at Downsview Park in Toronto just hours before a scheduled performance by the band Radiohead. The accident resulted in the death of a drum technician and injuries to several others, raising concerns about safety regulations in the concert industry.
events.name: Radiohead stage collapse

events.enhanced_description: On June 17, 2012, snap legislative elections were held in Greece following the failure to form a government after the previous elections. The New Democracy party, led by Antonis Samaras, won 129 out of 300 seats, allowing them to form a government.
events.name: Greek snap elections

events.enhanced_description: On June 18, 2012, the Shenzhou 9 spacecraft, carrying three Chinese astronauts including Liu Yang, the first Chinese woman in space, successfully docked with the Tiangong-1 space laboratory. This achievement marked a significant milestone in China's space exploration efforts.
events.name: Shenzhou 9 docking

events.enhanced_description: On June 21, 2012, the Congress of Paraguay approved the impeachment of President Fernando Lugo, citing his handling of a land conflict that resulted in violence. The following day, Lugo was removed from power, and Vice President Federico Franco assumed the presidency.
events.name: Fernando Lugo impeachment

events.enhanced_description: On June 24, 2012, Lonesome George, the last known individual of the Pinta Island tortoise subspecies, died in Galápagos National Park, marking the extinction of the subspecies. His death highlighted the ongoing issues of biodiversity loss and conservation efforts.
events.name: Lonesome George's death

events.enhanced_description: On June 30, 2012, Mohamed Morsi, a member of the Muslim Brotherhood, was elected as the 5th President of Egypt, becoming the first president elected democratically by the Egyptian people. His election sparked mixed reactions and protests across the country.
events.name: Mohamed Morsi's election

events.enhanced_description: On July 1, 2012, the final match of UEFA Euro 2012 took place in Kyiv, Ukraine, where Spain faced Italy. Spain won decisively with a score of 4-0, achieving their third consecutive international tournament victory.
events.name: UEFA Euro 2012 final

events.enhanced_description: On July 4, 2012, CERN announced the discovery of a new particle consistent with the Higgs boson after experiments conducted at the Large Hadron Collider. This discovery was a significant milestone in particle physics, confirming theories about the fundamental building blocks of the universe.
events.name: Higgs boson announcement

events.enhanced_description: On July 20, 2012, a mass shooting occurred at a movie theater in Aurora, Colorado, during a screening of 'The Dark Knight Rises,' resulting in 12 fatalities and 58 injuries. The shooter, James Holmes, was later apprehended and faced multiple charges.
events.name: Aurora, Colorado shooting

events.enhanced_description: On July 21, 2012, Turkish adventurer Erden Eruç became the first person in history to complete a solo human-powered circumnavigation of the Earth. His journey involved rowing, cycling, and trekking, showcasing extraordinary endurance and determination.
events.name: Erden Eruç's circumnavigation

events.enhanced_description: On July 23, 2012, a massive coronal mass ejection from the Sun narrowly missed Earth by just nine days. Had it struck, it was estimated to potentially cause damages up to $2.6 trillion to electrical infrastructure worldwide.
events.name: The Solar storm of 2012

events.enhanced_description: The 2012 Summer Olympics, held in London, England, showcased athletes from around the world competing in various sports. This event marked a significant moment in sports history, celebrating athletic excellence and international unity.
events.name: 2012 Summer Olympics

events.enhanced_description: On July 30, 2012, India experienced the worst power outage in world history, leaving approximately 620 million people without electricity. This incident highlighted significant issues within the country's power infrastructure and management.
events.name: 2012 India blackouts

events.enhanced_description: On August 1, 2012, Microsoft announced the completion of Windows 8, a significant update to its operating system that introduced a new user interface and features aimed at touch-screen devices. This release marked a pivotal moment in the evolution of personal computing.
events.name: Development of Windows 8

events.enhanced_description: On August 6, 2012, NASA's Curiosity rover successfully landed on Mars as part of the Mars Science Laboratory mission. This event marked a significant milestone in space exploration, allowing scientists to study the Martian surface and search for signs of past life.
events.name: Curiosity rover landing

events.enhanced_description: On August 10, 2012, a massacre occurred at Forward Operating Base Delhi in Garmsir, Afghanistan, where Taliban militants attacked Afghan security forces. The incident highlighted the ongoing conflict and challenges faced by Afghan forces in securing the region.
events.name: Forward Operating Base Delhi Massacre

events.enhanced_description: The Azad Maidan riots erupted on August 11, 2012, in Mumbai, India, during a protest against communal violence in Myanmar. The demonstration turned violent, leading to clashes between protesters and police, resulting in multiple injuries and arrests.
events.name: Azad Maidan riots

events.enhanced_description: On August 16-17, 2012, an attack occurred at Zion Square in Jerusalem where a group of Israeli youths assaulted four Palestinian teenagers. This incident raised tensions in the city and highlighted ongoing ethnic and political conflicts.
events.name: Zion Square assault

events.enhanced_description: On August 24, 2012, the House of Representatives of Japan passed a resolution condemning South Korean President Lee Myung-bak's visit to the disputed Liancourt Rocks. This event escalated tensions between Japan and South Korea over territorial disputes.
events.name: Japan's resolution on Liancourt Rocks

events.enhanced_description: On August 25, 2012, Voyager 1 became the first human-made object to exit the Solar System and enter interstellar space. This milestone in space exploration marked a new chapter in humanity's quest to understand the cosmos.
events.name: Voyager 1 enters interstellar space

events.enhanced_description: On August 31, 2012, Armenia severed diplomatic relations with Hungary following the extradition of Ramil Safarov to Azerbaijan, who had been convicted of killing an Armenian soldier. This decision was met with widespread criticism and highlighted ongoing tensions in the region.
events.name: Armenia-Hungary diplomatic relations severed

events.enhanced_description: On September 4, 2012, Windows 7 surpassed Windows XP in global market share, marking a significant shift in operating system usage among consumers and businesses. This change reflected the growing acceptance of newer technology.
events.name: Windows 7 overtakes Windows XP

events.enhanced_description: On September 7, 2012, Canada officially severed diplomatic ties with Iran by closing its embassy in Tehran and expelling Iranian diplomats from Ottawa. This decision was driven by concerns over Iran's support for Syria and its nuclear program.
events.name: Canada cuts ties with Iran

events.enhanced_description: On September 11, 2012, a series of coordinated terrorist attacks targeted United States diplomatic missions worldwide, notably resulting in the death of US Ambassador J. Christopher Stevens in Benghazi, Libya. These attacks sparked widespread debate over their motivations and implications.
events.name: Terrorist attacks on diplomatic missions

events.enhanced_description: On September 22, 2012, the United Kingdom reported a novel coronavirus case to the World Health Organization, marking the beginning of increased global awareness and monitoring of emerging infectious diseases.
events.name: Novel coronavirus case reported

events.enhanced_description: On October 1, 2012, Boko Haram militants carried out a horrific attack on Federal Polytechnic in Mubi, Nigeria, resulting in the deaths of dozens of students. This attack exemplified the severe threat posed by Boko Haram to educational institutions in the region.
events.name: Federal Polytechnic, Mubi attack

events.enhanced_description: On October 14, 2012, Austrian skydiver Felix Baumgartner made history by becoming the first person to break the sound barrier without machine assistance during a record-breaking space dive from a height of 128,000 feet over Roswell, New Mexico.
events.name: Felix Baumgartner's space dive

events.enhanced_description: On October 16, 2012, seven paintings valued at $25 million were stolen from the Kunsthal museum in Rotterdam, Netherlands. This high-profile art heist raised questions about security measures in cultural institutions.
events.name: Kunsthal art heist

events.enhanced_description: On October 22, 2012, Hurricane Sandy, the largest Atlantic hurricane on record, struck the United States East Coast, causing widespread devastation, resulting in 233 deaths and approximately $68.7 billion in damages.
events.name: Hurricane Sandy

events.enhanced_description: On October 26, 2012, Microsoft released Windows 8 to the general public, introducing a new interface designed for touch devices and aiming to unify the user experience across PCs and tablets.
events.name: Release of Windows 8

events.enhanced_description: On October 28, 2012, Jorge Lorenzo was crowned the World Champion of the 2012 Grand Prix motorcycle racing season, solidifying his status as one of the top competitors in the sport.
events.name: Jorge Lorenzo World Champion

events.enhanced_description: On November 1, 2012, a catastrophic truck crash occurred in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, resulting in an explosion that caused significant damage and loss of life. The incident raised concerns about road safety regulations and emergency response in urban areas.
events.name: 2012 Riyadh truck crash

events.enhanced_description: On November 6, 2012, Barack Obama was reelected as President of the United States, defeating Republican challenger Mitt Romney in a closely watched election that highlighted key issues such as healthcare and the economy.
events.name: 2012 United States presidential election

events.enhanced_description: On November 14, 2012, Israel launched Operation Pillar of Defense against the Gaza Strip, resulting in the death of Hamas military chief Ahmed Jabari. The operation escalated violence in the region, leading to a ceasefire brokered by Egyptian and US officials.
events.name: Operation Pillar of Defense

events.enhanced_description: On December 9, 2012, Typhoon Bopha, known as 'Pablo' in the Philippines, struck Mindanao, resulting in at least 1,067 fatalities and leaving around 838 people missing. The storm caused widespread devastation and highlighted the region's vulnerability to natural disasters.

events.enhanced_description: On November 29, 2012, the UN General Assembly approved a motion granting Palestine non-member observer state status. This decision was a significant step in the Palestinian quest for statehood and recognition on the international stage.
events.name: UN General Assembly grants Palestine observer status

events.enhanced_description: On December 6, 2012, the state of Washington became the first jurisdiction in the modern world to officially legalize the possession of cannabis for personal use. This landmark decision marked a significant shift in drug policy and regulation.
events.name: Washington legalizes cannabis

events.enhanced_description: During the UN Climate Change Conference held in Doha, Qatar, parties agreed to extend the Kyoto Protocol until 2020, aiming to combat climate change through international cooperation. This conference was crucial in shaping future climate policies and commitments.
events.name: UN Climate Change Conference 2012

events.enhanced_description: The Séléka coalition launched a successful offensive against the Central African Republic government, leading to the overthrow of President François Bozizé. This event marked the beginning of a civil war that would have devastating effects on the nation.
events.name: Séléka Overthrows Central African Republic Government

events.enhanced_description: On February 7, 2016, North Korea launched the Kwangmyŏngsŏng-4 reconnaissance satellite into orbit, which was widely condemned by the international community as a cover for long-range ballistic missile testing. This event heightened tensions in the region and drew global criticism.
events.name: North Korea Satellite Launch

events.enhanced_description: The date 12/12/12 marked the last time in the 21st century that the month, day, and final two digits of the year were the same. This unique occurrence sparked interest and celebrations among numerology enthusiasts.
events.name: Last Repeating Date of the Century (12/12/12)

events.enhanced_description: The Sandy Hook Elementary School shooting resulted in the tragic deaths of twenty-six people, including twenty children, and the gunman, Adam Lanza. This incident sparked national debates on gun control and school safety in the United States.
events.name: Sandy Hook Elementary School Shooting

events.enhanced_description: On December 15, 2012, Tehrik-i-Taliban militants launched a coordinated attack on Bacha Khan International Airport in Peshawar, Pakistan, resulting in a fierce gun battle with security forces. This attack underscored the ongoing security challenges faced by Pakistan in combating terrorism.
events.name: 2012 Pakistan airport attack

events.enhanced_description: The 2012 FIFA Club World Cup took place in Yokohama, Japan, where Sport Club Corinthians Paulista emerged victorious, defeating Chelsea FC in the final. This marked Corinthians' first title in the Club World Cup, solidifying their status in international football.
events.name: 2012 FIFA Club World Cup

events.enhanced_description: Grupo Santander announced the acquisition of the remaining 10% of Banesto, effectively absorbing it into Banco Santander. This strategic move was part of Santander's efforts to consolidate its position in the banking sector.
events.name: Grupo Santander Acquires Banesto

events.enhanced_description: An overcrowded boat capsized off the coast of Somalia, resulting in the tragic drowning of at least 55 people. This incident highlighted the ongoing humanitarian crisis and the dangers faced by migrants in the region.
events.name: Somalia Boat Capsizing

events.enhanced_description: The end of the 13th b'ak'tun in the Mayan calendar was marked by festivities in countries that were part of the Maya civilization, including Mexico and Guatemala. Major celebrations took place at Chichén Itzá and Tikal, reflecting the cultural significance of this event.
events.name: 2012 Phenomenon: End of 13th b'ak'tun

events.enhanced_description: On December 31, 2012, authorities in Canada foiled a plot to carry out terrorist attacks on VIA Rail trains, allegedly orchestrated by individuals with ties to al-Qaeda. The incident raised alarms about domestic security and the threat of terrorism in Canada.
events.name: 2013 VIA Rail Canada terrorism plot

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2013, an attempt was made to use ricin, a highly toxic substance, as a weapon in Washington, D.C. The incident highlighted concerns about bioterrorism and the potential for chemical attacks in urban areas.
events.name: 2013 ricin attacks

events.enhanced_description: In January 2013, a judge ordered the Los Angeles Diocese to release documents related to the sexual abuse scandal within the Catholic Church. This ruling was a significant moment in the ongoing efforts to address and acknowledge the church's handling of abuse cases.
events.name: Judge orders L.A. Diocese to release sexual abuse documents (January 2013)

events.enhanced_description: In 2013, the conferimento O.M.R.I. ceremony took place in the Sala Di Liegro at Palazzo Valentini in Rome, honoring Paolo Salvati for his contributions. This event reflects the cultural recognition of individuals who have made significant impacts in their fields.
events.name: Palazzo Valentini, sala Di Liegro, 2013, Roma

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2013, researchers from Oregon Health & Science University published a study in the journal Nature describing the first successful production of human embryonic stem cells through cloning. This groundbreaking research has significant implications for regenerative medicine and therapeutic applications.
events.name: Human embryonic stem cells by cloning (duplicate)

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2013, the World Health Organization officially named the novel coronavirus causing severe respiratory illness as Middle East Respiratory Syndrome (MERS). This naming was crucial for public health communication and research efforts.
events.name: MERS naming

events.enhanced_description: In 2013, the Supreme Court of the United States decided United States v. Windsor, which struck down a key provision of the Defense of Marriage Act, thereby granting federal recognition to same-sex marriages. This landmark ruling was a significant victory for LGBTQ+ rights.
events.name: United States v. Windsor

events.enhanced_description: In early 2013, a significant tornado outbreak occurred in Illinois, with an EF4 tornado striking Washington, causing extensive damage estimated at $935 million and resulting in three fatalities. This event underscored the vulnerability of communities to severe weather and the importance of disaster preparedness.
events.name: Tornado outbreak in Illinois

events.enhanced_description: In 2013, the Moldovan-flagged cargo ship MV Rhosus made port in Beirut, Lebanon, carrying 2,750 tonnes of ammonium nitrate. The ship was deemed unseaworthy and its cargo was left in the port, leading to a catastrophic explosion in 2020 that devastated the city.
events.name: MV Rhosus arrives in Beirut

events.enhanced_description: On January 4, 2013, a mass shooting occurred in Kawit, Philippines, resulting in multiple casualties. The incident raised concerns about gun violence and public safety in the region.
events.name: Kawit shooting

events.enhanced_description: A powerful Mw 7.5 earthquake struck near Craig, Alaska, shaking the Prince of Wales Island region. The earthquake was classified as moderate and raised concerns about seismic activity in the area.
events.name: 2013 Craig, Alaska Earthquake

events.enhanced_description: In a series of bomb blasts across Pakistan, at least 130 people were killed and over 270 injured. This tragic event underscored the ongoing violence and instability in the region.
events.name: Bomb Blasts in Pakistan

events.enhanced_description: The French military initiated a five-month intervention in Mali, targeting the militant Islamist group Ansar Dine. This operation aimed to restore stability in the region amidst rising extremism.
events.name: French Military Intervention in Mali

events.enhanced_description: A hostage crisis at a natural gas facility near In Aménas, Algeria, resulted in the deaths of thirty-nine international workers and one security guard. This incident highlighted the ongoing threats posed by terrorism in the region.
events.name: In Aménas Hostage Crisis

events.enhanced_description: Barack Obama was sworn in for a second term as President of the United States, marking a significant moment in American political history. His inauguration was attended by thousands and was a celebration of his re-election.
events.name: Barack Obama's Second Inauguration

events.enhanced_description: A devastating fire at a nightclub in Santa Maria, Brazil, resulted in the deaths of an estimated 245 people. This tragedy raised serious concerns about safety regulations and emergency preparedness in public venues.

locations.name: Santa Maria, Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil

events.name: Santa Maria Nightclub Fire

events.enhanced_description: The Emergency Alert Systems of five television stations across various U.S. states were hijacked, airing a false 'Zombie apocalypse' hoax. This incident is noted as one of the largest cybersecurity breaches in EAS history.

locations.name: Montana, Michigan, Wisconsin, New Mexico, United States

events.name: EAS Zombie Apocalypse Hoax

events.enhanced_description: North Korea conducted its third underground nuclear test, which drew widespread condemnation from the international community and led to tightened economic sanctions. This test heightened tensions in the region and raised concerns about nuclear proliferation.
events.name: North Korea's Third Nuclear Test

events.enhanced_description: A meteor exploded over the Russian city of Chelyabinsk, injuring nearly 1,500 people and damaging thousands of buildings. This event was the most powerful meteor strike in over a century, prompting discussions on planetary defense.
events.name: Chelyabinsk Meteor Explosion

events.enhanced_description: American scientists successfully used a 3D printer to create a living lab-grown ear from collagen and animal ear cell cultures. This breakthrough holds promise for future medical applications, particularly in transplant surgery.
events.name: 3D Printed Lab-Grown Ear

events.enhanced_description: Park Geun-hye made history by becoming the first woman to be elected as president of South Korea. Her presidency marked a significant milestone in the country's political landscape and gender representation.
events.name: Park Geun-hye Becomes President of South Korea

events.enhanced_description: Pope Benedict XVI resigned from the papacy, becoming the first pope to do so voluntarily since Celestine V in 1294. His resignation marked a historic moment in the Catholic Church, prompting discussions about the future of the papacy.
events.name: Benedict XVI Resignation

events.enhanced_description: Cardinal Jorge Mario Bergoglio of Argentina was elected as the 266th pope, taking the name Francis. He became the first Jesuit pope and the first pope from the Americas, marking a significant shift in the Catholic Church's leadership.
events.name: Election of Pope Francis

events.enhanced_description: After rebel forces captured the capital, Bangui, Central African Republic President François Bozizé fled to the Democratic Republic of the Congo. This marked a significant turning point in the Central African Republic's ongoing conflict.

image.caption: Map of Central African Republic Bush War movements during the coup that deposed President François Bozizé.

locations.name: Kinshasa, Democratic Republic of the Congo

events.name: François Bozizé Flees to DRC

events.enhanced_description: The European Union agreed to a €10 billion economic bailout for Cyprus, aimed at stabilizing the country's economy amidst a banking crisis. This bailout was a significant event in the context of the Eurozone financial challenges.
events.name: EU Economic Bailout for Cyprus

events.enhanced_description: On March 29, 2013, a landslide at the Gyama Mine in Tibet resulted in the deaths of several miners and highlighted the dangers associated with mining operations in the region. Rescue efforts were complicated by the remote location and challenging terrain.
events.name: 2013 Gyama Mine landslide

events.enhanced_description: On April 2, 2013, the United Nations General Assembly adopted the Arms Trade Treaty, aimed at regulating the international trade of conventional weapons and preventing their diversion to the illicit market. This landmark treaty was a significant step towards promoting peace and security globally.

image.caption: Map showing the status of signatures and ratifications of the Arms Trade Treaty.

events.name: The United Nations General Assembly adopts the Arms Trade Treaty

events.enhanced_description: On April 9, 2013, Uhuru Kenyatta was inaugurated as the fourth president of Kenya at the Moi International Sports Centre. His presidency marked a significant moment in Kenyan politics, following a contentious election process.

locations.name: Moi International Sports Centre, Nairobi, Kenya

events.name: inauguration of Uhuru Kenyatta

events.enhanced_description: On April 13, 2013, Nicolás Maduro was declared the winner of the Venezuelan presidential election, narrowly defeating his opponent Henrique Capriles Radonski. The election followed the death of Hugo Chávez and was marked by controversy and protests that continued for months.
events.name: Venezuelan presidential election

events.enhanced_description: On April 15, 2013, two bombs were detonated by Chechen-born brothers Tamerlan and Dzhokhar Tsarnaev at the Boston Marathon, resulting in the deaths of three individuals and injuring 264 others. This tragic event sparked a massive manhunt and raised significant concerns about domestic terrorism.
events.name: Boston Marathon bombing

events.enhanced_description: On April 21, 2013, businessman Horacio Cartes won the Paraguayan general election, defeating Efraín Alegre. This election marked a significant political shift in Paraguay following the impeachment of former President Fernando Lugo.
events.name: 2013 Paraguayan general election

events.enhanced_description: On April 24, 2013, the collapse of the Rana Plaza building in Savar, Bangladesh, resulted in the deaths of 1,134 people, making it one of the deadliest industrial disasters in history. The tragedy highlighted severe safety issues in the garment industry and led to international calls for reform.
events.name: 2013 Savar building collapse

events.enhanced_description: On April 30, 2013, Willem-Alexander was inaugurated as King of the Netherlands following the abdication of his mother, Queen Beatrix. This event marked the first time in over a century that a male monarch took the throne in the Netherlands.
events.name: Willem-Alexander inaugurated as King of the Netherlands

events.enhanced_description: On May 14, 2013, the Eurovision Song Contest took place in Malmö, Sweden, where Danish singer Emmelie de Forest won with her song 'Only Teardrops.' This annual event showcases musical talent from across Europe and has a significant cultural impact.
events.name: Eurovision Song Contest 2013

events.enhanced_description: On May 15, 2013, researchers from Oregon Health & Science University published a study in the journal Nature describing the first successful production of human embryonic stem cells through cloning. This groundbreaking research has significant implications for regenerative medicine and therapeutic applications.
events.name: Human embryonic stem cells by cloning

events.enhanced_description: On May 22, 2013, off-duty British Army soldier Fusilier Lee Rigby was murdered in Woolwich, London, by Islamic terrorists Michael Adebolajo and Michael Adebowale. This shocking attack raised concerns about extremism and security in the UK.
events.name: Lee Rigby murder

events.enhanced_description: On May 25, 2013, a French soldier was stabbed in La Défense, a major business district near Paris, in an attack that raised concerns about security and the threat of terrorism in France. The incident was part of a broader pattern of violence targeting military personnel.
events.name: 2013 La Défense attack

events.name: Edward Snowden disclosures

events.enhanced_description: On June 7, 2013, the brutal gang rape and murder of a young woman in Kamduni, West Bengal, sparked widespread protests and discussions about women's safety and rights in India. The case became emblematic of the larger issues of gender-based violence in the country.
events.name: 2013 Kamduni gang rape and murder case

events.enhanced_description: On June 12, 2013, Jiroemon Kimura, recognized as the oldest verified man in history, passed away at the age of 116 years and 54 days. His longevity drew attention to the factors contributing to a long and healthy life.

events.enhanced_description: On June 22, 2013, a spree shooting occurred in Shanghai, resulting in multiple casualties and raising alarms about public safety and gun violence in urban China. The incident prompted discussions about gun control and security measures.

events.enhanced_description: On June 23, 2013, a tragic bus accident occurred in the Morača canyon in Montenegro, resulting in the deaths of 19 Romanian tourists and injuring 27 others. This incident raised concerns about road safety in the region.
events.name: Montenegro bus crash

events.enhanced_description: On June 25, 2013, Emir Hamad bin Khalifa Al Thani abdicated the throne of Qatar, passing power to his son, Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani. This transition marked a significant moment in Qatari history and governance.
events.name: Abdication of Hamad bin Khalifa Al Thani

events.enhanced_description: On June 26, 2013, Kevin Rudd won the Australian Labor Party leadership ballot, reclaiming the position of Prime Minister of Australia three years after being replaced by Julia Gillard. This political shift was significant in the context of Australian politics.

events.enhanced_description: On June 30, 2013, a series of bombings in Quetta, Pakistan, resulted in numerous casualties and highlighted the ongoing violence and instability in the region. These attacks were part of a broader trend of terrorism affecting Pakistan.
events.name: June 2013 Pakistan bombings

events.enhanced_description: On July 1, 2013, Croatia officially became the 28th member of the European Union, marking a significant milestone in the country's post-war recovery and integration into European structures.

events.enhanced_description: On July 3, 2013, Egyptian President Mohamed Morsi was deposed in a military coup d'état amid widespread protests against his rule. This event led to significant political turmoil and violence in Egypt.

events.enhanced_description: On July 6, 2013, a runaway train carrying crude oil derailed in Lac-Mégantic, Quebec, leading to a catastrophic explosion that killed 47 people and destroyed much of the town's center. events.name: Lac-Mégantic train derailment

events.enhanced_description: Asiana Airlines Flight 214 crashed while landing at San Francisco International Airport on July 6, 2013, resulting in the deaths of three passengers and injuries to many others. events.enhanced_description: On July 21, 2013, Philippe was sworn in as King of the Belgians following the abdication of his father, Albert II. This event marked a new chapter in the Belgian monarchy and was celebrated with national festivities.

events.enhanced_description: The XIV World Youth Day took place in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, attracting millions of young Catholics from around the world to celebrate their faith and engage in discussions on various social issues. events.enhanced_description: On July 26, 2013, a bombing attack in Parachinar, Pakistan, targeted a crowded market, resulting in numerous casualties. This attack was part of the ongoing sectarian violence in the region and underscored the challenges of security in Pakistan.

events.enhanced_description: On August 4, 2013, a terrorist attack occurred at the Ekayana Monastery in Jakarta, Indonesia, resulting in casualties and highlighting the ongoing threat of religiously motivated violence in the region. The incident raised concerns about security for religious minorities.

events.enhanced_description: TU Me, an instant messaging and Voice over IP application, was discontinued on August 8, 2013. The app was developed to provide users with a platform for free communication but ultimately could not compete with other established messaging services.

events.enhanced_description: Geometry Dash, a popular platform game developed by Swedish developer RobTop, was released on August 13, 2013. The game quickly gained a large following due to its challenging levels and engaging gameplay mechanics.

events.enhanced_description: On August 14, 2013, eleven security personnel were killed in Kerdasa, Giza, Egypt, during clashes with militants. This massacre highlighted the ongoing violence and instability in Egypt following the Arab Spring.
events.name: Kerdasa massacre

events.enhanced_description: On August 14, 2013, Egyptian security forces raided two camps of anti-coup protesters in Cairo, resulting in the deaths of at least 2,696 people. This event was described by Human Rights Watch as one of the largest killings of demonstrators in recent history, marking a significant moment in the ongoing political turmoil in Egypt.
events.name: Egyptian anti-coup protests raid

events.enhanced_description: Horacio Cartes was sworn in as the President of Paraguay on August 15, 2013, following a successful election campaign. His presidency focused on economic reforms and improving the country's infrastructure.

events.enhanced_description: Kuben Upper Secondary School, the most expensive public school in Norway, opened its doors on August 19, 2013. The school was designed to provide modern educational facilities and promote innovative teaching methods.

events.enhanced_description: On August 21, 2013, a mass shooting occurred in Meet al-Attar, Egypt, resulting in multiple casualties. The incident raised concerns about public safety and the ongoing violence in the region.
events.name: Meet al-Attar shooting

events.enhanced_description: On August 21, 2013, a chemical attack in Ghouta, Syria, resulted in the deaths of approximately 1,429 people during the ongoing Syrian Civil War. The attack drew international condemnation and raised questions about the use of chemical weapons in conflict.
events.name: Ghouta chemical attack

events.enhanced_description: On August 29, 2013, the United Kingdom Parliament voted against military intervention in Syria, following the Ghouta chemical attack. This decision reflected deep divisions within British politics regarding foreign military engagement.

events.enhanced_description: On September 4, 2013, a stabbing attack occurred at Spring High School in Texas, resulting in injuries and prompting discussions about school safety and violence in educational institutions. The incident highlighted the need for improved security measures.

events.enhanced_description: The 2013 Australian federal election took place on September 7, 2013, resulting in a victory for the Liberal/National Coalition led by Tony Abbott, who defeated the incumbent Labor Government led by Prime Minister Kevin Rudd. Abbott's win marked a significant shift in Australian politics.
events.name: 2013 Australian federal election

events.enhanced_description: The 2013 Colorado floods began on September 8, 2013, resulting from heavy rainfall in the Colorado River Basin. The floods caused widespread damage, displacing thousands and leading to significant loss of life and property.
events.name: 2013 Colorado floods

events.enhanced_description: On September 13, 2013, the U.S. consulate in Herat was attacked by Taliban militants, resulting in casualties and highlighting the ongoing instability in Afghanistan. This incident underscored the persistent threat posed by insurgent groups in the region.
events.name: 2013 attack on U.S. consulate in Herat

events.enhanced_description: Grand Theft Auto V was released on September 17, 2013, and quickly became a cultural phenomenon, earning over half a billion dollars on its first day. The game was praised for its expansive open world and engaging narrative.
events.name: Grand Theft Auto V release

events.enhanced_description: On September 21, 2013, al-Shabaab militants attacked the Westgate shopping mall in Nairobi, Kenya, resulting in at least 62 civilian deaths and over 170 injuries. The attack was part of a broader campaign by the group against perceived Western influences in the region.
events.name: Westgate shopping mall attack

events.enhanced_description: In October 2013, a series of bombings occurred in Myanmar, raising concerns about the country's security situation amidst ongoing ethnic tensions and political unrest. These attacks highlighted the fragility of peace in a nation transitioning from military rule.
events.name: October 2013 Myanmar bombings

events.enhanced_description: On October 10, 2013, delegates from approximately 140 countries and territories signed the Minamata Treaty, a United Nations Environment Programme treaty aimed at protecting human health and the environment from mercury emissions. The treaty represents a significant global commitment to environmental protection.
events.name: Minamata Treaty signing

events.enhanced_description: On October 12, 2013, an apartment building collapsed in Medellín, Colombia, killing twelve people. The incident raised concerns about building safety standards and regulations in the country.

events.enhanced_description: Lao Airlines Flight 301 crashed on approach to Pakse Airport in Laos on October 16, 2013, killing all 49 people on board. The crash was attributed to adverse weather conditions and pilot error.

events.enhanced_description: Microsoft released Windows 8.1 on October 17, 2013, as an update to its Windows 8 operating system. The update aimed to address user feedback and improve the overall user experience.
events.name: Release of Windows 8.1

events.enhanced_description: On October 18, 2013, Saudi Arabia made history by rejecting a seat on the United Nations Security Council, citing dissatisfaction with the UN's handling of regional issues, particularly in Syria and Palestine. This unprecedented decision drew international attention and debate.
events.name: Saudi Arabia rejects UN Security Council seat

events.enhanced_description: On November 1, 2013, a shooting incident at a Golden Dawn office in Irakleio resulted in the murder of two party members, reflecting the violent political climate in Greece at the time. events.enhanced_description: Typhoon Haiyan, one of the strongest tropical cyclones on record, struck the Philippines and Vietnam on November 8, 2013, causing widespread devastation and resulting in at least 6,241 deaths. The storm highlighted the vulnerability of coastal communities to extreme weather events.
events.name: Typhoon Haiyan impact

events.enhanced_description: On November 12, 2013, Francis Bacon's 'Three Studies of Lucian Freud' sold for a record-breaking $142.4 million at a New York City auction, making it the most expensive artwork ever sold at auction. The piece is a triptych of portraits of Bacon's friend and fellow artist, Lucian Freud.

events.enhanced_description: The Paris attacks on November 15 and 18, 2013, involved a series of coordinated terrorist assaults across the city, resulting in significant casualties and widespread fear. These attacks prompted international discussions on security and counter-terrorism measures.

events.enhanced_description: On November 17, 2013, Tatarstan Airlines Flight 363 tragically crashed while attempting to land at Kazan International Airport, resulting in the loss of all 50 people on board. The incident raised significant concerns regarding aviation safety and led to investigations into the airline's operational practices.
events.name: Tatarstan Airlines Flight 363 crash

events.enhanced_description: The Euromaidan protests erupted on November 21, 2013, in Kyiv, Ukraine, following President Viktor Yanukovych's decision to suspend an association agreement with the European Union in favor of closer ties with Russia. This movement, which called for European integration and government accountability, marked a significant turning point in Ukraine's political landscape.
events.name: Euromaidan Protests Begin

events.enhanced_description: On November 24, 2013, Iran reached a landmark agreement with six world powers to limit its nuclear development program in exchange for relief from economic sanctions. This agreement was seen as a significant step towards resolving longstanding tensions over Iran's nuclear ambitions.
events.name: Iran Nuclear Agreement

events.enhanced_description: On November 29, 2013, a police helicopter tragically crashed into The Clutha pub in Glasgow, Scotland, resulting in the deaths of 10 individuals and injuring 31 others. The incident raised serious questions about air safety regulations and emergency response protocols.
events.name: Clutha helicopter crash

events.enhanced_description: On December 3, 2013, Australia officially transitioned from analog to digital television, marking a significant milestone in broadcasting technology. This change aimed to improve picture and sound quality while freeing up spectrum for other uses.
events.name: End of Analog Television in Australia

events.enhanced_description: On December 7, 2013, delegates at the Ninth Ministerial Conference of the World Trade Organization signed the Bali Package agreement, aimed at reducing global trade barriers. This agreement was a significant step towards enhancing international trade cooperation.
events.name: Bali Package Agreement

events.enhanced_description: On December 14, 2013, China's Chang'e 3 spacecraft successfully soft-landed on the Moon, carrying the Yutu rover. This historic achievement marked the first soft landing on the Moon since 1976 and demonstrated China's growing capabilities in space exploration.
events.name: Chang'e 3 Moon Landing

events.enhanced_description: On December 15, 2013, violent clashes erupted between ethnic Dinka and Nuer members of the presidential guard in Juba, South Sudan, igniting a brutal civil war that would lead to widespread violence and humanitarian crises across the nation.

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2014, Latvia officially adopted the euro as its currency, becoming the 18th member of the Eurozone. This transition was seen as a significant step in Latvia's integration into the European Union and its economic development.
events.name: Latvia Adopts Euro

events.enhanced_description: In February 2014, the West African Ebola virus epidemic began, ultimately infecting over 28,000 people and resulting in more than 11,000 deaths. This outbreak was the most severe in history, prompting international health responses and raising awareness about infectious disease preparedness.
events.name: West African Ebola Virus Epidemic Begins

events.enhanced_description: In February 2014, the number of people in the United States using mobile devices to access the internet surpassed those using desktop computers for the first time. This shift marked a significant change in digital consumption habits and foreshadowed the mobile-first era.
events.name: Mobile Internet Usage Surpasses Desktop

events.enhanced_description: The fifth ICC T20 World Cup was held in Bangladesh, showcasing international cricket teams competing in the shortest format of the game, which has gained immense popularity worldwide.

events.enhanced_description: In early 2014, prior to the major offensive, international military intervention against ISIL began, as the group gained ground in Iraq. This intervention was a response to the escalating violence and instability in the region.

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2014, the World Health Organization (WHO) declared the Ebola outbreak in West Africa a Public Health Emergency of International Concern. This declaration aimed to mobilize international resources and support to combat the outbreak, which had already claimed thousands of lives.
events.name: WHO declares Ebola outbreak a Public Health Emergency

events.enhanced_description: The World Summit of Nobel Peace Laureates, planned for October 13-15 in Cape Town, was suspended following a boycott by Nobel Laureates protesting the South African government's refusal to issue a visa to the Dalai Lama. This incident underscored the complex relationship between South Africa and China.
events.name: World Summit of Nobel Peace Laureates suspension

events.enhanced_description: On January 5, 2014, India successfully launched the GSAT-14 communication satellite aboard the GSLV Mk.II D5 rocket, marking the first successful flight of an Indian cryogenic rocket engine. This achievement showcased India's advancements in space technology.
events.name: GSAT-14 Satellite Launch

events.enhanced_description: On January 9, 2014, the Elk River Chemical Spill occurred in Charleston, West Virginia, when a chemical leak from a Freedom Industries plant contaminated the water supply for 300,000 residents. This environmental disaster raised serious concerns about chemical safety regulations and public health.
events.name: Elk River Chemical Spill

events.enhanced_description: On January 18, 2014, a stampede occurred near Malabar Hills in Mumbai during a religious event, leading to numerous fatalities and injuries. This tragedy underscored the challenges of managing large crowds in densely populated urban areas.
events.name: 2014 Mumbai stampede

events.enhanced_description: From February 7 to 23, 2014, the XXII Olympic Winter Games were held in Sochi, Russia, featuring the introduction of slopestyle events for the first time. The games showcased athletic prowess and international unity amidst political tensions.
events.name: XXII Olympic Winter Games

events.enhanced_description: On February 13, 2014, Belgium became the first country in the world to legalize euthanasia for terminally ill patients of any age. This landmark decision sparked global discussions about end-of-life choices and medical ethics.
events.name: Belgium Legalizes Euthanasia

events.enhanced_description: On February 15, 2014, a brutal attack in Izghe resulted in the massacre of 106 civilians, attributed to Boko Haram militants. This incident exemplified the escalating violence and humanitarian crisis in northeastern Nigeria.
events.name: Izghe attack

events.enhanced_description: On February 22, 2014, the Verkhovna Rada of Ukraine voted to remove President Viktor Yanukovych from office, replacing him with Oleksandr Turchynov, following days of civil unrest that resulted in around 100 fatalities. This pivotal moment marked a significant shift in Ukraine's political landscape.
events.name: Revolution of Dignity

events.enhanced_description: On February 26, 2014, Kevin Lau, a prominent Hong Kong journalist, was stabbed in a politically charged attack that raised alarms about press freedom and safety in the region. The incident sparked widespread condemnation and protests advocating for journalistic rights.
events.name: Knife attack on Kevin Lau

events.enhanced_description: On March 1, 2014, a brutal attack occurred at the Kunming railway station in Kunming, Yunnan, China, where eight knife-wielding terrorists killed 31 people and injured 143 others. This incident highlighted the ongoing security challenges faced by China.
events.name: Kunming Railway Station Attack

events.enhanced_description: On March 5, 2014, Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro severed diplomatic and political ties with Panama, accusing the country of conspiring against his government. This decision reflected the increasing tensions within Latin American politics.

events.enhanced_description: On March 8, 2014, Malaysia Airlines Flight 370, a Boeing 777 en route from Kuala Lumpur to Beijing, mysteriously disappeared over the Gulf of Thailand with 239 people on board. events.name: 2014 Larkana temple attack

events.enhanced_description: On March 16, 2014, a disputed referendum was held in Crimea regarding its status, which resulted in a majority voting to join Russia. This event escalated tensions between Russia and Ukraine, leading to international condemnation and sanctions.
events.name: Crimean Status Referendum

events.enhanced_description: On March 20, 2014, a mass shooting occurred at the Serena Hotel in Kabul, a popular venue for foreign diplomats and journalists, highlighting the persistent security threats in Afghanistan. events.enhanced_description: On March 24, 2014, a shooting incident occurred at the Norfolk Navy Station, raising alarms about security within military installations. The event prompted discussions about gun control and safety measures in sensitive environments.

events.enhanced_description: Gabriel García Márquez, the renowned Colombian author and Nobel laureate, passed away on April 17, 2014, in Jardines del Pedregal, Mexico. His death marked the loss of a literary giant whose works profoundly influenced contemporary literature.

events.enhanced_description: On April 13, 2014, a shooting spree at the Overland Park Jewish Community Center resulted in multiple fatalities and injuries, highlighting the threat of anti-Semitic violence in the United States. events.enhanced_description: On May 23, 2014, militants attacked the Indian consulate in Herat, Afghanistan, reflecting the complex geopolitical tensions in the region. This incident underscored the risks faced by diplomatic missions in volatile areas.
events.name: 2014 attack on Indian consulate in Herat

events.enhanced_description: Narendra Modi was sworn in as the 14th Prime Minister of India, succeeding Manmohan Singh, marking a significant political shift in the country with the rise of the Bharatiya Janata Party.
events.name: Narendra Modi Becomes Prime Minister of India

events.enhanced_description: On June 1, 2014, the Los Angeles Kings defeated the New York Rangers 3-2 in Game 5 of the Stanley Cup Final, clinching the series 4-1. This victory marked the Kings' second Stanley Cup championship in franchise history.
events.name: Los Angeles Kings Win Stanley Cup

events.enhanced_description: On June 5, 2014, the Sunni militant group known as the Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant (ISIL) launched a significant offensive in northern Iraq, targeting the capital city of Baghdad. This offensive aimed to overthrow the Shiite-led government of Prime Minister Nouri al-Maliki, escalating sectarian tensions in the region.
events.name: ISIS Offensive in Northern Iraq

events.enhanced_description: On June 8, 2014, a tragic incident occurred when a mass drowning took place in the Beas River, resulting in numerous fatalities. This event raised awareness about safety measures during religious pilgrimages in India.
events.name: 2014 Beas River Tragedy

events.enhanced_description: On June 12, 2014, ISIL perpetrated the Camp Speicher massacre, killing 1,566 Shia Iraqi Air Force cadets. This tragic event marked one of the deadliest terrorist attacks in history and highlighted the brutal tactics employed by ISIL during its campaign in Iraq.
events.name: Camp Speicher Massacre

events.enhanced_description: On June 13, 2014, an international military intervention against ISIL commenced, aimed at countering the group's rapid territorial gains in Iraq. This intervention involved multiple nations and marked a significant escalation in the global response to the threat posed by ISIL.
events.name: International Military Intervention Against ISIL

events.enhanced_description: On June 14, 2014, the Catholic Church announced the removal of restrictions on clerical marriage within the Eastern Catholic Churches' diaspora. This decision was seen as a significant shift in church policy, reflecting a more inclusive approach.
events.name: Catholic Church Removes Clerical Marriage Restrictions

events.enhanced_description: On June 15, 2014, the San Antonio Spurs triumphed over the Miami Heat in the NBA Finals, winning the series 4-1. This victory marked the Spurs' fifth championship in franchise history, solidifying their legacy in the NBA.
events.name: San Antonio Spurs Win NBA Championship

events.enhanced_description: On June 19, 2014, Felipe VI ascended to the throne of Spain following the abdication of his father, Juan Carlos I. This transition marked a new chapter in the Spanish monarchy, with Felipe VI emphasizing modernization and transparency.
events.name: Felipe VI Becomes King of Spain

events.enhanced_description: On June 25, 2014, a series of violent attacks occurred in central Nigeria, attributed to Boko Haram insurgents, exacerbating the ongoing security crisis in the region. These incidents highlighted the challenges faced by the Nigerian government in maintaining order.
events.name: June 2014 central Nigeria attacks

events.enhanced_description: On June 25, 2014, a bomb blast occurred in Wuse, Abuja, part of a series of attacks attributed to Boko Haram. This incident further underscored the escalating violence and terror threats in Nigeria.
events.name: Wuse Bomb Blast

events.enhanced_description: On June 29, 2014, the Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant (ISIL) declared itself a caliphate, with Abu Bakr al-Baghdadi as its caliph. This declaration marked a pivotal moment in the group's campaign to establish a state governed by its interpretation of Islamic law.
events.name: ISIL Declares Itself a Caliphate

events.enhanced_description: On July 8, 2014, Brazil faced Germany in the semi-finals of the FIFA World Cup, suffering a shocking defeat with a score of 7-1. This match is remembered as one of the most significant upsets in World Cup history, deeply impacting Brazilian football.
events.name: Brazil vs. Germany in FIFA World Cup Semi-Finals

events.enhanced_description: On July 9, 2014, a mass shooting occurred in Spring, Texas, raising concerns about gun violence in the United States. The event added to the ongoing national debate regarding gun control and public safety.
events.name: 2014 Spring, Texas shooting

events.enhanced_description: On July 13, 2014, Germany defeated Argentina 1-0 in the final match of the FIFA World Cup, securing their fourth title. The match, held at the Maracanã Stadium in Rio de Janeiro, was decided by a late goal from Mario Götze.
events.name: Germany Wins FIFA World Cup

events.enhanced_description: On July 17, 2014, Malaysia Airlines Flight 17, a Boeing 777, was shot down over eastern Ukraine, resulting in the deaths of all 298 passengers and crew on board. This tragic incident heightened tensions in the region and drew international condemnation.

image.caption: Makeshift memorial at Amsterdam Schiphol Airport for the victims of Malaysia Airlines Flight 17.
image.credit: Roman Boed from The Netherlands — Amsterdam Airport: Flight MH17 Memorial
image.date_qualification: Image date: 2014-07-20 12:44; this is a memorial photographed after the crash, not a photograph of the crash itself.
image.rights_statement: LicenseShortName: CC BY 2.0; UsageTerms: Creative Commons Attribution 2.0; Copyrighted: True

events.name: Malaysia Airlines Flight 17 Crash

events.enhanced_description: On July 18, 2014, Typhoon Rammasun made landfall in Hainan, China, as a category 5 super typhoon. The storm resulted in 88 fatalities and caused approximately $7.14 billion in damages, marking it as one of the most destructive typhoons to hit the region.
events.name: Typhoon Rammasun Hits Hainan, China

events.enhanced_description: On July 20, 2014, Monty Python Live (Mostly) concluded its run in London, marking the end of the famous British comedy group Monty Python, which had been active since 1969. This event celebrated their legacy in comedy and entertainment.
events.name: Monty Python Live (Mostly) Closes

events.enhanced_description: On July 21, 2014, the United Nations Security Council adopted Resolution 2166 in response to the shootdown of Malaysia Airlines Flight 17. This resolution called for accountability and emphasized the need for a thorough investigation into the incident.

locations.name: New York City, New York, United States

events.name: UN Security Council Adopts Resolution 2166

events.enhanced_description: On July 24, 2014, Air Algérie Flight 5017, a McDonnell Douglas MD-83, crashed in Mali, resulting in the deaths of all 116 people on board. This tragic accident raised concerns about aviation safety in conflict zones.
events.name: Air Algérie Flight 5017 Crash

events.enhanced_description: On July 28, 2014, the world marked the 100-year anniversary of the commencement of World War I, which began with Austria-Hungary's declaration of war on Serbia. This anniversary prompted reflections on the war's impact and the lessons learned.
events.name: 100-Year Anniversary of World War I's Commencement

events.enhanced_description: On August 3, 2014, the 2014 Commonwealth Games took place in Glasgow, Scotland, featuring athletes from across the Commonwealth nations. This multi-sport event celebrated athletic excellence and cultural exchange.
events.name: 2014 Commonwealth Games

events.enhanced_description: On August 3, 2014, ISIL launched a brutal attack in the Sinjar District of Iraq, resulting in the massacre of over 4,000 Yazidis. This event highlighted the severe humanitarian crisis and the persecution faced by minority groups in the region.
events.name: Sinjar Massacre

events.enhanced_description: On August 4, 2014, the death of Ms Dhu, an Aboriginal woman, in police custody sparked outrage and highlighted issues of systemic racism and police accountability in Australia. This incident ignited discussions about the treatment of Indigenous Australians.
events.name: Death of Ms Dhu

events.enhanced_description: On August 7, 2014, Khmer Rouge leaders Nuon Chea and Khieu Samphan were found guilty of crimes against humanity and sentenced to life imprisonment by the Khmer Rouge Tribunal. This verdict was a significant step towards justice for the victims of the Khmer Rouge regime.
events.name: Khmer Rouge Leaders Convicted

events.enhanced_description: In 2014, the United States military initiated an air campaign in northern Iraq aimed at curbing the advance of ISIL militants, who were rapidly gaining territory and threatening regional stability. This intervention marked a significant escalation in U.S. involvement in Iraq following the withdrawal of troops in 2011.
events.name: American-led Intervention in Iraq

events.enhanced_description: On August 9, 2014, the shooting of Michael Brown, an African American teenager, by a police officer in Ferguson, Missouri, sparked widespread protests and riots. This incident became a pivotal moment in the Black Lives Matter movement, highlighting issues of racial injustice and police violence in the United States.
events.name: Shooting of Michael Brown in Ferguson

events.enhanced_description: Starting on September 15, 2014, ISIS militants launched a prolonged offensive to capture the strategically significant town of Kobanî in northern Syria. The battle lasted for six months and became a focal point of resistance against ISIS, drawing international attention and support for the Kurdish defenders.
events.name: ISIS offensive on Kobanî

events.enhanced_description: On September 18, 2014, Scotland held a historic referendum in which voters decisively chose to remain part of the United Kingdom, rejecting independence. The referendum was a culmination of years of political debate and was marked by high voter turnout and intense campaigning.
events.name: 2014 Scottish independence referendum

events.enhanced_description: The Battle of Sanaa on September 21, 2014, marked the beginning of the Yemeni Civil War, as Houthi forces captured the capital city of Sanaa. This event led to a rapid takeover of the Yemeni government and escalated the conflict that would draw in regional powers.
events.name: Battle of Sanaa

events.enhanced_description: On September 22, 2014, the United States and several Arab partners launched an airstrike campaign against ISIS targets in Syria. This intervention aimed to degrade ISIS's capabilities and support local forces fighting against the group.
events.name: American-led intervention in Syria

events.enhanced_description: On September 24, 2014, Alton Nolen attacked a food processing plant in Moore, Oklahoma, resulting in a fatality. This incident raised questions about workplace safety and the motivations behind such violent acts.
events.name: Alton Nolen

events.enhanced_description: On September 24, 2014, India's Mars Orbiter Mission, known as Mangalyaan, successfully entered Martian orbit, making India the first Asian nation to achieve this feat. The mission was celebrated for its cost-effectiveness and technological achievements.
events.name: Mars Orbiter Mission reaches Mars

events.enhanced_description: The 2014 World Summit of Nobel Peace Laureates, scheduled for October 13-15 in Cape Town, was suspended due to a boycott by Nobel Laureates protesting the South African government's refusal to grant a visa to the Dalai Lama. This incident highlighted tensions between South Africa and China.
events.name: 2014 World Summit of Nobel Peace Laureates

events.enhanced_description: On the night of September 26, 2014, forty-three male students from the Ayotzinapa Rural Teachers' College were forcibly abducted in Iguala, Guerrero, Mexico. The incident, allegedly involving local police and organized crime, sparked widespread protests and demands for justice, leading to the resignation of Guerrero's governor.
events.name: Ayotzinapa student abduction

events.enhanced_description: On September 27, 2014, Mount Ontake erupted unexpectedly, resulting in the deaths of several climbers on its slopes. This eruption was Japan's deadliest volcanic event in over 90 years, prompting widespread concern about volcanic activity in the region.
events.name: Mount Ontake eruption

events.enhanced_description: On September 28, 2014, Benny Tai Yiu-ting announced the launch of the Occupy Central movement as thousands of protesters occupied the Hong Kong government headquarters. The protests highlighted demands for democratic reforms and were met with police resistance, including the use of tear gas.
events.name: Hong Kong protests

events.enhanced_description: On October 3, 2014, Stefan Löfven was appointed as the new Prime Minister of Sweden, succeeding Fredrik Reinfeldt. His leadership marked a shift in Swedish politics, focusing on social welfare and immigration issues.
events.name: Stefan Löfven becomes Prime Minister of Sweden

events.enhanced_description: On October 19, 2014, the Roman Catholic Church beatified Pope Paul VI, recognizing his contributions to the Church and his role in the Second Vatican Council. This event was a significant moment in the Church's modern history.
events.name: Beatification of Pope Paul VI

events.enhanced_description: On October 20, 2014, Joko Widodo was inaugurated as the 7th President of Indonesia, marking a new era in Indonesian politics with promises of reform and development. His election was seen as a shift towards a more populist approach in governance.
events.name: Joko Widodo inaugurated as President of Indonesia

events.enhanced_description: On October 24, 2014, Alan Eustace set a world record for the highest and longest free fall jump from an altitude of 135,908 feet over Roswell, New Mexico. His jump, which broke the sound barrier, showcased advancements in space diving technology.
events.name: Alan Eustace's free fall jump

events.enhanced_description: On October 31, 2014, Blaise Compaoré resigned as President of Burkina Faso following widespread protests against his attempts to amend the constitution to extend presidential term limits. His resignation marked a significant turning point in the country's political landscape.
events.name: Blaise Compaoré resigns

events.enhanced_description: On November 1, 2014, Bangladesh experienced a nationwide blackout that affected millions of people. The outage was attributed to a failure in the power grid, highlighting ongoing challenges in the country's energy infrastructure.
events.name: Bangladesh nationwide blackout

events.enhanced_description: On November 2, 2014, a significant prison break occurred in Kogi State, Nigeria, allowing numerous inmates to escape. This event highlighted the challenges facing the Nigerian penal system and the ongoing issues of security and governance.
events.name: Kogi prison break

events.enhanced_description: On November 2, 2014, the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) released the final part of its Fifth Assessment Report, warning of severe and irreversible damage from global emissions of CO2. The report called for urgent action to mitigate climate change impacts.
events.name: IPCC releases Fifth Assessment Report

events.enhanced_description: On November 3, 2014, One World Trade Center officially opened in New York City, becoming the tallest building in the Western Hemisphere. The building stands as a symbol of resilience and renewal following the September 11 attacks.

image.caption: Worm’s-eye view of One World Trade Center, its glass facade reflecting clouds.
image.date_qualification: Photographed April 17, 2026; the image is a later view of the building, not a photograph of the 2014 opening.
image.rights_statement: LicenseShortName: CC BY-SA 4.0; UsageTerms: Creative Commons Attribution-Share Alike 4.0; Copyrighted: True

events.name: One World Trade Center opens

events.enhanced_description: On November 12, 2014, the Philae probe, part of the Rosetta mission, successfully landed on Comet 67P, marking the first time a spacecraft had landed on a comet. This historic achievement provided valuable data about the origins of the solar system.
events.name: Philae probe lands on Comet 67P

events.enhanced_description: On November 18, 2014, an explosion occurred at a wastewater treatment facility in Santa Clara, California, raising concerns about industrial safety and environmental regulations. The incident prompted investigations into safety protocols in similar facilities.
events.name: Santa Clara Waste Water explosion

events.enhanced_description: On November 23, 2014, a suicide bombing at a volleyball match in Yahyakhel District resulted in numerous civilian casualties, underscoring the ongoing violence in Afghanistan. This tragic event highlighted the risks faced by civilians in conflict zones.
events.name: 2014 Yahyakhel suicide bombing

events.enhanced_description: On November 28, 2014, a bombing in Kano, Nigeria, attributed to Boko Haram, resulted in significant casualties and injuries. This attack exemplified the ongoing threat of terrorism in Nigeria and the challenges faced by security forces.
events.name: 2014 Kano bombing

events.enhanced_description: The murder of Ibolya Ryan, an American teacher, occurred in Abu Dhabi, where she was stabbed to death in her home. This incident raised concerns about safety and crime in the UAE, prompting discussions on the legal system and law enforcement.
events.name: Murder of Ibolya Ryan

events.enhanced_description: On December 3, 2014, the Japanese space agency JAXA launched the uncrewed Hayabusa2 space probe from the Tanegashima Space Center. The mission aims to collect rock samples from the asteroid Ryugu and return them to Earth.
events.name: Hayabusa2 launched

events.enhanced_description: On December 9, 2014, a bus bombing in Maramag, Bukidnon, Philippines, resulted in multiple casualties and injuries. The attack was attributed to ongoing conflicts in the region, highlighting the security challenges faced by the country.
events.name: 2014 Bukidnon bus bombing

events.enhanced_description: A series of bombings in Kabul on December 11, 2014, targeted military and civilian areas, resulting in significant casualties. These attacks underscored the ongoing violence and instability in Afghanistan amidst the Taliban's resurgence.
events.name: December 2014 Kabul bombings

events.enhanced_description: On December 15, 2014, a shooting incident in Salford Township, Montgomery County, Pennsylvania, resulted in multiple fatalities. The event shocked the local community and raised discussions about gun violence and mental health.
events.name: 2014 Montgomery County shootings

events.enhanced_description: On December 15, 2014, a siege at the Lindt Cafe in Sydney resulted in the deaths of two hostages and the gunman, Man Haron Monis. The incident raised concerns about terrorism and security in Australia.
events.name: Lindt Cafe siege

events.enhanced_description: On December 16, 2014, the Pakistani Taliban carried out a mass shooting at an army school in Peshawar, Pakistan, killing at least 145 people, mostly schoolchildren. This tragic event drew international condemnation and highlighted the ongoing security challenges in Pakistan.
events.name: Peshawar school massacre

events.enhanced_description: On December 17, 2014, U.S. President Barack Obama announced the resumption of normal diplomatic relations between the United States and Cuba, marking a significant shift in U.S. foreign policy after decades of isolation. This announcement aimed to foster dialogue and cooperation between the two nations.
events.name: U.S. resumes diplomatic relations with Cuba

events.enhanced_description: On December 19, 2014, the tragic discovery of eight children found dead in Cairns, Queensland, shocked Australia. The incident, attributed to a family member, raised urgent discussions on child safety and mental health issues.
events.name: Cairns child killings

events.enhanced_description: On December 22, 2014, a vehicle ramming attack in Nantes, France, injured several people and heightened fears of terrorism in Europe. The incident prompted increased security measures and investigations into potential extremist links.
events.name: 2014 Nantes attack

events.enhanced_description: On December 28, 2014, Indonesia AirAsia Flight 8501 crashed into the Java Sea while en route from Surabaya, Indonesia, to Singapore. All 162 passengers and crew on board perished, marking one of the deadliest aviation disasters in Indonesian history.
events.name: Indonesia AirAsia Flight 8501 crash

events.enhanced_description: On December 29, 2014, clashes between Boko Haram militants and Cameroonian forces in the Far North region resulted in significant violence. This incident highlighted the ongoing threat of terrorism in the region and the challenges faced by local security forces.
events.name: December 2014 Cameroon clashes

events.enhanced_description: On December 31, 2014, a stampede occurred during New Year's Eve celebrations in Shanghai, China, resulting in the deaths of 36 people and injuring 49 others. The incident raised concerns about crowd control and safety measures during large public events.
events.name: Shanghai New Year's Eve stampede

events.enhanced_description: The Fantoni and Nunes cheating allegation emerged in early 2015, surrounding a contract bridge scandal involving high-profile players. The controversy raised questions about ethics in competitive bridge and led to discussions about regulations in the sport.
events.name: Fantoni and Nunes cheating allegation

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2015, Lithuania officially adopted the euro as its currency, replacing the litas and becoming the 19th member of the Eurozone. This significant economic transition aimed to strengthen Lithuania's integration into the European Union.
events.name: Lithuania adopts the euro

events.enhanced_description: In January 2015, ISIL fighters detonated three car bombs and opened fire on civilians in Kobanî, Syria, resulting in the deaths of more than 220 people. This massacre underscored the brutal tactics employed by ISIL during the Syrian Civil War.
events.name: Kobanî Massacre

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2015, a terrorist attack occurred at a tourist resort in Port El Kantaoui, Tunisia, where 22-year-old Seifeddine Rezgui opened fire, killing 38 people. This attack targeted foreign tourists and raised concerns about security in Tunisia.
events.name: Sousse Attacks

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2015, a suicide bomber attacked the Imam Ja'far as-Sadiq Mosque in Kuwait City, killing 27 people and injuring 227 others. This attack targeted Shia Muslims during Friday prayers, highlighting sectarian tensions in the region.
events.name: Kuwait Mosque Bombing

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2015, NASA's New Horizons spacecraft made its historic flyby of Pluto, becoming the first spacecraft to explore the dwarf planet. This landmark event provided unprecedented data and images, revealing Pluto's complex geology and atmosphere.

image.caption: Artist’s impression of the New Horizons spacecraft flying past Pluto.
