events.enhanced_description: The 2018 Mexican general election was held to elect the president, all 128 members of the Senate, and all 500 members of the Chamber of Deputies. Andrés Manuel López Obrador was elected president, leading his coalition to a significant majority.
events.name: 2018 Mexican general election

events.enhanced_description: Lithuania officially became the 36th member of the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD), marking a significant milestone in its economic development and integration into the global economy.
events.name: Lithuania joins OECD

events.enhanced_description: Shoko Asahara, the former leader of the Aum Shinrikyo cult, was executed along with six other members for their roles in the 1995 Tokyo subway sarin attack. This event marked a significant moment in Japan's legal and social response to terrorism.

image.caption: Aum Shinrikyo religious facility.
image.credit: 吉川 祐介 — Own work
image.date_qualification: Depicts an Aum Shinrikyo religious facility, not Asahara’s execution; image date: 1996-09-08.
image.rights_statement: LicenseShortName: CC BY-SA 4.0; UsageTerms: Creative Commons Attribution-Share Alike 4.0; Copyrighted: True

events.name: Execution of Shoko Asahara

events.enhanced_description: The 2018 Japan floods resulted from torrential rains, causing flash floods and landslides in Hiroshima, Kurashiki, and Ehime Prefectures. The disaster led to 232 confirmed deaths and significant damage to infrastructure.
events.name: 2018 Japan floods

events.enhanced_description: Eritrea and Ethiopia officially declared an end to their twenty-year conflict, a significant step towards peace and reconciliation in the Horn of Africa. This agreement was celebrated by both nations and the international community.
events.name: Eritrea and Ethiopia end conflict

events.enhanced_description: Twelve boys and their football coach were successfully rescued from the flooded Tham Luang Nang Non cave in Thailand after a 17-day ordeal that captured global attention. The rescue operation involved numerous divers and rescuers from around the world.

locations.name: Tham Luang Nang Non cave, Chiang Rai, Thailand

events.name: Tham Luang cave rescue

events.enhanced_description: The 2018 Brussels NATO summit was held to discuss key issues facing the alliance, including defense spending and security challenges. Leaders from member countries gathered to reaffirm their commitments to collective defense.
events.name: 2018 Brussels NATO summit

events.enhanced_description: On July 15, 2018, the 2018 FIFA World Cup final was held at Luzhniki Stadium in Moscow, where France triumphed over Croatia to win their second World Cup title. The match was a thrilling contest, showcasing top-tier football talent.
events.name: 2018 FIFA World Cup Final

events.enhanced_description: The EU–Japan Economic Partnership Agreement was signed, creating the world's largest bilateral free trade deal and establishing an open trade zone covering nearly one-third of global GDP. This agreement aimed to enhance economic ties between the two regions.
events.name: EU–Japan Economic Partnership Agreement signed

events.enhanced_description: The collapse of Saddle Dam D in Paksong, Laos, resulted in a catastrophic flood, leaving up to 1,100 people missing. This disaster highlighted the risks associated with dam construction and management in the region.
events.name: Collapse of Saddle Dam D in Laos

events.enhanced_description: In July 2018, devastating wildfires swept through Greece, particularly affecting the regions of Attica, including the town of Mati. The fires resulted in the tragic loss of 102 lives and the destruction of numerous homes and structures, prompting widespread national and international responses for aid and recovery.
events.name: Heavy wildfires in Greece leave 102 dead and more than a hundred buildings destroyed

events.enhanced_description: Scientists reported the discovery of a subglacial lake on Mars, located 1.5 km below the southern polar ice cap. This finding marked a significant milestone in the search for water and potential life on Mars.
events.name: Discovery of subglacial lake on Mars

events.enhanced_description: Severe wildfires in Greece resulted in the tragic loss of 102 lives and the destruction of over a hundred buildings. The fires were among the deadliest in Greece's history, prompting national and international responses.
events.name: Wildfires in Greece

events.enhanced_description: On July 26, 2018, Facebook's share price plummeted by nearly 20% after the company disclosed a slowdown in user growth, attributed to the fallout from the Cambridge Analytica data leak scandal. This drop resulted in a staggering loss of over $109 billion in market value, marking the largest single-day loss in corporate history.
events.name: Facebook share price drop

events.enhanced_description: The longest total lunar eclipse of the 21st century occurred, lasting 102 minutes and 57 seconds. This celestial event attracted significant attention from astronomers and skywatchers around the world.

image.caption: Photograph of the total lunar eclipse, credited to Auvo Korpi.
image.credit: Auvo Korpi from Huhtamo, Finland — 2018.07.28 0005 300mm Lunar Total Eclipse 1
image.date_qualification: The supplied image date is 2018-07-28 00:18; this is the recorded image date, not an upload date. The event article dates the eclipse to July 27, 2018.
image.rights_statement: LicenseShortName: CC BY 2.0; UsageTerms: Creative Commons Attribution 2.0; Copyrighted: True

events.name: Longest total lunar eclipse of the 21st century

events.enhanced_description: On July 31, 2018, Aeroméxico Connect Flight 2431 crashed shortly after takeoff from Durango International Airport due to sudden wind shear caused by a microburst. Remarkably, all 103 people on board survived, although 39 sustained injuries in the incident.
events.name: Aeroméxico Connect Flight 2431 crash

events.enhanced_description: The 2018 Kivu Ebola outbreak began in August 2018 in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, marking the second-deadliest outbreak of the Ebola virus to date. It would later surpass the 2013 West African Ebola epidemic in terms of fatalities.
events.name: 2018 Kivu Ebola outbreak begins

events.enhanced_description: On August 2, 2018, Apple Inc. became the world's first public company to reach a market capitalization of $1 trillion. This milestone highlighted the company's significant growth and dominance in the technology sector under the leadership of CEO Tim Cook.
events.name: Apple Inc. achieves $1 trillion market capitalization

events.enhanced_description: On August 5, 2018, a magnitude 6.9 earthquake struck the island of Lombok, Indonesia, resulting in the deaths of 563 individuals and injuring over a thousand. The earthquake caused widespread destruction and prompted significant humanitarian responses.
events.name: Lombok earthquake

events.enhanced_description: On August 7, 2018, the United States reimposed sanctions on Iran, which had been lifted under the 2015 nuclear deal. This action escalated tensions between the two nations and had significant implications for international relations.
events.name: United States reimposes sanctions on Iran

events.enhanced_description: On August 10, 2018, widespread protests erupted across Romania against the government led by Prime Minister Viorica Dăncilă and PSD leader Liviu Dragnea. The protests turned violent in Bucharest, resulting in over 400 injuries and raising concerns about government repression.
events.name: Protests in Romania

events.enhanced_description: On August 10, 2018, heavy rainfall led to severe flooding in the Indian state of Kerala, marking the worst floods to hit the region in a century. The disaster resulted in significant loss of life and widespread displacement of communities.

image.caption: Flooding in Angamaly, Kerala.
image.date_qualification: Photograph of flooding in Angamaly during the 2018 Kerala floods; the saved image date is 2018-08-16, after the event record’s 2018-08-10 date.
image.rights_statement: LicenseShortName: CC BY-SA 4.0; UsageTerms: Creative Commons Attribution-Share Alike 4.0; Copyrighted: True

events.name: Floods in Kerala, India

events.enhanced_description: On August 12, 2018, the five littoral states of the Caspian Sea—Russia, Kazakhstan, Azerbaijan, Iran, and Turkmenistan—signed a convention that established the legal status of the Caspian Sea, resolving a 20-year dispute over territorial rights and resource management.
events.name: Caspian Sea legal status convention signed

events.enhanced_description: On August 12, 2018, NASA launched the Parker Solar Probe, an uncrewed spacecraft designed to study the Sun's outer atmosphere and solar wind. This mission aims to enhance our understanding of solar phenomena and their impact on the solar system.

image.caption: The United Launch Alliance Delta IV Heavy rocket launches NASA’s Parker Solar Probe from Launch Complex 37 at Cape Canaveral Air Force Station, Florida.
image.date_qualification: Depicted event date: August 12, 2018; image metadata timestamp: 2018-08-12 03:31:01. Upload timestamp is not the depicted date.
image.rights_statement: LicenseShortName: Public domain; UsageTerms: Public domain; Copyrighted: False

events.name: NASA launches Parker Solar Probe

events.enhanced_description: On August 14, 2018, part of the Morandi Bridge in Genoa, Italy, collapsed during a violent storm, resulting in 43 fatalities. The incident raised serious concerns about infrastructure safety and accountability, with government officials blaming the private company responsible for the bridge's maintenance.
events.name: Morandi Bridge collapse

events.enhanced_description: The 2018 Asian Games were held from August 18 to September 2, 2018, in Jakarta and Palembang, Indonesia. This multi-sport event featured thousands of athletes from across Asia competing in various sports, showcasing regional talent and fostering unity.
events.name: 2018 Asian Games

events.enhanced_description: On August 20, 2018, 15-year-old Swedish student Greta Thunberg began her school strike for climate outside the Swedish parliament in Stockholm. Her actions sparked a global movement advocating for urgent action on climate change, inspiring millions of students worldwide to participate in similar protests.
events.name: Greta Thunberg's school strike for climate

events.enhanced_description: On August 23, 2018, Ecuador announced its withdrawal from the Bolivarian Alliance for the Peoples of Our America (ALBA), a regional bloc founded by leftist governments. This decision reflected a shift in Ecuador's foreign policy under President Lenín Moreno.
events.name: Ecuador withdraws from ALBA

events.enhanced_description: On August 24, 2018, Scott Morrison was elected as the new Prime Minister of Australia following a leadership ballot that ousted Malcolm Turnbull. Morrison's ascension marked a significant shift in the Australian political landscape.
events.name: Scott Morrison becomes Prime Minister of Australia

events.enhanced_description: On August 25, 2018, the highly publicized amateur boxing match between YouTubers KSI and Logan Paul took place at the Manchester Arena. Dubbed the biggest amateur boxing match in history, it attracted significant media attention and a large audience both in-person and online.

image.caption: Logan Paul at the weigh-in for his white-collar boxing match against KSI.
image.credit: KSIvsLogan — YouTube : KSI VS. LOGAN PAUL [OFFICIAL WEIGH IN] – View/save archived versions on archive.org
image.date_qualification: Depicted 2018-08-24, the day before the match on 2018-08-25.
image.rights_statement: LicenseShortName: CC BY 3.0; UsageTerms: Creative Commons Attribution 3.0; Copyrighted: True

events.name: KSI vs Logan Paul boxing match

events.enhanced_description: On September 2, 2018, a catastrophic fire broke out at the National Museum of Brazil in Rio de Janeiro, destroying over 90% of its collection, which included 20 million items. The incident highlighted the urgent need for better preservation and funding for cultural institutions.
events.name: Fire at the National Museum of Brazil

events.enhanced_description: On September 6, 2018, the Supreme Court of India delivered a landmark ruling decriminalizing homosexuality, overturning a colonial-era law that had criminalized same-sex relations. This decision marked a significant victory for LGBTQ+ rights in India.
events.name: Supreme Court of India decriminalizes homosexuality

events.enhanced_description: On September 9, 2018, Sweden held its general election to elect all 349 members of the Riksdag, the country's unicameral legislature. The election results indicated a shift in the political landscape, with significant gains for the Sweden Democrats.
events.name: 2018 Swedish general election

events.enhanced_description: On September 14, 2018, Hurricane Florence made landfall in North Carolina as a Category 1 hurricane, leading to record-breaking flooding and resulting in 54 fatalities. The storm caused an estimated $24.2 billion in damages, highlighting the devastating impact of climate-related disasters.
events.name: Hurricane Florence makes landfall

events.enhanced_description: On September 14, 2018, Typhoon Mangkhut struck the Philippines, Taiwan, Hong Kong, and parts of China, resulting in over 60 fatalities. The typhoon was one of the strongest storms of the year, causing widespread destruction and prompting emergency responses across the affected regions.

image.caption: Enhanced infrared satellite animation of Typhoon Mangkhut making landfall over northeastern Luzon.
image.credit: National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration Satellite Services Division — http://www.ssd.noaa.gov/PS/TROP/floaters/
image.date_qualification: The animation depicts the storm’s landfall on September 14, 2018; the upload date is later.
image.rights_statement: LicenseShortName: Public domain; UsageTerms: Public domain; Copyrighted: False

events.name: Typhoon Mangkhut impacts Asia

events.enhanced_description: On September 16, 2018, the first hydrail train entered service on the Buxtehude-Bremervörde-Bremerhaven-Cuxhaven line in Lower Saxony, Germany. This innovative train, powered by hydrogen fuel cells, represents a significant step towards sustainable public transportation.
events.name: Hydrail train enters service in Germany

events.enhanced_description: On September 17, 2018, during the Syrian Civil War, a Russian Il-20 reconnaissance plane was shot down by a Syrian surface-to-air missile while Israeli jets conducted airstrikes in western Syria. The incident resulted in the deaths of all 15 Russian servicemen on board, leading Russia to blame Israel for using the Russian aircraft as cover during the strikes.
events.name: Syrian Civil War: Il-20 Plane Shot Down

events.enhanced_description: On September 20, 2018, the MV Nyerere ferry capsized on Lake Victoria, resulting in the tragic deaths of at least 228 passengers. The incident highlighted ongoing concerns regarding safety regulations and the management of ferry services in the region.

image.caption: MV Nyerere ferry docked in Bugolora, Ukerewe Island.
image.date_qualification: Photographed October 2015, before the capsizing on 20 September 2018.
image.rights_statement: LicenseShortName: CC BY-SA 4.0; UsageTerms: Creative Commons Attribution-Share Alike 4.0; Copyrighted: True

events.name: MV Nyerere Capsizes

events.enhanced_description: On September 22, 2018, a terrorist attack during a military parade in Ahvaz, Iran, resulted in the deaths of 30 individuals, including five attackers, and injured 70 others. The attack was attributed to separatist groups and highlighted the ongoing tensions within the region.
events.name: Ahvaz Military Parade Attack

events.enhanced_description: On September 28, 2018, a magnitude 7.5 earthquake struck Sulawesi, Indonesia, triggering a devastating tsunami that claimed the lives of at least 4,340 people and injured over 10,679 others. The disaster caused widespread destruction and highlighted the region's vulnerability to seismic activity.
events.name: Sulawesi Earthquake and Tsunami

events.enhanced_description: On October 1, 2018, the International Court of Justice ruled that Chile is not obliged to negotiate access to the Pacific Ocean with Bolivia, a significant decision in the long-standing dispute between the two countries over maritime access. This ruling was met with mixed reactions from both nations.
events.name: ICJ Ruling on Chile and Bolivia

events.enhanced_description: On October 2, 2018, journalist Jamal Khashoggi was murdered inside the Saudi consulate in Istanbul, Turkey, an event that triggered a significant diplomatic crisis for Saudi Arabia. The incident raised global concerns regarding press freedom and human rights.
events.name: Jamal Khashoggi Murder

events.enhanced_description: On October 6, 2018, Latvia held its parliamentary election to elect all 100 members of the Saeima, the country's unicameral legislature. The election was a significant event in Latvian politics, reflecting the public's sentiments and priorities.
events.name: 2018 Latvian Parliamentary Election

events.enhanced_description: On October 8, 2018, the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) released its Special Report on Global Warming of 1.5 °C, warning that urgent and unprecedented changes across all aspects of society are necessary to limit global warming. The report emphasized the critical need for immediate action to mitigate climate change.
events.name: IPCC Special Report on Global Warming

events.enhanced_description: On October 10, 2018, Hurricane Michael made landfall at Mexico Beach, Florida, as a Category 5 hurricane, with winds reaching 160 mph. This hurricane was noted as the most intense to strike the mainland United States since Hurricane Camille in 1969, causing extensive damage and loss of life.
events.name: Hurricane Michael Landfall

events.enhanced_description: On October 16, 2018, Canada legalized the sale and use of cannabis, becoming the second country in the world to do so after Uruguay. This landmark decision marked a significant shift in drug policy and was seen as a progressive step in the realm of public health and criminal justice.
events.name: Canada Legalizes Cannabis

events.enhanced_description: Canada became the first major industrialized country to legalize cannabis for recreational use, with the legislation taking effect on October 17, 2018. This landmark decision was seen as a significant step in drug policy reform.
events.name: Canada legalizes cannabis for recreational use

events.enhanced_description: On October 17, 2018, a tragic school shooting and bomb attack in Kerch, Crimea, resulted in the deaths of 20 individuals and injuries to 70 others. This incident raised serious concerns about school safety and security in the region.
events.name: Kerch School Shooting

events.enhanced_description: On October 19, 2018, a tragic accident occurred when a train ran through a crowd at a Hindu festival in Amritsar, Punjab, resulting in at least 59 deaths and over 100 injuries. This incident sparked outrage and raised questions about safety measures during large public gatherings.
events.name: Train Accident in Punjab

events.enhanced_description: On October 20, 2018, approximately 700,000 people marched through central London demanding a second referendum on the final Brexit deal. This event became one of the largest protests in the UK, reflecting widespread public concern over the implications of Brexit.
events.name: Brexit March in London

events.enhanced_description: On October 23, 2018, the Hong Kong–Zhuhai–Macau Bridge, the world's longest sea crossing bridge, was officially opened by Chinese Paramount leader Xi Jinping. This monumental infrastructure project symbolizes enhanced connectivity in the Greater Bay Area.

image.caption: View of the west section of the Hong Kong–Zhuhai–Macau Bridge from a TurboJET.
image.date_qualification: Photograph taken on 2018-09-02, before the bridge’s inauguration on 2018-10-23 and opening to the public on 2018-10-24; depicts the bridge, not the opening ceremony.
image.rights_statement: LicenseShortName: CC BY-SA 4.0; UsageTerms: Creative Commons Attribution-Share Alike 4.0; Copyrighted: True

events.name: Opening of Hong Kong–Zhuhai–Macau Bridge

events.enhanced_description: On October 26, 2018, the highly anticipated video game Red Dead Redemption II was released on PS4 and Xbox One. The game would go on to become one of the best-selling video games of all time, with over 50 million copies sold.

locations.name: New York City, New York, United States

events.name: Release of Red Dead Redemption II

events.enhanced_description: On October 27, 2018, Michael D. Higgins was re-elected as President of Ireland, receiving 822,566 first preference votes in the election. His victory reaffirmed his popularity and the public's support for his policies.
events.name: Michael D. Higgins Re-elected

events.enhanced_description: On October 28, 2018, Jair Bolsonaro was elected as the next President of Brazil, securing 55% of the vote. His election marked a significant shift in Brazilian politics towards a right-wing agenda.
events.name: Jair Bolsonaro Elected President of Brazil

events.enhanced_description: On October 29, 2018, Lion Air Flight 610 crashed into the Java Sea shortly after takeoff from Jakarta, killing all 189 people on board. The incident raised serious concerns about aviation safety in Indonesia.
events.name: Lion Air Flight 610 Crash

events.enhanced_description: On October 30, 2018, NASA's Kepler space telescope mission concluded after the spacecraft ran out of fuel. The mission significantly advanced our understanding of exoplanets and the potential for life beyond Earth.

image.caption: NASA illustration of the Kepler space telescope.
image.date_qualification: Retrospective spacecraft illustration, not a photograph of the mission’s conclusion. No depicted image date is supplied.
image.rights_statement: LicenseShortName: Public domain; UsageTerms: Public domain; Copyrighted: False

locations.name: NASA Ames Research Center, California, United States

events.name: NASA's Kepler Mission Ends

events.enhanced_description: On November 1, 2018, NASA's Dawn mission concluded after the spacecraft ran out of hydrazine fuel. The mission provided invaluable data about the early solar system and the dwarf planet Ceres.

locations.name: NASA Jet Propulsion Laboratory, California, United States

events.name: NASA's Dawn Mission Concludes

events.enhanced_description: On November 4, 2018, three Venezuelan border guards were killed and ten others wounded in a suspected attack by the Colombian ELN guerrilla group in Amazonas state. This incident underscored the ongoing violence and instability along the Venezuela-Colombia border.
events.name: Amazonas Ambush

events.enhanced_description: On November 5, 2018, NASA's Voyager 2 spacecraft crossed the heliopause, marking its entry into interstellar space. Coincidentally, the Parker Solar Probe reached its first perihelion, the closest point to the Sun on its initial orbit, showcasing significant advancements in space exploration.
events.name: Voyager 2 and Parker Solar Probe Milestones

events.enhanced_description: On November 6, 2018, the United States held its midterm elections, which resulted in a significant shift in the balance of power in Congress. The Democratic Party regained control of the House of Representatives, while the Republican Party maintained control of the Senate.
events.name: 2018 United States Midterm Elections

events.enhanced_description: On November 8, 2018, the Camp Fire ignited in Butte County, California, becoming the deadliest and most destructive wildfire in California's history. The fire resulted in 88 fatalities and the destruction of 18,804 structures, devastating the town of Paradise.
events.name: Camp Fire Ignition

events.enhanced_description: On November 8, 2018, the Royal Norwegian Navy frigate Helge Ingstad collided with an oil tanker and subsequently sank in shallow waters off the coast of Norway. The incident led to significant damage, and the frigate was later scrapped.
events.name: Helge Ingstad Collision

events.enhanced_description: On November 11, 2018, nations around the world commemorated the centenary of the end of World War I with ceremonies, speeches, and parades. This day, known as Armistice Day, Veterans Day, and Remembrance Day, honored the sacrifices made during the war.
events.name: Centenary of World War I Armistice

events.enhanced_description: On November 26, 2018, NASA's InSight probe successfully landed on the surface of Mars. This mission aims to study the interior of the planet and gather data on its geological activity.
events.name: NASA's InSight Landing

events.enhanced_description: On November 27, 2018, Ukraine declared martial law following an armed incident in the Kerch Strait, where the Russian Federal Security Service fired upon and captured three Ukrainian Navy vessels. This escalation heightened tensions between Russia and Ukraine.
events.name: Kerch Strait Incident

events.enhanced_description: On November 28, 2018, Chinese scientist He Jiankui announced at a public conference in Hong Kong that he had altered the DNA of twin girls to make them resistant to HIV. This controversial claim raised significant ethical concerns regarding gene editing in humans.
events.name: He Jiankui's Gene Editing Announcement

events.enhanced_description: On November 30, 2018, the Kanden Tunnel Trolleybus, one of the last remaining trolleybus systems in Japan, closed its operations. This marked the end of an era for this mode of public transportation in the country.
events.name: Closure of Kanden Tunnel Trolleybus

events.enhanced_description: On December 1, 2018, France experienced its worst civil unrest since the protests of 1968 due to the yellow vests movement. Protests in Paris escalated into riots, resulting in hundreds of injuries and significant property damage.
events.name: Yellow Vests Movement Protests

events.enhanced_description: On December 1, 2018, the Oulu Police informed the public about a significant case of child sexual exploitation that had emerged in the city. This incident highlighted growing concerns regarding child safety and exploitation in Finland.
events.name: Oulu Child Sexual Exploitation Case

events.enhanced_description: On December 3, 2018, NASA reported the arrival of the OSIRIS-REx probe at the asteroid Bennu. This mission is the agency's first sample-return mission to an asteroid, aiming to collect and return samples to Earth.
events.name: OSIRIS-REx Arrival at Bennu

events.enhanced_description: On December 4, 2018, Spain entered into an institutional crisis surrounding the General Council of the Judiciary (CGPJ). This crisis raised concerns about judicial independence and governance in the country.
events.name: Spanish Institutional Crisis

events.enhanced_description: On December 7, 2018, the U.N.'s International Telecommunication Union reported that over half of the world's population, specifically 51.2 percent, were using the Internet by the end of 2018. This milestone reflects the rapid growth of digital connectivity worldwide.
events.name: Global Internet Usage Report

events.enhanced_description: On December 9, 2018, parliamentary elections were held in Armenia, marking a significant moment in the country's political landscape following the Velvet Revolution earlier that year. The elections were seen as a test of the new government's legitimacy.
events.name: Armenian Parliamentary Elections

events.enhanced_description: On December 15, 2018, nearly 200 nations convened at the Katowice Climate Change Conference, agreeing on rules to implement the 2015 Paris Agreement. This conference was crucial in advancing global efforts to combat climate change.
events.name: Katowice Climate Change Conference

events.enhanced_description: On December 17, 2018, Scandinavian tourists Louisa Vesterager Jespersen and Maren Ueland were murdered by Islamic terrorists in the foothills of Mount Toubkal near Imlil, Morocco. The brutal nature of the crime, including video evidence, shocked the international community.
events.name: Murder of Scandinavian Tourists in Morocco

events.enhanced_description: On December 19, 2018, Gatwick Airport in England experienced major disruption due to reports of drone sightings near the runway. The incident affected approximately 140,000 passengers and 1,000 flights, marking one of the largest disruptions in recent aviation history.

image.caption: Aerial view of Gatwick Airport’s north terminal, pier 6, and connecting sky bridge.
image.date_qualification: A 2012 aerial view of the airport site, not a photograph of the 2018 drone incident.
image.rights_statement: LicenseShortName: CC BY 2.0; UsageTerms: Creative Commons Attribution 2.0; Copyrighted: True

events.name: Gatwick Airport Drone Incident

events.enhanced_description: On December 20, 2018, in the Sea of Japan, the South Korean warship ROKS Gwanggaeto the Great targeted a Japanese P-1 maritime patrol airplane with its fire control radar. This incident escalated tensions between South Korea and Japan amid ongoing disputes.
events.name: ROKS Gwanggaeto the Great Incident

events.enhanced_description: On December 21, 2018, the Dow Jones Industrial Average closed at 22,445 after experiencing its worst week since 2008. This decline raised concerns about the stability of the financial markets and the economy.
events.name: Dow Jones Industrial Average Decline

events.enhanced_description: On December 22, 2018, an eruption from Krakatoa caused a tsunami that struck the Sunda Strait in Indonesia, resulting in at least 430 fatalities and nearly 1,500 injuries. The disaster highlighted the ongoing volcanic activity in the region.
events.name: Krakatoa Tsunami

events.enhanced_description: The second government shutdown of the United States, which began on December 22, 2018, was primarily due to a dispute over funding for the U.S.-Mexico border wall. This shutdown lasted for 35 days, making it the longest in U.S. history, and ended on January 25, 2019.
events.name: The United States government enters a second government shutdown

events.enhanced_description: On December 24, 2018, Burundi officially moved its capital from Bujumbura to Gitega. This decision was part of a broader effort to promote development in the interior of the country.
events.name: Burundi Capital Relocation

events.enhanced_description: On December 26, 2018, the Dow Jones Industrial Average recorded its largest ever one-day point gain, rising by 1,086 points. This rebound followed a period of significant market volatility.
events.name: Dow Jones One-Day Gain

events.enhanced_description: On December 31, 2018, an apartment block in Magnitogorsk, Chelyabinsk Oblast, Russia, partially collapsed, resulting in 39 deaths and 17 injuries. The official investigation attributed the collapse to a gas explosion.

image.caption: Rubble removal at the collapsed apartment block in Magnitogorsk.
image.credit: Вячеслав Мальцев — YouTube : https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VZ76AwrCKmY – View/save archived versions on archive.org
image.date_qualification: The described scene is dated 2 January 2019, two days after the 31 December 2018 collapse; the supplied image_date gives only the year 2019.
image.rights_statement: LicenseShortName: CC BY 3.0; UsageTerms: Creative Commons Attribution 3.0; Copyrighted: True

events.name: Magnitogorsk Building Collapse

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2019, NASA's New Horizons spacecraft made a historic close approach to the Kuiper belt object 486958 Arrokoth, providing unprecedented data about this distant celestial body. This flyby occurred approximately 4 billion miles from Earth, revealing insights into the early solar system.

image.caption: Transparent illustration of the New Horizons spacecraft.
image.credit: National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) , Applied Physics Laboratory — " PEPSSI Instrument Tastes Pluto's Atmosphere " from the Applied Physics Laboratory New Horizons website.
image.date_qualification: The image is dated 2015-07-03, not the 2019 flyby date.
image.rights_statement: LicenseShortName: Public domain; UsageTerms: Public domain; Copyrighted: False

events.name: New Horizons makes a close approach to the Kuiper belt object (KBO) 486958 Arrokoth

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2019, Jair Bolsonaro was inaugurated as the President of Brazil, marking the beginning of his four-year term. His presidency has been characterized by controversial policies and a shift towards right-wing governance.
events.name: Jair Bolsonaro begins his term as President of Brazil

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2019, Qatar announced its withdrawal from the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC), signaling a shift in its energy policy and focus on natural gas production. This decision was part of Qatar's strategy to enhance its global energy market position.
events.name: Qatar withdraws from OPEC

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2019, works published by authors who died in 1948 entered the public domain in many countries, including the United States. This marked a significant moment in copyright law, allowing greater access to literary works.
events.name: Works published by authors who died in 1948 enter the public domain

events.enhanced_description: In 2019, fossil fragments discovered in Callao Cave in the Philippines revealed the existence of a new species of human, named Homo luzonensis. This discovery provided significant insights into human evolution and migration in Southeast Asia.
events.name: Fossil Discovery of Homo luzonensis

events.enhanced_description: In April 2019, amid widespread protests, Sudanese President Omar al-Bashir was deposed in a coup d'état after nearly 30 years in power. This event marked a significant turning point in Sudan's political landscape and led to calls for democratic reforms.
events.name: Omar al-Bashir Deposed

events.enhanced_description: In early 2019, Venezuelan opposition leader Juan Guaidó led an attempted uprising against President Nicolás Maduro amid a severe political crisis. This event highlighted the ongoing struggle for power and governance in Venezuela.
events.name: Venezuelan Presidential Crisis

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2019, Russian President Vladimir Putin signed into law a controversial 'sovereign internet' bill aimed at enhancing government control over internet traffic within Russia. This legislation raised concerns about censorship and the potential for increased surveillance.
events.name: Putin signs sovereign internet bill

events.enhanced_description: In early 2019, the Syrian Army launched a major ground offensive against one of the last rebel strongholds in the country, specifically targeting the Idlib region. This offensive was part of the ongoing Syrian civil war, which has resulted in significant humanitarian crises.
events.name: Syrian Army offensive

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2019, a violent prison riot in Acarigua, Venezuela, resulted in the deaths of 29 prisoners and injuries to 19 guards. The incident highlighted the severe issues of overcrowding and violence within the Venezuelan prison system.
events.name: Acarigua prison riot

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2019, Japan resumed commercial whaling after a 30-year moratorium, following its withdrawal from the International Whaling Commission. This controversial decision sparked international criticism and raised concerns about the conservation of whale populations.
events.name: Japan resumes commercial whaling

events.enhanced_description: In 2019, Japan announced restrictions on high-tech exports to South Korea, marking the beginning of a trade dispute between the two countries. This move was seen as a response to historical grievances and escalated tensions in East Asia.

image.caption: U.S. Secretary of State Michael R. Pompeo participates in a U.S.-Japan-Republic of Korea trilateral meeting in Bangkok.
image.credit: U.S. Department of State from United States — Secretary Pompeo Participates in U.S.-Japan-Republic of Korea Trilateral Meeting
image.date_qualification: A contemporaneous diplomatic meeting related to Japan–South Korea relations, not a depiction of Japan announcing export restrictions.

events.name: Japan tightens high-tech exports to South Korea

events.enhanced_description: In 2019, the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) confirmed that Iran had breached the limit on its stockpile of enriched uranium, raising concerns about the country's nuclear program and compliance with international agreements. This development heightened tensions between Iran and Western nations.
events.name: IAEA confirms Iran's uranium breach

events.enhanced_description: During the annual July 1 protests in 2019, marking the anniversary of Hong Kong's handover to China, a group of protesters stormed the Legislative Council, vandalizing portraits and furniture before being dispersed by police. This event marked a significant escalation in the ongoing protests against perceived encroachments on Hong Kong's autonomy.
events.name: 2019–2020 Hong Kong protests

events.enhanced_description: In 2019, a fire on the Russian deep-diving submarine Losharik resulted in the deaths of 14 crew members, including submarine commander Denis Dolonsky. The incident raised concerns about safety protocols in the Russian Navy and the operational risks associated with deep-sea missions.
events.name: Losharik submarine fire

events.enhanced_description: In 2019, the World Health Organization (WHO) declared the Kivu Ebola epidemic a public health emergency of international concern, highlighting the severity of the outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. This declaration aimed to mobilize international resources and support to combat the epidemic.
events.name: WHO declares Kivu Ebola epidemic emergency

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2019, the United States officially withdrew from the Intermediate-Range Nuclear Forces Treaty, a landmark arms control agreement established with Russia in 1987. This withdrawal marked a significant shift in U.S.-Russia relations and raised concerns about a new arms race.
events.name: U.S. withdrawal from INF Treaty

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2019, Japan announced the removal of South Korea from its list of most trusted trading partners, a move that escalated tensions in the ongoing trade dispute between the two nations. This decision had significant implications for trade relations in the region.
events.name: Japan–South Korea trade dispute

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2019, Typhoon Lekima made landfall in Zhejiang, China, leading to the evacuation of over 1,000,000 people and resulting in numerous fatalities. The typhoon had previously caused severe flooding in the Philippines, showcasing the widespread impact of natural disasters in the region.
events.name: Typhoon Lekima

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2019, the Trump administration announced a delay in its proposal for 10 percent tariffs on certain consumer goods from China, while exempting other products. This decision came less than two weeks after the tariffs were initially proposed, reflecting ongoing negotiations and tensions in U.S.-China trade relations.
events.name: Trump administration tariff delay

events.enhanced_description: During the 2019–20 Hong Kong protests, a protester was shot in the chest with a live round of ammunition on January 1, 2019, leading to critical injuries. This incident intensified the already heightened tensions between protesters and law enforcement in the region.
events.name: Hong Kong protests shooting

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2019, the Nanfang'ao Bridge in Yilan County, Taiwan, collapsed, resulting in the deaths of six individuals and injuring over twenty others. This incident raised concerns about infrastructure safety in the region.
events.name: Nanfang'ao Bridge collapse

events.enhanced_description: In early October 2019, amid widespread protests, Ecuadorian President Lenín Moreno relocated the government to Guayaquil as protesters overtook the Carondelet Palace in Quito. The unrest was fueled by economic measures that were perceived as oppressive by the populace.
events.name: Ecuador protests government relocation

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2019, activists from Extinction Rebellion blocked the gates of Leinster House, the parliament of Ireland, to protest against government inaction on climate change. This action was part of a broader global movement advocating for urgent environmental reforms.
events.name: Extinction Rebellion protest in Ireland

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2019, Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan announced a military invasion of northeastern Syria, targeting the Syrian Democratic Forces (SDF) and other Kurdish militias. This announcement marked a significant escalation in Turkey's military involvement in the Syrian conflict.
events.name: Turkey's military invasion announcement

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2019, the United Nations Assistance Mission in Afghanistan and the U.N. Human Rights Office released a report stating that U.S. bombings in Nimroz and Farah Provinces, which resulted in the deaths of 39 civilians, were unlawful. The U.S. defended the attacks as targeting drug labs funding the Taliban.
events.name: UN report on US bombings in Afghanistan

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2019, a New York Times investigation revealed that Russian military aircraft had bombed at least 50 hospitals and clinics in opposition-held Idlib, Syria. This revelation highlighted the ongoing humanitarian crisis and the targeting of civilian infrastructure during the Syrian Civil War.
events.name: Russian bombing investigation in Idlib

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2019, riots erupted in Santiago, Chile, as civil unrest escalated in response to a series of economic measures and government declarations perceived as abusive by protesters. The unrest reflected widespread dissatisfaction with the socio-economic conditions in the country.
events.name: Santiago riots

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2019, the bodies of 39 individuals were discovered in a truck container in Essex, England. The incident raised serious concerns about human trafficking and the safety of migrants attempting to reach the UK.
events.name: Essex truck container tragedy

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2019, Google announced that its 53-qubit 'Sycamore' processor had achieved quantum supremacy, a significant milestone in quantum computing. This claim was met with skepticism from competitors, particularly IBM.
events.name: Google quantum supremacy announcement

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2019, Twitter announced a ban on all political advertising worldwide, a move aimed at combating misinformation and promoting transparency on its platform. This decision was part of a broader trend among social media companies to regulate political content.
events.name: Twitter political advertising ban

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2019, a 6.5 magnitude earthquake struck the island of Mindanao in the Philippines, occurring just two days after a previous quake had already left at least five people dead and around 12,000 homeless. The region faced significant challenges in recovery and relief efforts.
events.name: Mindanao earthquake

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2019, a train caught fire near Rahim Yar Khan, Pakistan, due to gas used by passengers for cooking on board. The blaze resulted in the tragic deaths of at least 74 individuals, highlighting safety concerns in the country's rail system.
events.name: Train fire in Pakistan

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2019, heavy rains and flooding in Beledweyne, Somalia, resulted in three deaths and left approximately 200,000 people homeless. The flooding also affected neighboring Kenya, where additional casualties and displacements were reported.
events.name: Flooding in Beledweyne, Somalia

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2019, Speaker of the U.S. House of Representatives Nancy Pelosi formally requested the House Judiciary Committee to initiate the drafting of articles of impeachment against President Donald Trump, marking a significant moment in U.S. political history.
events.name: Speaker of the U

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2019, the World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA) unanimously voted to impose a four-year ban on Russia from international sports due to widespread doping violations, which would exclude the country from major upcoming events including the 2020 Summer Olympics.
events.name: WADA bans Russia

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2019, a volcanic eruption occurred on White Island in New Zealand, resulting in the tragic deaths of 22 individuals and injuring 25 others, highlighting the dangers associated with active volcanic sites.

locations.name: Whakatāne, Bay of Plenty, New Zealand

events.name: White Island eruption

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2019, a Chilean Air Force C-130 transport aircraft tragically crashed while en route to Base Presidente Eduardo Frei Montalva in Antarctica, resulting in the loss of all 38 personnel on board.
events.name: Chilean military aircraft crash

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2019, Sanna Marin was appointed as the Prime Minister of Finland, making history as the youngest serving prime minister in the world at the age of 34, reflecting a significant shift in Finnish politics.
events.name: Sanna Marin becomes Prime Minister

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2019, the Democratic members of the U.S. House of Representatives announced formal charges against President Donald Trump, accusing him of abuse of power and obstruction of Congress, making him the third president in U.S. history to face impeachment.
events.name: Impeachment charges against Trump

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2019, the CHEOPS (CHaracterising ExOPlanet Satellite) space telescope was launched, designed to study the formation of extrasolar planets and to determine their precise characteristics, marking a significant advancement in astronomical research.
events.name: CHEOPS space telescope launch

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2019, the U.S. House of Representatives voted to approve two articles of impeachment against President Donald Trump, making him the third president in American history to be impeached, a pivotal moment in U.S. political history.
events.name: House approves impeachment articles

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2019, Libya's Government of National Accord activated a cooperation agreement with Turkey, paving the way for potential Turkish military intervention in the ongoing Second Libyan Civil War, a significant development in the region's geopolitical landscape.
events.name: Libya-Turkey cooperation accord

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2019, a severe locust plague devastated approximately 173,000 acres (70,000 hectares) of crop and grazing land across Ethiopia and Somalia, threatening food security in the region.
events.name: Locust plague in Ethiopia and Somalia

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2019, a Philippine court convicted Andal Ampatuan Jr., his brother Zaldy Ampatuan, and 31 others of 57 counts of murder, sentencing them to life imprisonment without parole for their involvement in the Maguindanao massacre, a landmark case in Philippine justice.
events.name: Ampatuan massacre convictions

events.enhanced_description: On December 20, 2019, the United States established the United States Space Force, a new branch of the armed forces dedicated to space warfare. This move marked a significant shift in military strategy and the importance of space in national defense.

locations.name: United States Capitol, Washington, D.C., United States

events.name: United States Space Force founded

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2019, the Dutch Supreme Court ruled that the government is responsible for managing carbon dioxide emissions and must protect human rights, reinforcing the legal framework for climate action in the Netherlands.
events.name: Dutch Supreme Court ruling on emissions

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2019, a court in Turkey sentenced five men to death and another three to 24 years in prison for their involvement in the murder of journalist Jamal Khashoggi at the Saudi consulate in Istanbul, a case that drew international attention.
events.name: Khashoggi murder convictions

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2019, a tragic bus accident occurred in South Sumatra, Indonesia, resulting in multiple fatalities and injuries as the vehicle plunged into a ravine, highlighting the dangers of road travel in the region.
events.name: Bus accident in South Sumatra

events.enhanced_description: On December 29, 2019, a report by the Multi-Sector Epidemic Response Committee indicated that 2,231 people had died in the ongoing Kivu Ebola epidemic in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. This epidemic highlighted the challenges of managing infectious diseases in the region.
events.name: Kivu Ebola epidemic report

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2019, the Taliban's ruling council agreed to a temporary cease-fire in Afghanistan, signaling a potential pathway to a peace agreement with the United States amidst ongoing conflict in the region.
events.name: Taliban cease-fire agreement

events.enhanced_description: On December 31, 2019, Iraqi militiamen and protesters breached the front gate of the United States embassy in Baghdad following a U.S. military operation targeting an Iraqi militia. This incident marked a significant escalation in tensions between the U.S. and Iranian-backed groups in Iraq.
events.name: US embassy breach in Baghdad

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2019, the Wuhan Municipal Health Commission reported the first official cases of 'viral pneumonia', which would later be identified as COVID-19, marking the beginning of a global pandemic.
events.name: COVID-19 pandemic reports

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2019, nearly five years after his abdication, King Juan Carlos I of Spain announced his retirement from public life. His departure marked the end of an era for the Spanish monarchy, which had undergone significant changes during his reign.
events.name: King Juan Carlos I retires from public life

events.enhanced_description: In January 2019, Sammarinese voters participated in the Marino referendum, which aimed to end discrimination based on sexual orientation and initiate a legislative initiative for electoral reform. This vote represented a significant step towards equality and modernization in San Marino.
events.name: Marino referendum in San Marino

events.enhanced_description: In January 2019, Mount Sinabung in Indonesia experienced a large explosive eruption, sending a 7,000-meter ash column into the air and generating a pyroclastic flow that traveled 3-3.5 kilometers. This eruption was part of the volcano's ongoing activity, which has affected local communities.
events.name: Mount Sinabung eruption

events.enhanced_description: In 2019, the Hong Kong government controversially declared that ongoing protests had 'turned into a riot.' This declaration was met with widespread criticism and further fueled tensions between protesters and authorities.
events.name: 2019 Hong Kong protest declared a riot

events.enhanced_description: In 2019, Human Rights Watch and Amnesty International issued reports condemning severe human rights violations in Chile amid widespread protests. These reports highlighted excessive police violence, including the use of non-lethal ammunition against protesters, leading to significant injuries.
events.name: 2019 Chilean protests

events.enhanced_description: On January 2, 2019, Adventist Health Systems announced its rebranding to AdventHealth, reflecting a commitment to a more holistic approach to health care. This change aimed to unify its various services under a single brand identity.

image.caption: The Mardian J. Blair Administrative Center, AdventHealth’s headquarters.
image.date_qualification: Headquarters site image dated 2011-12-01, before the 2019 rebranding; it depicts the organization’s site, not the rebranding event.

events.name: Adventist Health Systems rebrands to AdventHealth

events.enhanced_description: On January 3, 2019, China's Chang'e 4 spacecraft made history by becoming the first artificial object to successfully land on the far side of the Moon. This landmark achievement opened new avenues for lunar exploration and scientific research.
events.name: Chang'e 4 lands on the far side of the Moon

events.enhanced_description: On January 5, 2019, Bartholomew I of Constantinople issued a formal decree granting independence to the Orthodox Church of Ukraine from the Russian Orthodox Church. This significant move was a pivotal moment in the ongoing religious and political tensions between Ukraine and Russia.
events.name: Bartholomew I grants independence to the Orthodox Church of Ukraine

events.enhanced_description: On January 5, 2019, Pope Francis made a historic visit to Abu Dhabi, marking the first time a pope visited the Arabian Peninsula. This visit was significant for interfaith dialogue and aimed at promoting peace and understanding among different religions.

locations.name: Abu Dhabi, Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates

events.name: Pope Francis arrives in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates, becoming the first pope to visit the Arabian Peninsula

events.enhanced_description: On January 6, 2019, Muhammad V of Kelantan abdicated the federal throne of Malaysia, becoming the first Malaysian monarch to do so. His unexpected resignation sparked discussions about the future of the monarchy in Malaysia.
events.name: Muhammad V of Kelantan abdicates the throne

events.enhanced_description: On January 7, 2019, a faction of the Armed Forces of Gabon attempted a coup d'état against the government. This event highlighted the political instability in the country and raised concerns about the future of governance in Gabon.
events.name: Armed Forces of Gabon attempts a coup d'état

events.enhanced_description: On January 10, 2019, Venezuela entered a presidential crisis as Juan Guaidó and the National Assembly declared incumbent President Nicolás Maduro 'illegitimate.' This declaration marked the beginning of widespread protests and international attention on Venezuela's political turmoil.
events.name: Venezuela enters a presidential crisis

events.enhanced_description: On January 23, 2019, thousands of people protested in Venezuela in favor of disputed interim President Juan Guaidó. The protests turned violent, resulting in several deaths, and led President Maduro to sever diplomatic ties with the United States.
events.name: Protests in Venezuela in favor of Juan Guaidó

events.enhanced_description: On January 25, 2019, a mine tailings dam broke in Brumadinho, Brazil, resulting in a catastrophic disaster that killed at least 248 people and left 22 missing. This incident raised significant concerns about mining safety regulations in Brazil.
events.name: Brumadinho dam disaster

events.enhanced_description: On January 28, 2019, the U.S. Justice Department charged Chinese tech firm Huawei with multiple counts of fraud, escalating tensions between the United States and China. This legal action was part of a broader conflict over trade and technology.
events.name: U.S. Justice Department charges Huawei

events.enhanced_description: On February 1, 2019, U.S. President Donald Trump confirmed that the United States would withdraw from the Intermediate-Range Nuclear Forces Treaty of 1987, citing Russian non-compliance. This decision heightened tensions in U.S.-Russia relations.
events.name: U.S. confirms withdrawal from the INF Treaty

events.enhanced_description: On February 3, 2019, Pope Francis arrived in Abu Dhabi, becoming the first pope to visit the Arabian Peninsula. His visit aimed to promote interfaith dialogue and strengthen relations between the Catholic Church and the Muslim world.
events.name: Pope Francis visits Abu Dhabi

events.enhanced_description: In February 2019, Nayib Bukele was elected as the President of El Salvador, representing the Grand Alliance for National Unity (GANA). His election marked a significant shift in Salvadoran politics, ending a decade of two-party dominance.

locations.name: San Salvador, San Salvador, El Salvador

events.name: Presidential election: Nayib Bukele is elected president

events.enhanced_description: On February 6, 2019, Freedom House declared Hungary no longer a free country, marking it as the first country in the European Union to be labeled 'partly free.' This assessment raised concerns about the state of democracy in Hungary.
events.name: Freedom House declares Hungary partly free

events.enhanced_description: On February 7, 2019, anti-government protests demanding the resignation of Haitian President Jovenel Moïse began in several cities across Haiti. These protests were fueled by economic hardship and political dissatisfaction.
events.name: 2019 Haitian protests begin

events.enhanced_description: On February 12, 2019, the Republic of Macedonia officially renamed itself the Republic of North Macedonia, resolving a long-standing dispute with Greece. This change paved the way for North Macedonia's integration into NATO and the European Union.

image.caption: Officials sign the Prespa Agreement beside Lake Prespa.
