events.enhanced_description: On February 21, 2019, SpaceIL launched the Beresheet probe, marking the world's first privately financed mission to the Moon. This ambitious project aimed to land on the lunar surface and conduct scientific experiments.
events.name: SpaceIL launches Beresheet probe

events.enhanced_description: On February 23, 2019, amid attempts to send humanitarian aid to Venezuela from Colombia, President Nicolás Maduro severed diplomatic ties with Colombia. This decision escalated tensions in the region during the ongoing Venezuelan presidential crisis.
events.name: Venezuelan presidential crisis: Maduro severs ties with Colombia

events.enhanced_description: In early 2019, amid a humanitarian crisis, Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro severed diplomatic ties with Colombia as tensions escalated over the delivery of humanitarian aid. This decision was part of a broader political conflict regarding the legitimacy of Maduro's presidency.
events.name: Venezuelan presidential crisis: President Maduro severs diplomatic ties with Colombia amid attempts to send humanitarian aid to the country across the border

events.enhanced_description: In February 2019, Muhammadu Buhari was reelected as President of Nigeria, securing a second term amidst significant challenges including economic issues and security concerns. His party, the All Progressives Congress, also won a majority in the National Assembly.
events.name: General election: Incumbent president Muhammadu Buhari is reelected

events.enhanced_description: On February 24, 2019, Cuba held a constitutional referendum in which the new constitution was approved by 90.61% of valid votes. This marked a significant step in the country's political evolution under President Miguel Díaz-Canel.
events.name: 2019 Cuban constitutional referendum

events.enhanced_description: In February 2019, Moldova held parliamentary elections to fill all 101 seats in its legislature. The elections were marked by political tensions and were seen as crucial for the country's future direction.
events.name: Moldovan parliamentary election is held to elect all 101 members of the Parliament of Moldova

events.enhanced_description: In February 2019, Macky Sall was reelected as President of Senegal, winning a second term in an election that was closely watched for its fairness and transparency. His victory was seen as a continuation of his policies aimed at economic growth.
events.name: Presidential election: Incumbent president Macky Sall is reelected

events.enhanced_description: On February 26, 2019, the Indian Air Force conducted airstrikes on purported militant camps in Balakot, Pakistan. This military action was a response to a terrorist attack in India and marked the beginning of heightened tensions between India and Pakistan.
events.name: Indian Air Force launches airstrikes in Balakot, Pakistan

events.enhanced_description: On February 27, 2019, the second summit between U.S. President Donald Trump and North Korean leader Kim Jong Un was held in Hanoi, Vietnam. This meeting aimed to discuss denuclearization and improve diplomatic relations between the two countries.
events.name: 2019 North Korea–United States summit

events.enhanced_description: In March 2019, Maldives President Ibrahim Mohamed Solih appointed Mohamed Hameed CP as the new police service commissioner, a move aimed at reforming the police force and enhancing public safety.
events.name: Maldives President Ibrahim Mohamed Solih appoints Mohamed Hameed CP as police service commissioner

events.enhanced_description: On March 3, 2019, SpaceX successfully conducted an uncrewed demonstration flight of its Crew Dragon spacecraft, achieving autonomous docking with the International Space Station. This marked a significant milestone in NASA's Commercial Crew Program.
events.name: An uncrewed demonstration flight of the new crew capable version of the SpaceX Dragon spacecraft, intended to carry American astronauts into space, achieves successful autonomous docking with the International Space Station

events.enhanced_description: In March 2019, Estonia held parliamentary elections to elect all 101 members of the Riigikogu. The elections were characterized by a high voter turnout and were seen as a reflection of the public's engagement in the democratic process.
events.name: Estonian parliamentary election is held to elect all 101 members of the Riigikogu

events.enhanced_description: On March 5, 2019, researchers reported a second case of sustained remission from HIV, a decade after the first case known as the Berlin Patient. This case raised hopes for new treatments and a potential cure for HIV/AIDS.
events.name: A second case of sustained remission from HIV is reported, ten years after the Berlin Patient

events.enhanced_description: On March 6, 2019, Venezuela expelled German ambassador Daniel Kriener, accusing him of meddling in the country's internal affairs amid the ongoing presidential crisis. This incident highlighted the international tensions surrounding the political situation in Venezuela.
events.name: Venezuelan presidential crisis: Venezuela expels German ambassador Daniel Kriener for his alleged meddling in internal affairs

events.enhanced_description: On March 10, 2019, Ethiopian Airlines Flight 302, a Boeing 737 MAX 8, crashed shortly after takeoff from Addis Ababa, resulting in the deaths of all 157 people on board. This tragic event led to the grounding of all Boeing 737 MAX aircraft worldwide.
events.name: Ethiopian Airlines Flight 302 crash

events.enhanced_description: On March 15, 2019, Cyclone Idai made landfall in Mozambique, causing catastrophic flooding and power outages, leading to at least 1,073 fatalities. The cyclone severely impacted southern Africa, prompting international humanitarian responses.
events.name: Cyclone Idai makes landfall on Mozambique

events.enhanced_description: On March 15, 2019, terrorist attacks on two mosques in Christchurch, New Zealand, resulted in the deaths of 51 people and injuries to 50 others. This tragic event marked the deadliest mass shooting in New Zealand's history and sparked global condemnation.
events.name: Terrorist attacks on two mosques in Christchurch, New Zealand

events.enhanced_description: On March 19, 2019, Nursultan Nazarbayev announced his resignation as President of Kazakhstan after nearly 30 years in power. He appointed Kassym-Jomart Tokayev as acting president, marking a significant political transition in the country.
events.name: Nursultan Nazarbayev resigns as President of Kazakhstan

events.enhanced_description: On March 20, 2019, European antitrust regulators imposed a €1.49 billion fine on Google for anti-competitive practices in the online advertising market. This fine brought the total penalties against Google in the EU to nearly €8.76 billion.
events.name: Europe's antitrust regulators fine Google

events.enhanced_description: On March 23, 2019, the Syrian Democratic Forces announced the liberation of Al-Baghuz Fawqani, the last territory held by the Islamic State. This event marked a significant milestone in the fight against ISIS and the end of its territorial claims in Syria.

locations.name: Al-Baghuz Fawqani, Deir ez-Zor Governorate, Syria

events.name: The final territory of the Islamic State is liberated

events.enhanced_description: On March 24, 2019, Jakarta inaugurated the first phase of its Mass Rapid Transit (MRT) system, aimed at alleviating traffic congestion in the capital. This project represents a significant development in urban transportation in Indonesia.
events.name: The first phase of Jakarta's MRT system opened

events.enhanced_description: On March 26, 2019, the European Parliament voted 348 to 278 in favor of the EU Directive on Copyright in the Digital Single Market, which included controversial provisions like Article 13. This directive aimed to modernize copyright laws for the digital age.
events.name: The European Parliament votes in favour of the EU Directive on Copyright in the Digital Single Market

events.enhanced_description: On March 31, 2019, Taiwan scrambled its fighter aircraft in response to two Chinese jets crossing the maritime border. This incident underscored the ongoing tensions between Taiwan and China regarding airspace and territorial claims.
events.name: Taiwan scrambles its fighter aircraft after two Chinese jets crossed the maritime border

events.enhanced_description: On April 2, 2019, Abdelaziz Bouteflika resigned as President of Algeria after nearly two decades in power, following widespread protests against his rule. His resignation marked a significant turning point in Algerian politics.
events.name: Abdelaziz Bouteflika resigns as President of Algeria amid widespread protests

events.enhanced_description: On April 4, 2019, the Libyan National Army (LNA), led by General Khalifa Haftar, launched a surprise offensive towards the capital Tripoli, which was held by the Government of National Accord. This marked a significant escalation in the ongoing Second Libyan Civil War, as the LNA captured the strategic city of Gharyan.
events.name: Second Libyan Civil War: LNA Offensive

events.enhanced_description: On April 6, 2019, the Maldivian Democratic Party won a decisive victory in the parliamentary elections, securing 65 out of 85 seats in the People's Majlis. This election was a significant moment in Maldivian politics, reinforcing the party's influence following the election of President Ibrahim Mohamed Solih.
events.name: 2019 Maldivian parliamentary election

events.enhanced_description: On April 10, 2019, scientists from the Event Horizon Telescope project announced the first-ever image of a black hole, located in the center of the M87 galaxy. This groundbreaking achievement provided unprecedented visual evidence of black holes, confirming theories about their existence and properties.
events.name: First Image of a Black Hole

events.enhanced_description: On April 11, 2019, WikiLeaks co-founder Julian Assange was arrested by British police after spending seven years in the Ecuadorian embassy in London. His arrest marked a significant moment in the ongoing debate over press freedom and government transparency.
events.name: Julian Assange Arrested

events.enhanced_description: During Holy Week on April 15, 2019, a devastating fire engulfed Notre-Dame Cathedral in Paris, leading to the collapse of its roof and main spire. This tragic event sparked global concern for the preservation of cultural heritage and prompted discussions about restoration efforts.
events.name: Notre-Dame Cathedral Fire

events.enhanced_description: On April 16, 2019, a tragic avalanche at Howse Peak in Alberta claimed the lives of three renowned mountaineers: Austrians Hansjörg Auer and David Lama, and Canadian Jess Roskelley. Their deaths highlighted the dangers of high-altitude climbing and the risks faced by elite climbers.
events.name: Howse Peak Avalanche

events.enhanced_description: On April 18, 2019, NepaliSat-1 was launched, marking Nepal's first-ever research satellite sent into space. This milestone represented a significant advancement in Nepal's space capabilities and scientific research.
events.name: NepaliSat-1 Launch

events.enhanced_description: On April 21, 2019, a series of coordinated Islamist bomb attacks targeted eight locations in Sri Lanka, including three churches and four hotels, resulting in 259 deaths and over 500 injuries. This incident marked the deadliest terrorist attack in Sri Lanka since the end of the Civil War in 2009.
events.name: Sri Lanka Easter Bombings

events.enhanced_description: On April 25, 2019, North Korean leader Kim Jong Un visited Vladivostok, Russia, to hold a series of summits with Russian leaders, including President Vladimir Putin. This visit underscored the growing diplomatic ties between North Korea and Russia amidst ongoing tensions with the United States.
events.name: Kim Jong Un Visits Russia

events.enhanced_description: On April 28, 2019, explorer Victor Vescovo achieved the deepest dive in history, reaching Challenger Deep within the Mariana Trench at a depth of 10,928 meters (35,853 feet). This expedition contributed to our understanding of deep-sea environments and the challenges of extreme exploration.
events.name: Victor Vescovo's Deep Dive

events.enhanced_description: On April 29, 2019, Abu Bakr al-Baghdadi, the elusive leader of the Islamic State, appeared in undated footage released by the group, marking his first video appearance since 2014. This event reignited discussions about the status and influence of ISIS in the region.
events.name: Abu Bakr al-Baghdadi Video Appearance

events.enhanced_description: On April 30, 2019, Emperor Akihito of Japan abdicated from the throne, marking the first abdication by a Japanese monarch in nearly two centuries. This historic event ended the Heisei era and ushered in the Reiwa era with the ascension of his son, Naruhito, on May 1.
events.name: Emperor Akihito's Abdication

events.enhanced_description: On May 1, 2019, King Vajiralongkorn of Thailand married his personal bodyguard, Suthida Tidjai, in a surprise ceremony, elevating her to the status of queen consort. This event was notable for its unexpected nature and the implications for the Thai monarchy.
events.name: King Vajiralongkorn Marries

events.enhanced_description: On May 3, 2019, the number of deaths from the Kivu Ebola epidemic surpassed 1,000, marking it as the second deadliest Ebola outbreak in history, following the West African Ebola virus epidemic of 2013-2016. This outbreak raised significant concerns about public health and disease control in the region.

locations.name: Kivu, Democratic Republic of the Congo

events.name: Kivu Ebola Epidemic Deaths

events.enhanced_description: On May 3, 2019, the Gaza-Israel conflict escalated as the Israeli military launched airstrikes into Gaza, killing more than 20 Palestinians, including a pregnant woman and a toddler. This incident intensified the ongoing violence and tensions in the region.
events.name: Gaza–Israel Clashes

events.enhanced_description: On May 5, 2019, Aeroflot Flight 1492 crash-landed and burst into flames at Sheremetyevo International Airport in Moscow, resulting in the deaths of 41 of the 78 people on board. This tragic incident raised concerns about aviation safety and emergency response protocols.
events.name: Aeroflot Flight 1492 Crash

events.enhanced_description: On May 6, 2019, the Intergovernmental Science-Policy Platform on Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services (IPBES) released a report warning that biodiversity loss is accelerating, with over a million species threatened with extinction. The report highlighted the unprecedented decline of the natural world, largely attributed to human activities.
events.name: IPBES Biodiversity Report

events.enhanced_description: On May 8, 2019, Isabelle Holdaway, a 17-year-old British teenager, became the first patient to receive genetically modified phage therapy to combat a drug-resistant infection. This groundbreaking treatment represents a significant advancement in the fight against antibiotic-resistant bacteria.
events.name: First genetically modified phage therapy

events.enhanced_description: On May 10, 2019, the United States implemented a 25% tariff increase on $200 billion worth of Chinese imports, intensifying the ongoing trade war between the two nations. This move was part of broader negotiations aimed at addressing trade imbalances and intellectual property theft.
events.name: U.S. tariff hike on Chinese imports

events.enhanced_description: On May 12, 2019, four commercial ships, including two Saudi Aramco oil tankers, were damaged near Fujairah in the Gulf of Oman. The UAE labeled the incident a 'sabotage attack,' while the U.S. pointed fingers at Iran amid rising tensions in the region.
events.name: May 2019 Gulf of Oman incident

events.enhanced_description: On May 13, 2019, Swedish prosecutors announced the reopening of a rape allegation investigation against Julian Assange. This decision came as they expressed intentions to seek his extradition from the UK after he completed a prison sentence for skipping bail.
events.name: Reopening of Assange investigation

events.enhanced_description: On May 14, 2019, the Eurovision Song Contest took place in Tel Aviv, Israel, where Dutch singer Duncan Laurence won with his song 'Arcade.' This annual event showcases musical talent from various countries, drawing significant international attention.

locations.name: Tel Aviv, Tel Aviv District, Israel

events.name: Eurovision Song Contest 2019

events.enhanced_description: On May 17, 2019, Taiwan's parliament made history by becoming the first in Asia to legalize same-sex marriage. This landmark decision marked a significant step forward for LGBTQ+ rights in the region.
events.name: Taiwan legalizes same-sex marriage

events.enhanced_description: On May 18, 2019, the Australian federal election resulted in a narrow victory for Scott Morrison's Liberal/National Coalition government, defeating the Labor Party led by Bill Shorten. This election was notable for its unexpected outcome, defying many pre-election polls.
events.name: 2019 Australian federal election

events.enhanced_description: On May 19, 2019, Google announced it would cease Android update support for Huawei devices, including the Google Play Store and Gmail apps, following the company's blacklisting by the U.S. government. This decision had significant implications for Huawei's operations and its global market presence.
events.name: Google pulls support for Huawei

events.enhanced_description: On May 20, 2019, the revision of the International System of Units (SI) took effect, which was adopted by the majority of countries worldwide. This update aimed to enhance the precision and consistency of measurements across various scientific disciplines.
events.name: Revision of the SI system of measurement

events.enhanced_description: On May 23, 2019, the Indian general election concluded with Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) securing a landslide victory, winning 303 of the 543 parliamentary seats. This election reaffirmed Modi's leadership and the BJP's dominance in Indian politics.
events.name: 2019 Indian general election

events.enhanced_description: On May 24, 2019, British Prime Minister Theresa May announced her resignation as leader of the Conservative Party, effective June 7, 2019. Her decision followed significant pressure from party members and public dissatisfaction regarding her handling of Brexit.
events.name: Theresa May announces resignation

events.enhanced_description: On May 26, 2019, a series of riots in four different prisons in Amazonas, Brazil, resulted in the deaths of more than 50 prisoners. These violent outbreaks highlighted ongoing issues related to overcrowding and gang violence within the Brazilian prison system.
events.name: Amazonas prison massacres

events.enhanced_description: On May 27, 2019, U.S. President Donald Trump made an official state visit to Japan, becoming the first foreign leader to meet with Emperor Naruhito. This visit underscored the strong diplomatic ties between the United States and Japan.
events.name: Trump meets Emperor Naruhito

events.enhanced_description: On May 30, 2019, the 2019 Cricket World Cup commenced in England, featuring one match in Wales. England ultimately triumphed over New Zealand in the final, marking a significant achievement in the history of English cricket.

image.caption: Map showing 2019 Cricket World Cup participating nations and their qualification routes.
image.date_qualification: Created 21 August 2018, before the tournament; this is a map of participating nations, not a depiction of a match.
image.rights_statement: LicenseShortName: CC BY-SA 4.0; UsageTerms: Creative Commons Attribution-Share Alike 4.0; Copyrighted: True

events.name: 2019 Cricket World Cup

events.enhanced_description: On June 1, 2019, Liverpool F.C. secured their sixth UEFA Champions League title by defeating Tottenham Hotspur 2-0 at the Metropolitano Stadium in Madrid. Goals from Mohamed Salah and Divock Origi sealed the victory for the English club.
events.name: Liverpool F.C. wins UEFA Champions League

events.enhanced_description: On June 2, 2019, nearly five years after his abdication, King Juan Carlos I of Spain announced his retirement from public life. His departure marked the end of an era for the Spanish monarchy, which had undergone significant changes during his reign.
events.name: King Juan Carlos I retires

events.enhanced_description: On June 3, 2019, the Khartoum massacre occurred when Sudanese troops and Janjaweed militiamen violently stormed a protest camp outside military headquarters, resulting in the deaths of over 100 people. This brutal crackdown was part of the broader struggle for democracy in Sudan.
events.name: Khartoum massacre

events.enhanced_description: On June 3, 2019, U.S. President Donald Trump made a state visit to the United Kingdom, where he met with Queen Elizabeth II and outgoing Prime Minister Theresa May. This visit marked the first official state visit by a sitting U.S. president to the U.K. since 2011.
events.name: Trump's state visit to the U.K.

events.enhanced_description: On June 5, 2019, Chinese President Xi Jinping made a state visit to Russia, where he attended the St. Petersburg International Economic Forum. This visit underscored the strengthening ties between China and Russia amid global geopolitical shifts.
events.name: Xi Jinping's state visit to Russia

events.enhanced_description: In response to the Khartoum massacre during the Sudanese revolution, the African Union suspended Sudan's membership, highlighting the international community's condemnation of the violence against protesters. This action aimed to pressure the Sudanese military to restore civilian rule and address human rights violations.
events.name: Sudanese revolution: The African Union suspends Sudan's membership

events.enhanced_description: On June 7, 2019, Theresa May announced her resignation as leader of the Conservative Party following a tumultuous tenure marked by challenges in delivering Brexit. Her departure opened the door for a leadership contest that would eventually lead to Boris Johnson becoming Prime Minister.
events.name: Theresa May resigns as leader of the Conservative Party

events.enhanced_description: On June 11, 2019, Botswana's High Court ruled to decriminalize homosexuality, a landmark decision that marked a significant step forward for LGBTQ+ rights in the country. The ruling was celebrated by activists as a victory against colonial-era laws that criminalized same-sex relationships.
events.name: Botswana decriminalizes homosexuality

events.enhanced_description: On June 12, 2019, the Supreme Court of Ecuador ruled in favor of same-sex marriage, making it legal throughout the country. This decision was hailed as a significant advancement for LGBTQ+ rights in Ecuador and marked a shift towards greater acceptance and equality.
events.name: Ecuador legalizes same-sex marriage

events.enhanced_description: On June 13, 2019, two oil tankers were attacked near the Strait of Hormuz amid rising tensions between Iran and the United States. The U.S. government blamed Iran for the attacks, which heightened fears of a potential military confrontation in the region.

locations.name: Strait of Hormuz, Hormozgan Province, Iran

events.name: June 2019 Gulf of Oman incident

events.enhanced_description: On June 15, 2019, the Hong Kong government announced the indefinite suspension of the controversial extradition bill, but protests continued as demonstrators demanded the complete withdrawal of the bill and the resignation of Chief Executive Carrie Lam.
events.name: Hong Kong protests continue

events.enhanced_description: On June 16, 2019, a massive power outage affected nearly 50 million people across Argentina, Uruguay, and parts of Paraguay. The outage was attributed to a failure in the electrical grid, causing widespread disruption and highlighting vulnerabilities in the region's infrastructure.
events.name: Large-scale power outage in South America

events.enhanced_description: On June 17, 2019, a triple suicide bombing in Borno, Nigeria, killed 30 people and injured over 40 at a hall where spectators were watching a football match. The attack was attributed to Boko Haram, a militant group known for its violent insurgency in the region.
events.name: Triple suicide blast in Nigeria

events.enhanced_description: On June 18, 2019, the United States announced the deployment of an additional 1,000 troops to the Middle East amid escalating tensions with Iran. This move was part of a broader strategy to deter Iranian aggression in the region.
events.name: U.S. troop deployment to the Middle East

events.enhanced_description: On June 19, 2019, four men were charged with the murder of the 298 passengers and crew of Malaysia Airlines Flight 17, which was shot down over Eastern Ukraine in July 2014. This development marked a significant step in seeking justice for the victims of the tragedy.

image.caption: Map showing the routes of Malaysia Airlines Flight 17 and Singapore Airlines Flight 351.

events.name: Charges in Malaysia Airlines Flight 17 incident

events.enhanced_description: On June 20, 2019, Chinese President Xi Jinping made a historic state visit to North Korea, marking his first trip to the country as president. This visit was significant as it was the first by a Chinese leader in 14 years, reflecting the close ties between the two nations.
events.name: Xi Jinping's state visit to North Korea

events.enhanced_description: On June 20, 2019, Iran shot down a U.S. RQ-4 Global Hawk surveillance drone over the Strait of Hormuz, claiming it had violated Iranian airspace. The U.S. contended that the drone was in international airspace, escalating tensions between the two nations.

image.caption: Remnants of a U.S. RQ-4 Global Hawk surveillance drone shot down by Iran.
image.date_qualification: Photographed the day after the June 20, 2019 shoot-down; this depicts wreckage, not the shoot-down itself.

locations.name: Strait of Hormuz, Hormozgan Province, Iran

events.name: Iran shoots down U.S. drone

events.enhanced_description: On June 22, 2019, a coup attempt in Ethiopia's Amhara Region resulted in the assassination of regional president Ambachew Mekonnen and national military chief of staff Se'are Mekonnen. This event highlighted ongoing political instability and ethnic tensions within the country.
events.name: Amhara Region coup attempt

events.enhanced_description: On June 30, 2019, during a historic trilateral meeting at Panmunjom, U.S. President Donald Trump became the first sitting president to cross into North Korea. This unprecedented moment symbolized a potential thaw in relations and a commitment to restart denuclearization negotiations.
events.name: Trilateral meeting at Panmunjom

events.enhanced_description: In July 2019, the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) reported that July 2019 was the hottest month on record globally, with temperatures 0.95°C (1.71°F) above the 20th-century average. This report underscored the ongoing impacts of climate change and rising global temperatures.
events.name: NOAA reports hottest month on record

events.enhanced_description: On July 2, 2019, a total solar eclipse occurred over parts of South America, captivating millions of viewers. This astronomical event was the 58th solar eclipse from Saros cycle 127 and provided a unique opportunity for scientific observation and public engagement.
events.name: Total solar eclipse over South America

events.enhanced_description: On July 3, 2019, an airstrike conducted by the Libyan National Army, led by Field Marshal Khalifa Haftar, targeted the Tajoura Detention Center near Tripoli, resulting in the deaths of at least 53 migrants and injuring 130 others. This tragic event highlighted the ongoing conflict in Libya and the dire conditions faced by migrants in detention centers.
events.name: 2019 Tajoura migrant center airstrike

events.enhanced_description: On July 7, 2019, the New Democracy party, led by Kyriakos Mitsotakis, won a decisive victory in the Greek legislative election, securing 158 out of 300 seats in the Hellenic Parliament. This election marked a significant shift in Greek politics, ending the four-year rule of the leftist Syriza party.
events.name: 2019 Greek legislative election

events.enhanced_description: On July 7, 2019, the United States Women's National Soccer Team won the FIFA Women's World Cup held in France, defeating the Netherlands 2-0 in the final. This victory marked the team's fourth World Cup title, further solidifying their dominance in women's soccer.
figures: United States Women's National Soccer Team
events.name: 2019 FIFA Women's World Cup

events.enhanced_description: On July 10, 2019, the last Volkswagen Beetle rolled off the production line at the Volkswagen Puebla Plant in Mexico, marking the end of an era for the iconic car that had been in production for over 70 years. The final model was a 'Special Edition' and is set to be displayed in a museum, symbolizing the car's cultural significance.
events.name: Last Volkswagen Beetle rolls off the line

events.enhanced_description: On July 12, 2019, a coordinated car bomb and gun attack on the Asasey Hotel in Kismayo, Somalia, resulted in the deaths of at least 26 people, including two prominent journalists and nine foreign nationals. The Islamist group al-Shabaab claimed responsibility for the attack, which underscored the ongoing violence in the region.
events.name: Asasey Hotel attack

events.enhanced_description: On July 13, 2019, Hurricane Barry made landfall along the Gulf Coast, causing significant damage estimated at over $500 million and resulting in one fatality. The storm brought heavy rainfall and flooding, impacting several states, particularly Louisiana.
events.name: Hurricane Barry strikes the Gulf Coast

events.enhanced_description: On July 16, 2019, Ursula von der Leyen was elected as the first female President of the European Commission by the European Parliament, succeeding Jean-Claude Juncker. Her election marked a historic moment in EU politics, as she took on the role of leading the executive branch of the European Union.
events.name: Ursula von der Leyen elected President of the European Commission

events.enhanced_description: On July 17, 2019, Joaquín 'El Chapo' Guzmán, the notorious former leader of the Sinaloa Cartel, was sentenced to life in prison plus 30 years by a U.S. federal court. His conviction marked a significant victory in the fight against drug trafficking and organized crime in the United States.
events.name: United States v. Guzmán sentencing

events.enhanced_description: On July 18, 2019, an arson attack at Kyoto Animation Studio resulted in the deaths of 36 people and injuries to more than 30 others. This incident became one of the deadliest mass killings in Japan since World War II, shocking the nation and the global animation community.
events.name: Kyoto Animation arson attack

events.enhanced_description: On July 19, 2019, the Iranian Navy captured the British tanker Stena Impero and temporarily seized another vessel, the Mesdar, in the Persian Gulf. British Foreign Secretary Jeremy Hunt warned of 'serious consequences' if Iran did not release the tankers, escalating tensions between the UK and Iran.
events.name: Stena Impero seizure by Iranian Navy

events.enhanced_description: On July 21, 2019, a mob of over 100 suspected triad members attacked commuters at Yuen Long MTR station in Hong Kong, injuring 45 individuals, including a pro-democracy legislator and a pregnant woman. The incident raised serious concerns about police inaction and the safety of citizens amid ongoing protests.
events.name: Yuen Long MTR station attack

events.enhanced_description: On July 24, 2019, Boris Johnson was appointed Prime Minister of the United Kingdom after winning the Conservative Party leadership contest against Jeremy Hunt, succeeding Theresa May. His leadership marked a pivotal moment in UK politics, particularly regarding Brexit negotiations.
events.name: Boris Johnson becomes Prime Minister

events.enhanced_description: On July 26, 2019, the 2019 Pan American Games were officially opened in Lima, Peru, featuring athletes from across the Americas competing in various sports. This multi-sport event showcased regional talent and fostered unity among participating nations.

image.caption: Skyline of Lima, Peru.
image.date_qualification: Photographed September 13, 2013, before the 2019 Pan American Games; not an event photograph.
image.rights_statement: LicenseShortName: CC BY 2.0; UsageTerms: Creative Commons Attribution 2.0; Copyrighted: True

events.name: 2019 Pan American Games

events.enhanced_description: On July 30, 2019, India enacted a law banning the practice of triple talaq, a form of instant divorce in Islamic law, marking a significant step towards gender equality and women's rights in the country. The law aimed to protect Muslim women from arbitrary divorce.
events.name: India bans triple talaq

events.enhanced_description: On August 1, 2019, Danish polar research institution Polar Portal reported a significant spike in ice loss in Greenland, with 11 billion tons melting in a single day and a total of 197 gigatonnes during the month of July. This alarming data underscored the impacts of climate change on polar regions.
events.name: Greenland ice loss report

events.enhanced_description: On August 2, 2019, the United States officially withdrew from the Intermediate-Range Nuclear Forces Treaty, a landmark arms control agreement established with Russia in 1987. This withdrawal raised concerns about a new arms race and the future of nuclear disarmament efforts.
events.name: US withdraws from INF Treaty

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2019, the Indian government revoked the special status of Jammu and Kashmir, a move that was unprecedented and sparked widespread controversy and unrest in the region. This decision altered the constitutional framework governing the area and raised tensions between India and Pakistan.
events.name: Revocation of Jammu and Kashmir's special status

events.enhanced_description: On August 7, 2019, the Singapore Mediation Convention, also known as the UN Convention on International Settlement Agreements Resulting from Mediation, came into effect. This treaty requires ratifying states to enforce international commercial agreements in their courts, promoting mediation as a means of dispute resolution.
events.name: Singapore Mediation Convention comes into effect

events.enhanced_description: On August 8, 2019, reports indicated a possible nuclear explosion at the Nyonoksa weapons-testing site in Arkhangelsk Oblast, Russia, resulting in at least five fatalities and three injuries. The incident raised alarms about nuclear safety and the risks associated with military testing.
events.name: Nyonoksa radiation accident

events.enhanced_description: On August 10, 2019, a fuel tanker truck exploded in Morogoro, Tanzania, resulting in the tragic deaths of at least 89 individuals and injuring many others. The explosion occurred as people attempted to siphon fuel from the overturned tanker, highlighting the dangers associated with fuel transportation in the region.
events.name: Morogoro tanker explosion

events.enhanced_description: In August 2019, a series of wildfires broke out across the Canary Islands, particularly affecting Gran Canaria, Tenerife, and Lanzarote. The fires on Gran Canaria were especially severe, leading to extensive evacuations and significant damage to the island's forests.
events.name: 2019 Canary Islands wildfires

events.enhanced_description: On August 11, 2019, monsoon-related floods in India resulted in the deaths of at least 114 people, with the states of Kerala, Karnataka, and Maharashtra being the most affected. The floods were part of a larger pattern of severe weather that impacted the region, leading to widespread devastation and displacement.
events.name: 2019 Indian floods

events.enhanced_description: On August 12, 2019, Hong Kong International Airport was closed due to ongoing protests against the government, marking a significant escalation in the pro-democracy movement. The protests were characterized by widespread demonstrations and civil disobedience, reflecting deep-seated grievances among the population.

locations.name: Hong Kong International Airport, Hong Kong

events.name: 2019–20 Hong Kong protests

events.enhanced_description: On August 13, 2019, the yield curve for U.S. Treasury bonds inverted, with the yield rate for 2-year bonds surpassing that of 10-year bonds. This inversion is often seen as a predictor of economic recession, raising concerns among investors and economists alike.
events.name: U.S. yield curve inversion

events.enhanced_description: On August 14, 2019, the Dow Jones Industrial Average experienced a significant drop of over 500 points, driven by investor fears stemming from the recent yield curve inversion. This plunge reflected growing concerns about the potential for an economic downturn.
events.name: Dow Jones plunge

events.enhanced_description: On August 15, 2019, the European Central Bank announced the closure of PNB Banka, previously known as Norvik Banka, after determining that it had become insolvent. This decision marked a significant event in Latvia's banking sector, which had faced scrutiny from financial authorities.
events.name: PNB Banka insolvency

events.enhanced_description: On August 16, 2019, a Russian airstrike targeted the Hass refugee camp in Syria, resulting in the deaths of 20 civilians. This incident underscored the ongoing humanitarian crisis and the impact of military actions on civilian populations in conflict zones.
events.name: Russian airstrike in Hass

events.enhanced_description: On August 18, 2019, a symbolic funeral was held for Okjökull glacier in Iceland, which had completely melted after once covering 15.5 km². This event was attended by activists and officials, highlighting the impacts of climate change on glaciers worldwide.
events.name: Funeral for Okjökull glacier

events.enhanced_description: On August 19, 2019, protests erupted across Indonesian Papua in response to the arrest of Papuan students in Surabaya for allegedly disrespecting the Indonesian flag. The protests turned violent in several cities, marking a significant moment of civil unrest over issues of racial and ethnic discrimination.
events.name: 2019 Papua protests

events.enhanced_description: On August 21, 2019, Brazil's National Institute for Space Research reported that wildfires in the Amazon rainforest were burning at a record rate, with over 36,000 fires recorded that year. The smoke from these fires reached as far as São Paulo, raising international concerns about environmental degradation.
events.name: 2019 Amazon rainforest wildfires

events.enhanced_description: On August 23, 2019, German Chancellor Angela Merkel and French President Emmanuel Macron declared the widespread Amazon fires an international emergency, urging that the issue be addressed at the upcoming G7 summit. This statement highlighted the global significance of the environmental crisis in the Amazon.
events.name: Amazon fires as international emergency

events.enhanced_description: On August 25, 2019, two Israeli drones attacked Beirut, Lebanon, marking the first such incident between Israel and Lebanon since the 2006 Lebanon War. One drone crashed into the Hezbollah Media Center, while the second exploded in the air, causing damage to the building.
events.name: 2019 Beirut drone crash

events.enhanced_description: On August 31, 2019, a sightseeing helicopter crashed in the mountains of Skoddevarre in Alta Municipality, Norway, resulting in the tragic deaths of all six occupants. The incident raised concerns about aviation safety in the region.
events.name: 2019 Alta helicopter crash

events.enhanced_description: Hurricane Dorian made landfall on Grand Bahama, Bahamas, as the strongest hurricane ever recorded in the Atlantic basin outside the Caribbean and Gulf of Mexico, with sustained wind speeds reaching 185 mph. The storm caused catastrophic damage, leading to at least 43 confirmed deaths and widespread destruction.
events.name: Hurricane Dorian makes landfall

events.enhanced_description: The MV Conception, a dive boat, caught fire and sank near Santa Cruz Island, California, resulting in the deaths of 34 people. This incident marked the worst maritime disaster in California in over 150 years.
events.name: Sinking of MV Conception

events.enhanced_description: Hong Kong Chief Executive Carrie Lam announced the official withdrawal of the controversial Fugitive Offenders and Mutual Legal Assistance in Criminal Matters Legislation (Amendment) Bill 2019 amid ongoing protests. This decision was part of a broader response to public discontent regarding social and economic inequalities.
events.name: Withdrawal of Fugitive Offenders Bill

events.enhanced_description: India's Chandrayaan-2 mission successfully placed its orbiter in lunar orbit, marking a significant achievement in space exploration. However, the lander Vikram tragically crashed on the Moon's surface during its descent.
events.name: Chandrayaan-2 lunar probe

events.enhanced_description: U.S. President Donald Trump announced the cancellation of planned peace talks with the Taliban at Camp David following their claimed responsibility for bombings in Kabul that resulted in the death of a U.S. soldier. This decision highlighted the complexities of the Afghan peace process.
events.name: Cancellation of Taliban peace talks

events.enhanced_description: The Parliament of the United Kingdom was prorogued amid unprecedented protests from opposition MPs, who displayed signs in the House of Commons and resisted backing the shutdown. This event sparked significant political controversy and public outcry.
events.name: Prorogation of the UK Parliament

events.enhanced_description: Astronomers announced the groundbreaking detection of water in the atmosphere of exoplanet K2-18b, marking the first such discovery for an exoplanet located in the habitable zone around a star. This finding has significant implications for the search for extraterrestrial life.
events.name: Detection of water on exoplanet K2-18b

events.enhanced_description: Two Saudi Aramco oil refineries in Abqaiq and Khurais were attacked by drones, resulting in significant fires and disruptions to oil production. Houthi militants claimed responsibility for the attack, which impacted nearly half of Saudi Arabia's oil exports.
events.name: 2019 Abqaiq–Khurais attack

events.enhanced_description: A gas explosion occurred in Koltsovo, Novosibirsk Oblast, Russia, igniting a fire in a bioweapons plant that housed dangerous viruses, including smallpox and ebola. The incident raised significant concerns regarding biosecurity and safety protocols.
events.name: Gas explosion in Koltsovo

events.enhanced_description: Interest rates on repurchase agreements (repos) in the United States experienced a sudden and unexpected spike, causing concern among financial analysts and prompting discussions about the implications for the broader economy.
events.name: Spike in U.S. repo rates

events.enhanced_description: A U.S. drone attack in Nangarhar Province, Afghanistan, resulted in the deaths of 30 Afghan nut farmers and injuries to 40 others. This incident highlighted the ongoing complexities and tragic consequences of military operations in the region.
events.name: U.S. drone attack in Nangarhar

events.enhanced_description: An international climate strike and protest, led by young activists and adults, took place just days before the UN Climate Summit, demanding urgent action to address the climate crisis. The event mobilized 6 million people across 4,500 locations in 150 countries, marking one of the largest climate mobilizations in history.
events.name: Global climate strike

events.enhanced_description: In response to the September 14 attack on Saudi oil refineries, U.S. President Donald Trump approved the deployment of several hundred troops and military equipment to Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates. Both nations vowed to defend themselves against further threats.
events.name: U.S. troop deployment to Saudi Arabia

events.enhanced_description: Nearly three weeks after Hurricane Dorian made landfall, the official death toll rose to 52, with 1,300 individuals reported missing in the Bahamas. Rescuers faced the grim reality of widespread devastation and the stench of rotting bodies amid the rubble.
events.name: Death toll from Hurricane Dorian

events.enhanced_description: Thomas Cook, one of the oldest and largest travel firms, declared bankruptcy after last-minute rescue negotiations failed, leaving 600,000 tourists stranded worldwide. This event underscored the vulnerabilities in the travel industry.
events.name: Bankruptcy of Thomas Cook

events.enhanced_description: Thomas Cook, one of the oldest and largest travel firms in the world, declared bankruptcy after failing to secure last-minute rescue negotiations, leaving approximately 600,000 tourists stranded globally. This event marked a significant moment in the travel industry, highlighting the vulnerabilities of traditional travel agencies in the face of changing market dynamics.
events.name: Thomas Cook goes bankrupt

events.enhanced_description: In a significant political move, Russia formally adopted the Paris climate agreement, committing to international efforts to combat climate change. This decision was part of a broader global initiative to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and address environmental challenges.
events.name: Russia adopts the Paris climate agreement

events.enhanced_description: The Supreme Court of the United Kingdom unanimously ruled in the case of R (Miller) v The Prime Minister that the prorogation of Parliament in September 2019 was unlawful and void. This landmark decision had significant implications for the political landscape in the UK.

locations.historical_name: Supreme Court of the United Kingdom
locations.name: Supreme Court of the United Kingdom

events.name: UK Supreme Court ruling on prorogation

events.enhanced_description: The Supreme Court of the United Kingdom delivered a landmark ruling in the case of R (Miller) v The Prime Minister, declaring the prorogation of Parliament in September 2019 unlawful and void. This ruling underscored the court's role in upholding parliamentary sovereignty amidst the contentious Brexit debate.

locations.name: Supreme Court of the United Kingdom

events.name: UK Supreme Court rules on prorogation

events.enhanced_description: U.S. Speaker of the House Nancy Pelosi announced the initiation of a formal impeachment inquiry against President Donald Trump, citing concerns over his dealings with Ukraine. This marked a pivotal moment in American politics, reflecting deep partisan divisions and raising questions about presidential accountability.
events.name: Impeachment inquiry against Donald Trump

events.enhanced_description: During the United Nations General Assembly in New York, the Financial Sector Commission on Modern Slavery and Human Trafficking released its final report titled 'Unlocking Potential: A Blueprint for Mobilizing Finance Against Slavery and Trafficking.' This report aimed to mobilize financial resources to combat modern slavery and human trafficking.
events.name: UN report on modern slavery

events.enhanced_description: In a powerful demonstration for climate action, approximately 500,000 people marched in Montreal, Canada, led by activist Greta Thunberg and Prime Minister Justin Trudeau. This protest was part of a larger global movement, with millions participating worldwide to demand urgent action on climate change.
events.name: Climate change protest in Montreal

events.enhanced_description: The Republic of Ireland committed to planting 440 million trees over the next twenty years as part of its strategy to combat climate change. This initiative reflects a growing recognition of the importance of reforestation and environmental sustainability.
events.name: Ireland's tree planting promise

events.enhanced_description: During the ongoing 2019–20 Hong Kong protests, a protester was critically injured after being shot in the chest with live ammunition. This incident intensified the already volatile situation, drawing international attention to the protests against the government's actions.
events.name: Hong Kong protests: Protester shot

events.enhanced_description: In a tragic incident in Mali, 25 soldiers were killed and 60 others went missing following coordinated attacks on two army camps in Boulkessi and Mondoro. This attack highlighted the ongoing security challenges faced by the Malian government in combating insurgency and terrorism.
events.name: Attack on army camps in Mali

events.enhanced_description: European Commission spokesperson Daniel Rosario issued a warning of retaliatory measures against the United States if it proceeded with a proposed $7.5 billion tariff on various products, including olives and whiskey. This situation underscored the ongoing trade tensions between the U.S. and the EU.
events.name: EU threatens retaliatory measures

events.enhanced_description: In response to escalating protests, Hong Kong Chief Executive Carrie Lam invoked the Emergency Regulations Ordinance to ban face masks in public gatherings. This controversial decision aimed to curb the anonymity of protesters and restore order amidst the ongoing unrest.
events.name: Hong Kong bans face masks

events.enhanced_description: During a week of protests in Iraq, police violence resulted in the deaths of 91 individuals, highlighting the intense public discontent with government corruption and economic hardship. The protests were part of a larger movement demanding political reform and accountability.
events.name: Iraqi protests: Police violence

events.enhanced_description: In the midst of widespread protests against economic measures, the Ecuadorian government, led by President Lenín Moreno, relocated to Guayaquil as protesters overtook the Carondelet Palace in Quito. This marked a significant escalation in the civil unrest that gripped the country.
events.name: Ecuadorian protests: Government relocation

events.enhanced_description: President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan of Turkey announced a military invasion into northeastern Syria, targeting the Syrian Democratic Forces (SDF) and other Kurdish militias. This offensive raised concerns over regional stability and the humanitarian impact on civilians in the area.
events.name: Turkish offensive into Syria

events.enhanced_description: Typhoon Hagibis, one of the most powerful storms to hit Japan in decades, made landfall, prompting the evacuation of over seven million people. The typhoon caused widespread damage and raised concerns about disaster preparedness in the region.

image.date_qualification: Depicted date: 2019-10-12.
