events.enhanced_description: The Supreme Court of Spain sentenced nine leaders of the Catalan independence movement to prison terms ranging from 9 to 13 years for sedition and misuse of public funds. This ruling sparked violent protests across Catalonia, reflecting the ongoing tensions surrounding the independence movement.
events.name: Trial of Catalonia independence leaders

events.enhanced_description: Venezuelan councilman and opposition politician Edmundo Rada was reported missing, only to be found dead the following day in Petare, Caracas. His death, marked by signs of violence, raised alarms about the safety of political figures in Venezuela amidst ongoing political turmoil.
events.name: Edmundo Rada reported missing

events.enhanced_description: Following the arrest of Ovidio Guzmán López, son of notorious drug lord El Chapo, violent shootouts erupted in Culiacán, Mexico. The chaos resulted in eight deaths and the escape of 56 inmates from prison, leading to Guzmán's release to restore order.
events.name: Culiacán shootouts after Ovidio Guzmán's arrest

events.enhanced_description: NASA astronauts Jessica Meir and Christina Koch made history by conducting the first all-female spacewalk outside the International Space Station. This milestone was celebrated as a significant achievement for women in science and space exploration.
events.name: First all-female spacewalk

events.enhanced_description: An estimated one million people marched through London in a protest organized by the People's Vote campaign, demanding a second referendum on Brexit. This demonstration reflected the ongoing divisions within the UK regarding its future relationship with the European Union.
events.name: People's Vote protest for second Brexit referendum

events.enhanced_description: The discovery of 39 bodies in a truck container in Essex, England, shocked the nation and raised serious concerns about human trafficking. A 25-year-old man from Northern Ireland was arrested on suspicion of murder in connection with this tragic incident.
events.name: Bodies found in Essex truck container

events.enhanced_description: The Supreme Court of Spain ruled in favor of exhuming the remains of dictator Francisco Franco from the Valle de los Caídos, a controversial site that had become a symbol of Spain's Francoist past. Franco's remains were re-inhumed in a private crypt with his wife on October 24, 2019, marking a significant moment in Spain's ongoing reconciliation with its history.
events.name: Exhumation of Francisco Franco

events.enhanced_description: In 2019, Chile held a constitutional referendum where 90.61% of voters approved the process to draft a new constitution. This event was a response to widespread protests demanding social and political reforms.
events.name: Constitutional referendum: The new constitution was approved by 90.61% of valid votes

events.enhanced_description: Tourists visited the summit of Uluru for the last time as a ban on climbing the iconic rock came into effect, reflecting a growing respect for Indigenous culture and the significance of the site to the Anangu people. This decision marked a pivotal moment in the reconciliation process between Indigenous Australians and the broader community.
events.name: Ban on climbing Uluru comes into effect

events.enhanced_description: During the Amazon Catholic bishops synod, a proposal was made to allow married men to be ordained as priests, challenging the long-standing Catholic discipline of celibacy. This proposal aimed to address the shortage of priests in the Amazon region and respond to the needs of local communities.
events.name: Amazon bishops synod proposes married priests

events.enhanced_description: U.S. President Donald Trump announced the death of Abu Bakr al-Baghdadi, the leader of the Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant, during a U.S. special forces operation. Al-Baghdadi reportedly detonated a suicide vest after being pursued, marking a significant moment in the fight against ISIS.
events.name: Death of Abu Bakr al-Baghdadi

events.enhanced_description: In a groundbreaking move, Twitter announced a global ban on all political advertising, aiming to reduce misinformation and the influence of money in politics. This decision was seen as a significant step in the ongoing debate over the role of social media in democratic processes.
events.name: Twitter bans political advertising

events.enhanced_description: On October 31, 2019, a fire broke out at Shuri Castle, a UNESCO World Heritage Site in Naha, Okinawa, Japan, destroying much of the historic structure. The castle, which had stood for over 500 years, was a symbol of the Ryukyu Kingdom and its cultural heritage.
events.name: Fire at Shuri Castle

events.enhanced_description: The 2019 Rugby Union World Cup culminated in a thrilling final held in Yokohama, Japan, where the South Africa Springboks triumphed over England with a score of 32-12. This victory marked South Africa's third World Cup title.
events.name: 2019 Rugby Union World Cup Final

events.enhanced_description: On November 4, 2019, nine members of the LeBarón and Langford families were killed by Mexican gang members while traveling to a wedding in Sonora, Mexico, approximately 110 kilometers south of the U.S. border. This incident drew international attention to the violence in Mexico.
events.name: LeBarón and Langford families massacre

events.enhanced_description: On November 5, 2019, a group of 11,000 scientists from around the world published a study in the journal BioScience, unequivocally warning that planet Earth is facing a climate emergency. This declaration aimed to raise awareness and prompt action against climate change.
events.name: Climate emergency warning by scientists

events.enhanced_description: On November 6, 2019, at least 37 people were killed and 60 others injured when gunmen attacked a convoy belonging to a Canadian gold mining company on a road in Fada N'Gourma, Burkina Faso. This attack underscored the growing insecurity in the region.
events.name: Fada N'Gourma attack

events.enhanced_description: On November 7, 2019, former Congolese rebel leader Bosco Ntaganda was sentenced to 30 years in prison for war crimes and crimes against humanity by the International Criminal Court. This marked the longest sentence ever handed down by the court.
events.name: Bosco Ntaganda sentencing

events.enhanced_description: On November 9, 2019, the Supreme Court of India awarded a disputed holy site in Ayodhya, Uttar Pradesh, to Hindus, rejecting a claim by Muslims. This ruling was expected to exacerbate sectarian tensions in the country.
events.name: Ayodhya Supreme Court ruling

events.enhanced_description: On November 10, 2019, Bolivian President Evo Morales and Vice President Álvaro García Linera resigned following three weeks of intense protests against alleged electoral fraud. Their resignations triggered a political crisis in Bolivia.
events.name: Bolivian protests and resignations

events.enhanced_description: On November 11, 2019, a transit of Mercury occurred, an astronomical event where the planet Mercury passes directly between the Earth and the Sun. This rare event is of significant interest to astronomers and enthusiasts alike.
events.name: Transit of Mercury

events.enhanced_description: In November 2019, amid widespread protests against the government of Evo Morales, Jeanine Áñez declared herself interim president of Bolivia. Her ascension to power was marked by political turmoil and allegations of a coup, as the country faced significant unrest and division.
events.name: 2019 Bolivian protests: Jeanine Áñez took power as interim President of Bolivia amidst political crisis

events.enhanced_description: On November 13, 2019, public impeachment hearings against U.S. President Donald Trump commenced in the House of Representatives. These hearings were a pivotal moment in the impeachment inquiry, focusing on allegations of abuse of power and obstruction of Congress.
events.name: Public impeachment hearings against U.S. President Donald Trump

events.enhanced_description: On November 14, 2019, a tragic mass shooting occurred at Saugus High School in Santa Clarita, California, resulting in three deaths, including the shooter, and three injuries. This incident reignited discussions on gun control and school safety in the United States.
events.name: Saugus High School mass shooting

events.enhanced_description: On November 17, 2019, during the ongoing protests in Hong Kong, police clashed with demonstrators attempting to breach cordons at The Hong Kong Polytechnic University. The situation escalated as protesters retaliated with Molotov cocktails and other projectiles, marking a significant confrontation in the protests.
events.name: 2019–20 Hong Kong protests: Police use tear gas and water cannons

events.enhanced_description: On November 19, 2019, Google launched Stadia, its cloud gaming service, marking the company's entry into the competitive video game market. This innovative platform aimed to redefine gaming by allowing users to stream games directly to their devices without the need for traditional consoles.
events.name: Google enters the video game market with the launch of Stadia

events.enhanced_description: On November 21, 2019, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu was indicted on charges of bribery, fraud, and breach of trust. This unprecedented legal action against a sitting prime minister sparked significant political debate and controversy in Israel.
events.name: Benjamin Netanyahu indicted on charges

events.enhanced_description: On November 23, 2019, the last known Sumatran rhinoceros in Malaysia died, marking a significant loss for conservation efforts. This event highlighted the urgent need for wildlife protection and the challenges faced in preserving endangered species.
events.name: Last known Sumatran rhinoceros in Malaysia dies

events.enhanced_description: On November 23, 2019, a non-binding independence referendum was held in Bougainville, an autonomous region of Papua New Guinea, where voters overwhelmingly supported independence. This referendum was a significant step in the region's quest for self-determination.
events.name: Bougainville independence referendum

events.enhanced_description: On November 24, 2019, a plane crash occurred shortly after takeoff in a densely populated area of Goma, Democratic Republic of the Congo, resulting in the deaths of all 19 people on board and at least 10 others on the ground. This tragic incident raised concerns about aviation safety in the region.

locations.name: Goma, North Kivu, Democratic Republic of the Congo

events.name: 2019 Busy Bee crash

events.enhanced_description: On November 25, 2019, the World Meteorological Organization reported that levels of heat-trapping greenhouse gases in the atmosphere reached a new record high of 407.8 parts per million. This alarming statistic underscored the ongoing climate crisis and the urgent need for global action.
events.name: World Meteorological Organization reports record greenhouse gas levels

events.enhanced_description: On November 26, 2019, a 6.4-magnitude earthquake struck near Durrës, Albania, resulting in the deaths of 51 people and injuring around 2,000 others. This earthquake was the strongest to hit Albania in over 40 years and was the deadliest earthquake worldwide in 2019.
events.name: 2019 Albania earthquake

events.enhanced_description: On November 27, 2019, the U.S. Government passed the Hong Kong Human Rights and Democracy Act, which aimed to support the pro-democracy movement in Hong Kong amidst ongoing protests against Chinese authority. This legislation was a significant statement of U.S. foreign policy regarding human rights.
events.name: U.S. Government passes the Hong Kong Human Rights and Democracy Act

events.enhanced_description: The first known human case of Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) was reported in Wuhan, Hubei, China, in December 2019. This marked the beginning of a global pandemic that would have profound impacts on health, economies, and daily life worldwide.
events.name: First known human case of COVID-19

events.enhanced_description: On December 2, 2019, Typhoon Kammuri struck the Philippines, prompting the evacuation of approximately 200,000 people. Fortunately, there were no reports of injuries or significant damage, showcasing the effectiveness of disaster preparedness in the region.
events.name: Typhoon Kammuri

events.enhanced_description: The 2019 United Nations Climate Change Conference was held in Madrid, Spain, after Chilean President Sebastián Piñera announced that Chile could not host the event due to political unrest. The conference aimed to address global climate change and its impacts.
events.name: 2019 United Nations Climate Change Conference

events.enhanced_description: In December 2019, a landslide in Burundi was reported to have caused at least 26 deaths. The incident highlighted the vulnerability of the region to natural disasters, particularly during the rainy season.
events.name: 2019 Burundi landslide

events.enhanced_description: On December 8, 2019, a devastating fire at a factory in Delhi, India, resulted in the deaths of 43 individuals and left at least 50 others injured. The incident raised concerns about safety regulations in industrial facilities.
events.name: Factory fire in Delhi

events.enhanced_description: On December 9, 2019, the World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA) voted unanimously to ban Russia from international sports for four years due to doping offenses. This decision meant that Russia would be excluded from major events, including the 2020 Summer Olympics and the 2022 World Cup.
events.name: WADA bans Russia from international sport

events.enhanced_description: On December 10, 2019, Sanna Marin was selected to lead Finland's Social Democratic Party, making her the world's youngest serving prime minister at the age of 34. Her leadership marked a significant moment in Finnish politics.
events.name: Sanna Marin becomes Prime Minister of Finland

events.enhanced_description: On December 11, 2019, the World Trade Organization (WTO) found itself unable to intervene in trade disputes after the United States blocked the appointment of new panel members. This situation raised concerns about the future of international trade governance.
events.name: World Trade Organization unable to intervene

events.enhanced_description: On December 12, 2019, Boris Johnson and his Conservative Party achieved a landslide victory in the United Kingdom general election, securing a majority of 80 seats in the House of Commons. This victory solidified Johnson's position as Prime Minister.
events.name: 2019 United Kingdom general election

events.enhanced_description: On December 16, 2019, Pope Francis abolished pontifical secrecy in cases of sexual abuse, a significant move following the Vatican's Meeting on the Protection of Minors. This decision aimed to enhance transparency and accountability within the Church.
events.name: Pope Francis abolishes pontifical secrecy

events.enhanced_description: On December 17, 2019, Shandong, China's first fully domestically built aircraft carrier, was commissioned into naval service. This milestone marked a significant advancement in China's naval capabilities.
events.name: Shandong aircraft carrier enters service

events.enhanced_description: On December 18, 2019, the CHEOPS space telescope was launched with the mission to study the formation of extrasolar planets and determine their characteristics. This mission represents a significant step forward in the field of exoplanet research.
events.name: CHEOPS space telescope launched

events.enhanced_description: On December 19, 2019, Libya's Government of National Accord activated a cooperation accord with Turkey, paving the way for potential Turkish military intervention in the ongoing Second Libyan Civil War. This agreement highlighted the complex geopolitical dynamics in the region.
events.name: Turkey-Libya cooperation accord

events.enhanced_description: On December 23, 2019, five men were sentenced to death and three others received prison sentences for their involvement in the murder of dissident journalist Jamal Khashoggi at the Saudi consulate in Istanbul. This case drew international attention and condemnation.
events.name: Khashoggi murder sentencing

events.enhanced_description: On December 24, 2019, thousands of Muslims protested in the Amhara Region of Ethiopia following the burning of four mosques. The protests highlighted ongoing tensions related to religious freedom and community rights in the region.
events.name: Protests in Ethiopia

events.enhanced_description: On December 27, 2019, corporate defaults on bonds in China reached a new record, raising concerns about the stability of the Chinese economy and the potential impacts on global markets.
events.name: Corporate defaults in China

events.enhanced_description: On December 30, 2019, Chinese scientist He Jiankui was sentenced to three years in prison and fined for his controversial genetic research, which included the creation of genetically edited human babies. This case raised significant ethical questions regarding genetic engineering.
events.name: He Jiankui sentenced

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2020, Croatia officially began its term as the presidency of the European Union, marking a significant milestone for the country in its role within the EU framework.
events.name: Croatia EU presidency

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2020, Croatia commenced its six-month term in the presidency of the European Union, becoming the first country from the former Yugoslavia to hold this position. This presidency involved leading EU meetings and setting the agenda for the EU's activities.
events.name: Croatia begins its term in the presidency of the European Union

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2020, Jakarta experienced severe flash floods that resulted in the deaths of 66 people, marking one of the worst flooding incidents in over a decade. The floods caused widespread damage and displacement in the capital city.

locations.name: Jakarta, Jakarta Special Capital Region, Indonesia

events.name: Flash floods struck Jakarta, Indonesia

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2020, Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan announced the deployment of Turkish troops to Libya in support of the United Nations-backed Government of National Accord amid the ongoing Second Libyan Civil War. This decision escalated international involvement in the conflict.
events.name: Second Libyan Civil War: Turkish troop deployment announced

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2020, the second round of the Croatian presidential election was held, where Zoran Milanović of the Social Democratic Party defeated the incumbent president Kolinda Grabar-Kitarović. This election marked a significant political shift in Croatia.
events.name: 2019–20 Croatian presidential election: Second round of voting

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2020, Iran launched ballistic missiles at two Iraqi military bases housing U.S. soldiers, resulting in injuries to over 100 personnel. This attack was a response to the killing of Iranian General Qasem Soleimani by a U.S. drone strike.

locations.name: Ain al-Asad Airbase, Al Anbar Governorate, Iraq

events.name: Iran launches ballistic missiles at Iraqi military bases

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2020, Ukraine International Airlines Flight 752 was shot down by Iranian forces shortly after takeoff from Tehran Imam Khomeini International Airport, resulting in the tragic loss of all 176 passengers and crew on board. This incident raised international tensions and scrutiny over Iran's military actions.
events.name: Ukraine International Airlines Flight 752 shot down

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2020, astronomers announced the discovery of TOI 1338-b, a rare circumbinary planet that orbits two stars. This discovery adds to the understanding of planetary systems and the diversity of exoplanets in the universe.
events.name: Discovery of circumbinary planet TOI 1338-b

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2020, Islamic State militants attacked a military base in Chinagodrar, Niger, resulting in the deaths of at least 89 Nigerien soldiers. This assault highlighted the ongoing security challenges faced by Niger in the Sahel region.
events.name: Islamic State militants assault Nigerien military base

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2020, Peru held parliamentary elections to elect all 130 members of the Congress of the Republic of Peru. This election was pivotal in shaping the legislative framework of the country.
events.name: Peruvian parliamentary election

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2020, basketball legend Kobe Bryant tragically died in a helicopter crash in Calabasas, California, along with his daughter Gianna and seven others. His death shocked fans worldwide and led to an outpouring of tributes to his legacy in sports.
events.name: Kobe Bryant dies in a helicopter crash

events.enhanced_description: During a demonstration in Barquisimeto, Venezuela, on an unspecified date, pro-government colectivos opened fire on supporters of disputed President Juan Guaidó, resulting in five injuries. This incident highlighted the ongoing political turmoil and violence in Venezuela.
events.name: Barquisimeto shooting

events.enhanced_description: In early 2020, the Democratic Republic of the Congo reported its first case of Ebola since February, marking a resurgence of the virus that had already claimed over 2,200 lives since the outbreak began in August 2018. The ongoing health crisis raised concerns about the country's healthcare system's ability to manage multiple epidemics simultaneously.
events.name: First case of Ebola since February 2020 in DRC

events.enhanced_description: In January 2020, the International Monetary Fund (IMF) projected a 3% contraction in the global economy, marking the worst economic downturn since the Great Depression of the 1930s. This announcement highlighted the severe impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on economic activities worldwide.
events.name: IMF World Economy Contraction Announcement

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2020, U.S. President Donald Trump announced the suspension of funding to the World Health Organization (WHO) pending an investigation into its handling of the COVID-19 pandemic and its relationship with China. This decision sparked significant controversy and debate regarding the U.S. role in global health governance.
events.name: Trump Suspends WHO Funding

events.enhanced_description: By early January 2020, the number of confirmed COVID-19 cases worldwide surpassed 2 million, reflecting the rapid spread of the virus. This milestone underscored the global health crisis that was unfolding, leading to widespread lockdowns and public health measures.
events.name: COVID-19 Cases Exceed 2 Million

events.enhanced_description: Due to the COVID-19 pandemic, the 2020 Tour de France was postponed until August 2020. This marked a significant disruption in the sports calendar, as the event is one of the most prestigious cycling races in the world.
events.name: Tour de France Delayed

events.enhanced_description: In January 2020, the China Securities Regulatory Commission approved a transaction allowing Switzerland's Credit Suisse to acquire a majority interest in a Chinese securities firm. This marked a significant milestone as it was the first instance of a foreign bank owning a majority stake in such a company since the easing of foreign ownership rules in 2018.
events.name: Credit Suisse Majority Interest Approval

events.enhanced_description: In early January 2020, Chinese authorities revised the COVID-19 death toll in Wuhan, adding 1,290 fatalities to the official count, bringing the total reported deaths in the country to 4,632. This revision raised concerns about the accuracy of data reported during the pandemic.
events.name: China Revises COVID-19 Death Toll

events.enhanced_description: By early January 2020, Europe surpassed the grim milestone of 100,000 COVID-19-related deaths, reflecting the severe impact of the pandemic across the continent. This statistic underscored the urgent need for effective public health responses and international cooperation.
events.name: Europe Surpasses 100,000 COVID-19 Deaths

events.enhanced_description: In early January 2020, the U.N. Human Rights Office accused Myanmar's military of conducting daily airstrikes in Rakhine and Chin states, resulting in civilian casualties. This accusation highlighted ongoing human rights concerns amid the conflict in Myanmar.
events.name: Myanmar Airstrikes Accusation

events.enhanced_description: In early January 2020, unrest erupted in major cities including Paris, Berlin, and Vladikavkaz as citizens protested against COVID-19 lockdown measures. These demonstrations reflected growing frustration over restrictions imposed to combat the pandemic.
events.name: COVID-19 Lockdown Protests

events.enhanced_description: In early January 2020, the Industrial Bank of Korea agreed to pay $86 million and enter a two-year deferred prosecution agreement to settle lawsuits with the U.S. Department of Justice. This settlement was related to a scheme that allegedly helped transfer $1 billion to Iran in 2011.
events.name: Industrial Bank of Korea Settlement

events.enhanced_description: In early January 2020, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Blue and White Alliance leader Benny Gantz reached an agreement to form a unity government, ending over a year of political deadlock. Under the deal, Netanyahu would remain in power for 18 months before Gantz took over.
events.name: Israeli Unity Government Agreement

events.enhanced_description: In early January 2020, two former high-ranking members of the Syrian Army went on trial in Koblenz, Germany, for alleged war crimes committed during the Syrian Civil War. This marked a significant moment in international law, as it was the first time Syrian military officials faced prosecution for their actions in the conflict.
events.name: Syrian War Crimes Trial

events.enhanced_description: In early January 2020, Facebook announced the removal of 'pseudoscience' and 'conspiracy theory' as options for targeted ads. This decision came amid increasing criticism of social media platforms for their role in spreading misinformation about COVID-19.
events.name: Facebook Removes Misinformation Ads

events.enhanced_description: In early January 2020, the Southern Transitional Council (STC) declared the establishment of a self-rule administration in southern Yemen, deploying forces in Aden. This move was met with resistance from local governors who pledged loyalty to the internationally recognized government.
events.name: Yemeni Civil War Self-Rule Declaration

events.enhanced_description: By early January 2020, the global death toll from COVID-19 surpassed 200,000, with the United Kingdom becoming the fifth country to report over 20,000 deaths. This grim milestone highlighted the pandemic's devastating impact on public health worldwide.
events.name: Global COVID-19 Death Toll Exceeds 200,000

events.enhanced_description: In early January 2020, astronomers detected a fast radio burst from the magnetar SGR 1935+2154, marking the first instance of such a burst detected within the Milky Way and linked to a known source. This discovery contributed to the understanding of cosmic phenomena.
events.name: Fast Radio Burst Detected

events.enhanced_description: In early January 2020, Colombia formalized its membership with the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD), becoming the 37th member of the organization. This membership reflects Colombia's commitment to economic reforms and international cooperation.
events.name: Colombia Joins OECD

events.enhanced_description: In early January 2020, the Indian Ministry of External Affairs condemned the U.S. Commission on International Religious Freedom for recommending that India be placed on a blacklist over various human rights concerns. This statement highlighted the ongoing tensions between India and the U.S. regarding human rights issues.
events.name: India Condemns US Commission Report

events.enhanced_description: In early January 2020, NASA officially selected SpaceX, Blue Origin, and Dynetics to develop its next-generation lunar lander, aiming to carry American astronauts to the Moon by 2024. This decision marked a significant step in the Artemis program, which seeks to return humans to the lunar surface.
events.name: NASA Selects Lunar Lander Contractors

events.enhanced_description: In early January 2020, Bulgaria applied to join the Exchange Rate Mechanism II (ERM II), a preparatory step for adopting the Euro. This application was part of Bulgaria's broader strategy to integrate more closely with the European Union.
events.name: Bulgaria Applies for ERM II

events.enhanced_description: In January 2020, astronomers Andrea Ghez and Reinhard Genzel announced the discovery of the first black hole located in a star system visible to the naked eye, named Sagittarius A*. This groundbreaking finding provided significant insights into the nature of black holes and their formation in the universe.
events.name: Astronomers announce the discovery of the first black hole located in a star system visible to the naked eye

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2020, new evidence emerged indicating that an Algerian-born French fishmonger in Bordeaux was treated for pneumonia from an unknown source on December 27, 2019. This case was later identified as an early instance of COVID-19, highlighting the virus's spread beyond initial epicenters.
events.name: COVID-19 pandemic: New evidence indicates that an Algerian-born French fishmonger was treated for pneumonia from an unknown source

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2020, the Iranian Navy frigate Jamaran mistakenly struck the support vessel Konarak with a missile during a naval exercise in the Strait of Hormuz, resulting in the tragic deaths of nineteen sailors. This incident marked a significant event in the context of military operations in the region.
events.name: The Iranian Navy frigate Jamaran accidentally strikes the Iranian support vessel Konarak with a missile

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2020, Wuhan, China, reported its first new coronavirus cases in over a month, including an 89-year-old man confirmed positive for COVID-19. This resurgence raised alarms about the potential for a second wave of infections in the city that was the initial epicenter of the pandemic.
events.name: COVID-19 pandemic: Wuhan reports its first coronavirus cases in more than a month

events.enhanced_description: As of January 1, 2020, the global death toll from COVID-19 surpassed 300,000, prompting warnings from the United Nations about a potential mental health crisis due to the pandemic's isolation and economic impacts. This milestone underscored the severe toll of the pandemic worldwide.
events.name: COVID-19 pandemic: The global death toll from COVID-19 exceeds 300,000

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2020, NATO Secretary General Jens Stoltenberg stated that the military alliance was prepared to support the UN-recognized Government of National Accord in Libya. This statement drew criticism from Greece, highlighting tensions within NATO regarding the recognition of the Libyan government.
events.name: NATO Secretary General Jens Stoltenberg comments on support for the UN-recognized Government of National Accord

events.enhanced_description: By January 1, 2020, the global death toll from COVID-19 had exceeded 300,000, marking a significant milestone in the pandemic's impact on public health worldwide. The situation prompted urgent calls for action to address the ongoing crisis.
events.name: The global death toll from COVID-19 exceeds 300,000

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2020, the United Nations issued a warning about a looming global mental health crisis stemming from the COVID-19 pandemic. The organization highlighted the effects of isolation, fear, and economic instability on mental well-being worldwide.
events.name: The UN warns of a global mental health crisis caused by isolation, fear, uncertainty and economic turmoil

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2020, the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs reported that nearly 1 million people were affected by flash floods in Beledweyne and Jowhar, Somalia, resulting in at least 24 fatalities. This humanitarian crisis underscored the vulnerability of communities to extreme weather events.
figures: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs
events.name: The UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs announces flash floods in Somalia

events.enhanced_description: In a historic move on January 1, 2020, the World Health Organization conducted its annual World Health Assembly via video conferencing instead of in-person meetings due to the COVID-19 pandemic. This adaptation highlighted the ongoing challenges posed by the global health crisis.
events.name: World Health Organization holds its annual World Health Assembly using video conferencing

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2020, Cyclone Amphan made landfall in eastern India and Bangladesh, resulting in over 100 fatalities and the evacuation of more than 4 million people. The cyclone caused damages exceeding $13 billion, marking it as the costliest cyclone recorded in the North Indian Ocean.
events.name: Cyclone Amphan makes landfall in eastern India and Bangladesh

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2020, the United States announced its intention to withdraw from the Open Skies Treaty within six months, citing continuous violations by Russia. This decision marked a significant shift in U.S. arms control policy and raised concerns about transparency in military activities.
events.name: The U.S. announces it will withdraw from the Open Skies Treaty

events.enhanced_description: As of January 1, 2020, the number of confirmed COVID-19 cases worldwide surpassed 5 million, with a record 106,000 new cases reported in a single day. This alarming statistic underscored the rapid spread of the virus and the challenges faced by health systems globally.
events.name: COVID-19 pandemic: The number of confirmed cases of COVID-19 passes 5 million worldwide

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2020, Flight PK8303, a Pakistan International Airlines passenger aircraft, tragically crashed in a residential area near Karachi, killing 97 of the 99 people on board and injuring dozens on the ground. This incident raised concerns about aviation safety in the region.
events.name: Flight PK8303 crashes in Karachi, Pakistan

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2020, Brazil surpassed Russia to become the country with the second highest number of confirmed COVID-19 cases, reporting over 330,000 cases. President Jair Bolsonaro's continued dismissal of the virus's threat drew criticism amid the escalating health crisis.
events.name: COVID-19 pandemic: Brazil overtakes Russia to become the country with the second highest number of COVID-19 cases

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2020, mining corporation Rio Tinto publicly admitted to the destruction of the 46,000-year-old Juukan Gorge caves in the Pilbara region of Western Australia. The company later issued an apology to the Aboriginal peoples who are the traditional owners of the site, sparking widespread outrage and calls for better protection of Indigenous heritage.
events.name: Mining corporation Rio Tinto admits to blowing up the Juukan Gorge caves

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2020, Egyptian President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi pardoned 3,157 prisoners in a gesture to celebrate Eid al-Fitr. This act of clemency was part of broader efforts to address prison overcrowding and promote goodwill in the country.
events.name: Egyptian President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi pardons 3,157 prisoners

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2020, Suriname held a general election to elect all 51 members of its National Assembly. This election was significant for the country's democratic process and governance.
events.name: Surinamese general election is held

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2020, Euroleague Basketball announced the cancellation of the 2019-20 Turkish Airlines EuroLeague and 7DAYS EuroCup seasons due to the COVID-19 pandemic. This decision reflected the widespread impact of the pandemic on global sports.
events.name: Euroleague Basketball cancels the 2019-20 seasons due to COVID-19 pandemic

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2020, protests erupted across hundreds of cities in the United States in response to the murder of George Floyd. These protests sparked a global movement against racism and police brutality, leading to ongoing demonstrations and calls for justice.
events.name: Protests caused by the murder of George Floyd break out across hundreds of cities in the U.S.

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2020, Costa Rica made history by becoming the first Central American country to legalize same-sex marriage. This landmark decision was celebrated by LGBTQ+ advocates and marked a significant step toward equality in the region.
events.name: Costa Rica becomes the first Central American country to legalise same-sex marriage

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2020, LATAM Airlines, the largest air carrier in Latin America, filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection. This move was a direct consequence of the financial strain caused by the COVID-19 pandemic on the aviation industry.
events.name: LATAM Airlines files for Chapter 11 bankruptcy

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2020, the Chinese National People's Congress voted in favor of national security legislation that criminalizes secession, subversion, and foreign interference in Hong Kong. This legislation granted the central government sweeping powers to suppress the pro-democracy movement in the region.
events.name: Chinese National People's Congress votes in favour of national security legislation for Hong Kong

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2020, the death toll from COVID-19 in the United States surpassed 100,000, a grim milestone that highlighted the pandemic's devastating impact on American society. This figure surpassed the combined death toll of the Vietnam and Korean Wars.
events.name: COVID-19 pandemic: The U.S. death toll passes 100,000

events.enhanced_description: The Serbian parliamentary election held in January 2020 resulted in the ruling For Our Children coalition securing 188 out of 250 seats in the National Assembly of Serbia, reinforcing the government's majority. This election was significant in shaping the political landscape of Serbia amidst ongoing challenges and controversies.
events.name: Serbian parliamentary election

events.enhanced_description: In January 2020, Kiribati held its presidential election, resulting in the reelection of incumbent president Taneti Maamau. This election was pivotal for the nation's governance and its approach to pressing issues such as climate change and economic development.

image.caption: Map showing the margin of victory in the 2020 Kiribati presidential election.

image.date_qualification: The depicted subject is the 2020 election; the map itself is dated 2024-07-25.
