events.name: Kiribati presidential election

events.enhanced_description: In early 2020, widespread protests erupted across Bulgaria, demanding the resignation of Prime Minister Boyko Borisov's government and Chief Prosecutor Ivan Geshev. The protests were fueled by public dissatisfaction with corruption and governance issues, marking a significant moment in Bulgaria's political landscape.
events.name: Protests in Bulgaria against Borisov's cabinet

events.enhanced_description: In response to stricter lockdown measures proposed by President Aleksandar Vučić amid rising COVID-19 cases, thousands rallied outside the National Assembly in Belgrade. This demonstration highlighted the tensions between government authority and public sentiment during the pandemic.
events.name: COVID-19 pandemic protests in Serbia

events.enhanced_description: In 2020, the European Central Bank (ECB) accepted Bulgaria and Croatia into the Exchange Rate Mechanism II (ERM II), a crucial step for both countries aspiring to adopt the euro. This marked a significant milestone in the European integration process for these nations.
events.name: Bulgaria and Croatia accepted into ERM II

events.enhanced_description: In a controversial move, President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan ordered the Hagia Sophia in Istanbul to be converted back into a mosque after a supreme court ruling annulled a 1934 decree that designated it as a museum. This decision reignited debates over cultural heritage and religious identity in Turkey.
events.name: Hagia Sophia reverts to mosque

events.enhanced_description: The 2020 Singaporean general election saw the ruling People's Action Party, led by Prime Minister Lee Hsien Loong, secure 83 out of 93 parliamentary seats. This election was significant as it took place during the COVID-19 pandemic, affecting campaigning and voter turnout.
events.name: Singaporean general election

events.enhanced_description: In 2020, during construction at the Santa Lucía Airport in Mexico City, the skeletons of 200 mammoths and 30 other animals were unearthed. This discovery is the largest find of mammoth bones to date, surpassing previous significant sites in the United States.

locations.name: Mexico City Santa Lucía Airport, Mexico

events.name: Discovery of mammoth skeletons at Mexico City Santa Lucía Airport

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2020, France, Germany, and the United Kingdom issued a joint note verbale to the United Nations, rejecting China's territorial claims in the South China Sea. This statement supported the ruling in the Philippines v. China case, which found that China's historic rights under the nine-dash line were inconsistent with the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea.
events.name: Joint note verbale by France, Germany, and the United Kingdom

events.enhanced_description: As of January 1, 2020, the number of confirmed COVID-19 cases worldwide surpassed 30 million, marking a significant milestone in the global pandemic. This alarming statistic highlighted the rapid spread of the virus and the urgent need for public health measures.
events.name: COVID-19 pandemic: Confirmed cases surpass 30 million

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2020, Sheikh Sabah Al-Sabah, the Emir of Kuwait, passed away at the age of 91. Following his death, Crown Prince Nawaf Al-Ahmad Al-Jaber Al-Sabah was named his successor, marking a significant transition in Kuwaiti leadership.
events.name: Death of Sheikh Sabah Al-Sabah

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2020, the Government of Thailand declared a 'severe' state of emergency in response to ongoing protests, banning gatherings of five or more people. This move initiated a crackdown on demonstrations and imposed media censorship.
events.name: Protests in Thailand

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2020, President Sooronbay Jeenbekov of Kyrgyzstan resigned from office following weeks of massive protests triggered by the October 2020 parliamentary election. Opposition leader Sadyr Japarov subsequently assumed the roles of both acting president and Prime Minister.
events.name: Resignation of Sooronbay Jeenbekov

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2020, Israel and Sudan agreed to normalize relations, marking the fifth peace deal between Israel and Arab nations. This agreement was part of a broader trend of diplomatic normalization in the region.
events.name: Israel and Sudan normalize relations

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2020, the number of confirmed COVID-19 cases worldwide surpassed 45 million, highlighting the ongoing global health crisis and the urgent need for continued public health measures.
events.name: COVID-19 pandemic: Confirmed cases surpass 45 million

events.enhanced_description: In December 2020, Sinovac Biotech announced that its COVID-19 vaccine demonstrated an efficacy rate of 91.25% in clinical trials conducted in Turkey. This promising result contributed to the global efforts to combat the COVID-19 pandemic.
events.name: COVID-19 pandemic: Sinovac's vaccine reached a rate of 91.25% efficacy in trials in Turkey

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2020, Pfizer and BioNTech announced their application for Emergency Use Authorization to the European Medicines Agency for their COVID-19 vaccine. This step was crucial in the effort to combat the pandemic in Europe.
events.name: COVID-19 pandemic: Pfizer and BioNTech apply for Emergency Use Authorization

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2020, the Arecibo Telescope at the Arecibo Observatory in Puerto Rico collapsed, just weeks after the announcement of its planned demolition. This event marked the end of an era for one of the world's most iconic radio telescopes, which had contributed significantly to astronomy and atmospheric science.
events.name: Collapse of the Arecibo Telescope

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2020, three activists in Hong Kong were sentenced to prison for their roles in the 2019-20 Hong Kong protests, with Joshua Wong receiving the longest sentence of 13.5 months. This event underscored the ongoing crackdown on dissent in Hong Kong.
events.name: Jailing of Hong Kong activists

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2020, the United Nations Commission on Narcotic Drugs voted to remove cannabis from the treaty list of dangerous drugs, acknowledging its medical value. This decision marked a significant shift in international drug policy.
events.name: UN removes cannabis from dangerous drugs list

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2020, the number of confirmed COVID-19 cases worldwide surpassed 65 million, with the global death toll exceeding 1.5 million. This alarming statistic highlighted the severe impact of the pandemic on global health.
events.name: COVID-19 pandemic: Global cases surpass 65 million

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2020, the United States announced its intention to withdraw from the Somali Civil War over the following month. This decision marked a significant shift in US foreign policy in the region.
events.name: US announces withdrawal from Somali Civil War

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2020, the United Kingdom became the first nation to initiate a mass vaccination campaign using the clinically authorized Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine. Margaret Keenan, aged 90, was the first person to receive the vaccine, marking a historic moment in the fight against COVID-19.
events.name: UK begins mass vaccination with Pfizer vaccine

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2020, Nepal and China officially agreed on the height of Mount Everest, confirming it to be 8,848.86 meters. This agreement resolved long-standing disputes regarding the mountain's elevation.
events.name: Nepal and China agree on Mount Everest height

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2020, Israel and Morocco normalized diplomatic relations, a significant development in Middle Eastern diplomacy. Concurrently, the United States reaffirmed its recognition of Moroccan sovereignty over Western Sahara.
events.name: Israel and Morocco normalize relations

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2020, the corruption trial of former French President Nicolas Sarkozy concluded, marking a significant moment in French politics and law. The trial was part of a broader investigation into allegations of corruption during his presidency.
events.name: Conclusion of Nicolas Sarkozy corruption trial

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2020, the number of confirmed COVID-19 cases worldwide surpassed 70 million, highlighting the ongoing severity of the pandemic. This statistic emphasized the urgent need for continued public health measures and vaccination efforts.
events.name: COVID-19 pandemic: Global cases surpass 70 million

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2020, Bhutan and Israel normalized diplomatic relations, marking a significant step in Bhutan's foreign policy. This development opened new avenues for cooperation between the two nations.
events.name: Bhutan and Israel normalize relations

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2020, the United States removed Sudan from its list of state sponsors of terrorism, a significant diplomatic move that aimed to improve relations between the two countries.
events.name: US removes Sudan from terrorism list

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2020, the United States imposed sanctions on Turkey in response to its purchase of the S-400 missile system from Russia. This marked the first time the US sanctioned a NATO ally, reflecting tensions within the alliance.
events.name: US sanctions Turkey over S-400 missile system

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2020, a total solar eclipse was visible from parts of the South Pacific Ocean, southern South America, and the South Atlantic Ocean. This astronomical event captivated observers and highlighted the beauty of celestial phenomena.
events.name: Total solar eclipse visible from South Pacific and South America

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2020, media outlets reported that astronomers had detected a radio signal, designated BLC1, from the direction of Proxima Centauri, the closest star to the Sun. This signal was considered one of the strongest candidates for extraterrestrial communication.
events.name: Astronomers detect radio signal BLC1 from Proxima Centauri

events.enhanced_description: On January 2, 2020, the Royal Australian Air Force and Navy were deployed to New South Wales and Victoria to assist in mass evacuation efforts amidst the devastating 2019–20 Australian bushfire season, which had caused widespread destruction.

locations.name: New South Wales and Victoria, Australia

events.name: Australian bushfire response

events.enhanced_description: On January 3, 2020, a U.S. drone strike at Baghdad International Airport resulted in the deaths of ten individuals, including Iranian General Qasem Soleimani and Iraqi paramilitary leader Abu Mahdi al-Muhandis, escalating tensions between the U.S. and Iran.
events.name: Baghdad drone strike

events.enhanced_description: On January 5, 2020, Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan announced the deployment of Turkish troops to Libya to support the United Nations-backed Government of National Accord amid the ongoing Second Libyan Civil War.
events.name: Turkish troop deployment to Libya

events.enhanced_description: On January 8, 2020, Iran launched ballistic missiles at two Iraqi military bases housing U.S. soldiers, injuring over 100 personnel, in retaliation for the U.S. drone strike that killed General Qasem Soleimani.
events.name: Iran missile strike on US bases

events.enhanced_description: On January 9, 2020, astronomers announced the discovery of TOI 1338-b, a rare circumbinary planet that orbits two stars, contributing to the understanding of planetary formation and the diversity of exoplanets.
events.name: Discovery of TOI 1338-b

events.enhanced_description: On January 10, 2020, Haitham bin Tariq was appointed as the Sultan of Oman following the death of his cousin, Sultan Qaboos bin Said, who had ruled for nearly 50 years. His ascension marked a significant transition in Oman's leadership and continuity of the Sultanate's policies.
events.name: Haitham bin Tariq succeeds Qaboos bin Said as the Sultan of Oman

events.enhanced_description: On January 11, 2020, Taiwan held its presidential and legislative elections, resulting in the re-election of incumbent president Tsai Ing-wen and a significant victory for her party, the Democratic Progressive Party, which secured 67 out of 113 seats in the Legislative Yuan.
events.name: Presidential and legislative elections are held in Taiwan

events.enhanced_description: On January 12, 2020, the Taal Volcano in the Philippines erupted, marking its first significant eruption since 1977. The eruption prompted widespread evacuations and raised concerns about the potential for a larger volcanic event.
events.name: The Taal Volcano in the Philippines has had its first major eruption since 1977

events.enhanced_description: On January 16, 2020, the impeachment trial of President Donald Trump commenced in the U.S. Senate, following his impeachment by the House of Representatives on charges of abuse of power and obstruction of Congress. The trial concluded with his acquittal on February 5, 2020.
events.name: The first impeachment trial of the President of the United States, Donald Trump, begins

events.enhanced_description: On January 18, 2020, a drone and missile attack on a military camp near Ma'rib, Yemen, resulted in the deaths of 111 Yemeni soldiers and five civilians. This incident highlighted the ongoing violence and instability in the region amidst the Yemeni Civil War.
events.name: Yemeni Civil War: Attack on military camp near Ma'rib

events.enhanced_description: On January 20, 2020, Chinese authorities confirmed that the severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) could be transmitted between humans, marking a critical point in the understanding of the COVID-19 pandemic that would soon affect the entire world.
events.name: COVID-19 pandemic: Confirmation of human-to-human transmission

events.enhanced_description: On January 22, 2020, Katerina Sakellaropoulou was elected as the first female president of Greece by the Hellenic Parliament. Her election was a historic moment for gender representation in Greek politics.
events.name: Katerina Sakellaropoulou elected as president of Greece

events.enhanced_description: On January 23, 2020, the Chinese city of Wuhan, identified as the epicenter of the COVID-19 outbreak, was placed under quarantine. This unprecedented measure included halting all public transport services and intercity flights, aiming to contain the spread of the virus.
events.name: Quarantine of Wuhan due to COVID-19 outbreak

events.enhanced_description: On January 26, 2020, Peru held its parliamentary elections to elect all 130 members of the Congress of the Republic of Peru. This election was crucial for shaping the legislative landscape of the country.
events.name: 2020 Peruvian parliamentary election

events.enhanced_description: On January 29, 2020, U.S. President Donald Trump signed the United States–Mexico–Canada Agreement (USMCA), a significant trade agreement intended to replace the North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA). This agreement aimed to modernize trade relations between the three countries.
events.name: Donald Trump signs the United States–Mexico–Canada Agreement

events.enhanced_description: On January 30, 2020, the World Health Organization (WHO) declared the outbreak of COVID-19 a public health emergency of international concern, marking the sixth time this measure had been invoked since 2009. This declaration underscored the global threat posed by the virus.
events.name: WHO declares COVID-19 a public health emergency

events.enhanced_description: On January 31, 2020, the United Kingdom and Gibraltar officially withdrew from the European Union, marking the end of a 47-year membership and beginning an 11-month transition period to negotiate future relations.
events.name: United Kingdom formally withdraws from the European Union

events.enhanced_description: On February 6, 2020, a Frecciarossa high-speed train derailed while traveling from Milan to Salerno in Livraga, Lombardy, Italy. The incident resulted in two fatalities and 31 injuries, raising concerns about railway safety standards.
events.name: Livraga derailment

events.enhanced_description: On February 8, 2020, Ireland held its general election to elect 160 members of the 33rd Dáil, the lower house of the Oireachtas. This election was significant in shaping the future political landscape of Ireland.
events.name: The 2020 Irish general election

events.enhanced_description: On February 11, 2020, the World Health Organization (WHO) officially named the disease caused by the novel coronavirus as COVID-19. This naming was part of the global effort to standardize terminology and facilitate communication regarding the pandemic.
events.name: WHO names the disease COVID-19

events.enhanced_description: NASA published a comprehensive study of Arrokoth, a Kuiper Belt object that is the most distant body ever explored by a spacecraft, following the New Horizons flyby in January 2019. This study provided valuable insights into the formation and evolution of the early solar system.
events.name: NASA publishes a detailed study of Arrokoth

events.enhanced_description: On February 19, 2020, a far-right extremist carried out a shooting spree in Hanau, Germany, targeting shisha bars, resulting in the deaths of eleven people and injuring five others. This tragic event highlighted the growing concerns over far-right extremism and violence in Germany.
events.name: Hanau shootings

events.enhanced_description: On February 24, 2020, the Pakatan Harapan coalition government in Malaysia collapsed, leading to the formation of the Perikatan Nasional coalition. Muhyiddin Yassin was appointed as the eighth Prime Minister, marking a significant political shift in the country.
events.name: Collapse of the Pakatan Harapan government in Malaysia

events.enhanced_description: On February 27, 2020, the Dow Jones Industrial Average experienced a significant drop of 1,190.95 points, or 4.4%, marking its largest one-day point decline at that time. This crash was largely attributed to growing fears surrounding the COVID-19 pandemic.
events.name: 2020 stock market crash

events.enhanced_description: Following the deaths of 34 Turkish soldiers in an airstrike by pro-Syrian government forces on February 28, 2020, NATO expressed solidarity with Turkey. This incident underscored the escalating tensions in the Syrian Civil War and Turkey's role in the conflict.
events.name: NATO expresses solidarity with Turkey

events.enhanced_description: On February 29, 2020, a conditional peace agreement was signed between the United States and the Taliban in Doha, Qatar. This agreement aimed to facilitate the withdrawal of U.S. troops from Afghanistan and initiate intra-Afghan negotiations.
events.name: U.S.-Taliban peace agreement

events.enhanced_description: On March 2, 2020, the Yahoo! Time capsule, which contained various digital artifacts from 2006, was opened. This event marked a nostalgic look back at the early days of the internet and the evolution of digital culture.
events.name: Opening of the Yahoo! Time capsule

events.enhanced_description: On March 5, 2020, the International Criminal Court authorized an inquiry into war crimes in Afghanistan, allowing for the investigation of U.S. citizens for the first time. This decision was significant in the context of international law and accountability.
events.name: International Criminal Court authorizes Afghanistan War Crimes inquiry

events.enhanced_description: On March 9, 2020, Italy became the first country to implement a nationwide quarantine in response to the COVID-19 outbreak. This unprecedented measure aimed to curb the spread of the virus and protect public health.
events.name: Italy implements nationwide quarantine

events.enhanced_description: On March 11, 2020, the World Health Organization officially declared the COVID-19 outbreak a pandemic, recognizing the global spread of the virus and the urgent need for coordinated international response efforts.
events.name: WHO declares COVID-19 a pandemic

events.enhanced_description: On March 12, 2020, global stock markets crashed due to the COVID-19 pandemic and the United States travel ban on the Schengen Area. The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell by over 2,300 points, marking the worst loss for the index since 1987.
events.name: Global stock market crash

events.enhanced_description: On March 13, 2020, the government of Nepal announced the closure of Mount Everest to climbers and the public for the remainder of the season due to concerns about the COVID-19 pandemic. This decision impacted many climbers and the local economy reliant on tourism.
events.name: Nepal closes Mount Everest

events.enhanced_description: On March 16, 2020, the Dow Jones Industrial Average experienced a historic drop of 2,997.10 points, marking the largest single-point drop in history at that time. This decline was a reaction to the escalating COVID-19 pandemic and economic uncertainty.
events.name: DJIA falls by 2,997

events.enhanced_description: On March 17, 2020, the COVID-19 pandemic continued to escalate, affecting countries worldwide and leading to widespread health and economic crises. Governments around the world were implementing measures to curb the spread of the virus.
events.name: COVID-19 pandemic

events.enhanced_description: In response to the COVID-19 pandemic, the European Union announced the closure of its external and Schengen borders for at least 30 days, marking a significant measure to curb the spread of the virus across member states.
events.name: Closure of EU Borders due to COVID-19

events.enhanced_description: The UEFA and CONMEBOL announced the postponement of Euro 2020 and the Copa América tournaments until the summer of 2021 due to the COVID-19 pandemic, impacting millions of fans and players worldwide.
events.name: Postponement of Euro 2020 and Copa América

events.enhanced_description: The Eurovision Song Contest 2020 was cancelled due to the COVID-19 pandemic, marking the first cancellation in the contest's 64-year history, which typically draws millions of viewers across Europe.
events.name: Cancellation of Eurovision Song Contest 2020

events.enhanced_description: The World Health Organization announced the Solidarity Trial, a global clinical trial aimed at finding effective treatments for COVID-19, involving multiple countries and healthcare systems.
events.name: Announcement of the Solidarity Trial

events.enhanced_description: As the COVID-19 pandemic escalated, the worldwide death toll surpassed 10,000, with total cases reaching a quarter of a million, highlighting the severity of the global health crisis.
events.name: COVID-19 Death Toll Surpasses 10,000

events.enhanced_description: The Bhadla Solar Park in Rajasthan, India, was commissioned, becoming the world's largest solar park and a significant step towards renewable energy production in the country.
events.name: Commissioning of Bhadla Solar Park

events.enhanced_description: On March 20, 2020, the worldwide death toll from the COVID-19 pandemic surpassed 10,000, with total cases reaching a quarter of a million. This grim milestone underscored the severity of the global health crisis.
events.name: COVID-19 pandemic: Worldwide death toll surpasses 10,000

events.enhanced_description: On March 24, 2020, the European Union announced the closure of its external and Schengen borders for at least 30 days in an effort to curb the COVID-19 pandemic. This decision significantly impacted travel and trade across Europe.
events.name: COVID-19 pandemic: EU closes borders

events.enhanced_description: In response to the COVID-19 pandemic, both India and the United Kingdom implemented nationwide lockdowns, affecting over 2.6 billion people globally and marking a critical moment in the fight against the virus.
events.name: Lockdown in India and the United Kingdom

events.enhanced_description: Chinese Premier Li Keqiang announced that the domestically transmitted COVID-19 epidemic was under control, reflecting the country's efforts to manage the outbreak.
events.name: Chinese Premier Reports Epidemic Under Control

events.enhanced_description: The International Olympic Committee and Japan announced the postponement of the 2020 Summer Olympics to 2021 due to the COVID-19 pandemic, a historic decision affecting athletes worldwide.
events.name: Postponement of the 2020 Summer Olympics

events.enhanced_description: The global number of confirmed COVID-19 cases reached 500,000, with nearly 23,000 deaths reported, as the pandemic continued to spread rapidly across countries.
events.name: Global COVID-19 Cases Reach 500,000

events.enhanced_description: On March 27, 2020, North Macedonia officially became the 30th member of NATO, marking a significant milestone in the country's integration into Euro-Atlantic structures. This membership was seen as a step towards enhancing regional security.
events.name: North Macedonia joins NATO

events.enhanced_description: On March 30, 2020, the price of Brent Crude oil fell by 9% to $23 per barrel, the lowest level since November 2002, amid the ongoing oil price war between Russia and Saudi Arabia. This decline had significant implications for the global oil market.
events.name: 2020 Russia–Saudi Arabia oil price war

events.enhanced_description: By April 2020, the global death toll from COVID-19 surpassed 100,000, reflecting a ten-fold increase from March 20. This alarming statistic prompted EU finance ministers to agree on a €540 billion loan package aimed at alleviating the economic fallout from the pandemic.
events.name: COVID-19 death toll exceeds 100,000 globally

events.enhanced_description: On April 5, 2020, the first known case of COVID-19 in a zoo animal was reported at the Bronx Zoo, where a four-year-old female Malayan tiger tested positive for the virus. This case highlighted the potential for zoonotic transmission of the virus from humans to animals.
events.name: First case of COVID-19 in a zoo animal

events.enhanced_description: The United States designated the Russian Imperial Movement as a terrorist organization, marking a significant step in addressing white supremacist groups and their activities.
events.name: U.S. Designates Russian Imperial Movement as Terrorist

events.enhanced_description: In response to the COVID-19 pandemic, Japan declared a state of emergency and finalized a substantial stimulus package, aiming to mitigate the economic impact of the crisis.
events.name: Japan Declares State of Emergency

events.enhanced_description: The Saudi-led coalition announced a unilateral ceasefire in Yemen, aligning with United Nations-led efforts to address the humanitarian crisis exacerbated by the COVID-19 pandemic.
events.name: Saudi-led Coalition Declares Ceasefire in Yemen

events.enhanced_description: In response to the economic challenges posed by the COVID-19 pandemic, EU finance ministers reached an agreement on a €540 billion loan package on April 9, 2020. This package was designed to support member states and mitigate the financial impact of the crisis.
events.name: EU finance ministers agree on loan package

events.enhanced_description: The Democratic Republic of the Congo reported its first case of Ebola since February 2020, amid an ongoing outbreak that has claimed over 2,200 lives since August 2018.
events.name: First Case of Ebola Reported in DRC

events.enhanced_description: On April 12, 2020, Pope Francis livestreamed the Urbi et Orbi blessing for Easter, marking the second such blessing in a month due to the COVID-19 pandemic. The first blessing occurred on March 27, during a special prayer service aimed at seeking an end to the pandemic.
events.name: Pope Francis Livestreams Urbi et Orbi Blessing

events.enhanced_description: On April 12, 2020, OPEC and its allies reached a historic agreement to cut oil production by 9.7 million barrels per day, the largest cut ever agreed upon. This decision was made in response to the plummeting demand for oil due to the COVID-19 pandemic.
events.name: OPEC oil production cut agreement

events.enhanced_description: On April 14, 2020, the International Monetary Fund (IMF) projected that the global economy would shrink by 3% due to the COVID-19 pandemic, marking the worst contraction since the Great Depression of the 1930s. This forecast highlighted the severe economic impact of the ongoing health crisis.
events.name: IMF predicts global economic contraction due to COVID-19

events.enhanced_description: On April 15, 2020, South Korea held its legislative election, where the Democratic Party of Korea-Platform Party alliance secured a significant victory, winning 180 out of 300 seats in the National Assembly. This election was notable for its high voter turnout and was conducted amid the COVID-19 pandemic, showcasing South Korea's effective public health measures.
events.name: South Korean Legislative Election

events.enhanced_description: On April 19, 2020, unrest erupted in major cities including Paris, Berlin, and Vladikavkaz as public opposition to COVID-19 lockdown measures intensified. Demonstrators expressed their frustrations over restrictions and the impact of the pandemic on their daily lives.
events.name: COVID-19 pandemic unrest in major cities

events.enhanced_description: On April 20, 2020, the ESA/JAXA space probe BepiColombo completed its final gravity assist maneuver around Earth, marking a significant milestone in its mission to explore Mercury. The spacecraft is set to make several gravity assists around Venus before arriving at Mercury in 2025.
events.name: BepiColombo's final gravity assist around Earth

events.enhanced_description: In early January 2020, oil prices reached a record low, with West Texas Intermediate falling into negative values for the first time in history. This unprecedented drop was largely attributed to a collapse in demand due to the COVID-19 pandemic and oversupply issues.
events.name: Record low oil prices

events.enhanced_description: On April 21, 2020, police in Mozambique reported that 52 male villagers were killed by Islamist militants in Muidumbe District after they refused to join the militants' ranks. This incident highlighted the ongoing violence and instability in the Cabo Delgado Province.
events.name: Mass killings in Mozambique

events.enhanced_description: On April 22, 2020, Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps successfully deployed the country's first military satellite using a new satellite carrier named 'Ghased' (Messenger). This event marked a significant step in Iran's military capabilities and ambitions in space.
events.name: Iran's military satellite deployment

events.enhanced_description: On April 23, 2020, two former high-ranking members of the Syrian Army went on trial in Koblenz, Germany, for alleged war crimes committed during the Syrian Civil War. This trial marked a historic moment as it was the first time Syrian military officials faced prosecution for their actions during the conflict.
events.name: Trial of Syrian Army officials for war crimes

events.enhanced_description: On April 25, 2020, the Southern Transitional Council (STC) announced the establishment of a self-rule administration in southern Yemen, deploying forces in Aden. This declaration was met with resistance from governors of multiple southern governorates who pledged loyalty to President Abdrabbuh Mansur Hadi.
events.name: Southern Transitional Council declares self-rule in Yemen

events.enhanced_description: On April 26, 2020, King Salman of Saudi Arabia issued a royal decree stating that individuals convicted of crimes committed while they were minors will no longer face execution. This decree represents a significant shift in the country's approach to juvenile justice.
events.name: Saudi Arabia bans execution for juvenile crimes

events.enhanced_description: On April 27, 2020, the number of confirmed COVID-19 cases worldwide surpassed 3 million, with over 1 million cases reported in the United States alone. This milestone underscored the global scale of the pandemic and the urgent need for effective public health responses.
events.name: COVID-19 cases surpass 3 million worldwide

events.enhanced_description: On April 28, 2020, astronomers detected a fast radio burst originating from the Magnetar SGR 1935+2154, marking the first such event detected within the Milky Way galaxy. This discovery provided new insights into the nature of these mysterious cosmic phenomena.
events.name: Detection of fast radio burst from Magnetar SGR 1935+2154

events.enhanced_description: On April 29, 2020, the near-Earth asteroid (52768) 1998 OR2, measuring approximately 2 kilometers in width, made a close approach to Earth at a distance of 0.042 AU (about 6.3 million kilometers). This event was notable as it will not approach closer than this until 2079.
events.name: Close approach of near-Earth asteroid 1998 OR2

events.enhanced_description: On April 30, 2020, NASA officially selected SpaceX, Blue Origin, and Dynetics to develop its next-generation lunar lander, which aims to carry American astronauts to the Moon by 2024. This decision is part of NASA's Artemis program to return humans to the lunar surface.
events.name: NASA selects companies for lunar lander development

events.enhanced_description: By May 2020, the total number of recovered COVID-19 patients worldwide reached 1 million, according to data from The Johns Hopkins University. This milestone indicated progress in the fight against the pandemic, although challenges remained.
events.name: COVID-19 Recovered Patients Reach 1 Million

events.enhanced_description: On May 2, 2020, the United Nations published a report stating that Russia's indiscriminate bombing of civilians in Syria constitutes a war crime, highlighting the ongoing humanitarian crisis and the impact of military actions on civilian populations.
events.name: United Nations report on Russia's bombing in Syria

events.enhanced_description: On May 3, 2020, Venezuelan dissidents, in collaboration with the North American private military company Silvercorp USA, attempted to infiltrate Venezuela and forcibly remove President Nicolás Maduro from office. The operation was unsuccessful and led to significant political fallout.
events.name: Failed invasion attempt in Venezuela

events.enhanced_description: On May 4, 2020, a team of British and Kenyan scientists announced the discovery of Microsporidia MB, a parasitic microbe that blocks mosquitoes from carrying malaria. This discovery has the potential to significantly impact malaria control efforts.
events.name: Discovery of Microsporidia MB

events.enhanced_description: On May 5, 2020, the UK reported a COVID-19 death toll of 32,313, surpassing Italy's toll of 29,029, marking the highest death toll in Europe during the pandemic and raising concerns about the government's response to the crisis.
events.name: COVID-19 death toll in the UK

events.enhanced_description: On May 6, 2020, astronomers announced the discovery of the first black hole located in a star system visible to the naked eye, marking a significant milestone in astrophysics and enhancing our understanding of the universe.
events.name: Discovery of the first visible black hole

events.enhanced_description: On May 8, 2020, the Aurangabad railway accident occurred in India, resulting in the tragic deaths of 16 migrants who were sleeping on the tracks when a freight train collided with them, highlighting the dangers faced by migrant workers during the COVID-19 pandemic.

image.caption: Aurangabad railway station.
image.date_qualification: Photograph of the railway station, a site associated with the accident; taken before the 2020 accident.
image.rights_statement: LicenseShortName: CC BY-SA 4.0; UsageTerms: Creative Commons Attribution-Share Alike 4.0; Copyrighted: True

events.name: Aurangabad railway accident

events.enhanced_description: On May 9, 2020, a cross-border clash occurred at the Nathu La crossing between Chinese and Indian soldiers, resulting in injuries to several troops. The confrontation involved approximately 150 soldiers and escalated tensions between the two nations.
events.name: Nathu La clash

events.enhanced_description: On May 10, 2020, the Iranian Navy frigate Jamaran accidentally struck the Iranian support vessel Konarak with a missile, resulting in the deaths of nineteen sailors. This incident marked a significant case of friendly fire within the Iranian military.
events.name: Friendly fire incident involving Iranian Navy

events.enhanced_description: On May 11, 2020, the Max Planck Institute for Evolutionary Anthropology published results from radiocarbon and DNA analysis of fossils found in the Bacho Kiro cave, indicating that modern humans may have arrived in Europe thousands of years earlier than previously thought.
events.name: Max Planck Institute findings in Bulgaria

events.enhanced_description: On May 12, 2020, gunmen stormed a maternity hospital in the Dashte Barchi neighborhood of Kabul, Afghanistan, killing 24 people, including two newborns. This brutal attack highlighted the ongoing violence in the region and the targeting of vulnerable populations.
events.name: Attack on maternity hospital in Kabul

events.enhanced_description: On May 14, 2020, the COVID-19 pandemic continued to affect countries worldwide, with various updates on case numbers and recovery rates being reported, reflecting the ongoing global health crisis.
events.name: COVID-19 pandemic updates

events.enhanced_description: On May 15, 2020, researchers announced the discovery of a 2.5 cm millipede fossil belonging to the Kampecaris genus on the island of Kerrera, which is believed to be the world's oldest-known land animal, dating back 425 million years to the Silurian period.
events.name: Discovery of ancient millipede fossil

events.enhanced_description: On May 16, 2020, Félicien Kabuga, a Rwandan businessman accused of supporting the Rwandan genocide, was arrested in Asnières-sur-Seine, France, after 26 years as a fugitive, marking a significant moment in the pursuit of justice for genocide victims.
events.name: Arrest of Félicien Kabuga

events.enhanced_description: On May 18, 2020, the United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs announced that nearly 1 million people were affected by flash floods in Beledweyne and Jowhar, Somalia, resulting in at least 24 deaths and highlighting the humanitarian crisis in the region.
events.name: Flash floods in Somalia

events.enhanced_description: On May 19, 2020, Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas announced the termination of all agreements with Israel and the United States in response to Israel's plans to annex the Jordan Valley, escalating tensions in the region.
events.name: Palestinian President's announcement

events.enhanced_description: On May 21, 2020, Cyclone Amphan made landfall in eastern India and Bangladesh, resulting in over 100 fatalities and the evacuation of more than 4 million people. It caused over $13 billion in damage, making it the costliest cyclone recorded in the North Indian Ocean.
events.name: Cyclone Amphan landfall

events.enhanced_description: On May 22, 2020, Flight PK8303, a Pakistan International Airlines passenger aircraft, crashed in a residential area near Karachi, killing 97 of the 99 people on board and injuring dozens on the ground, raising concerns about aviation safety in the region.
events.name: Pakistan International Airlines crash

events.enhanced_description: On May 23, 2020, China reported no new COVID-19 cases for the first time since the pandemic began, according to the National Health Commission, marking a significant milestone in the country's battle against the virus.
events.name: China reports no new COVID-19 cases

events.enhanced_description: On May 24, 2020, mining corporation Rio Tinto admitted to blowing up the 46,000-year-old Juukan Gorge caves in the Pilbara region of Western Australia, leading to widespread condemnation and raising issues regarding the protection of Indigenous heritage.
events.name: Destruction of Juukan Gorge caves

events.enhanced_description: On May 25, 2020, the 2020 Surinamese general election was held to elect all 51 members of the National Assembly of Suriname, a significant event in the country's democratic process.
events.name: 2020 Surinamese general election

events.enhanced_description: On May 26, 2020, protests erupted across hundreds of cities in the United States and around the world in response to the murder of George Floyd, highlighting issues of racism and police brutality.
events.name: Protests following George Floyd's murder

events.enhanced_description: On May 27, 2020, the Chinese National People's Congress voted in favor of national security legislation that criminalizes secession, subversion, terrorism, and foreign interference in Hong Kong, granting sweeping powers to the central government and escalating tensions with pro-democracy activists.
events.name: National security legislation in Hong Kong

events.enhanced_description: On May 30, 2020, the first crewed flight of the SpaceX Dragon 2 was launched from Cape Canaveral, Florida, marking the first crewed spacecraft to take off from U.S. soil since the retirement of the Space Shuttle in 2011, a significant milestone in commercial space travel.
events.name: SpaceX Dragon 2 crewed flight

events.enhanced_description: On June 1, 2020, the World Health Organization reported six new cases of Ebola and five deaths in a renewed outbreak in Mbandaka, Équateur Province, Democratic Republic of the Congo. This resurgence raised concerns about the ongoing challenges of controlling infectious diseases in the region.
events.name: Kivu Ebola epidemic: WHO reports new cases of Ebola in Mbandaka, Democratic Republic of the Congo

events.enhanced_description: By June 2020, the COVID-19 pandemic had escalated dramatically, with confirmed cases surpassing 9 million worldwide. This milestone highlighted the urgent need for global health responses and the impact of the virus on societies across the globe.
events.name: COVID-19 pandemic: Global cases surpass 9 million

events.enhanced_description: The Malawian presidential election in June 2020 saw Lazarus Chakwera of the Malawi Congress Party elected as president. This election was a significant moment in Malawi's democratic journey, following a controversial previous election that led to a court ruling for a rerun.
events.name: Malawian presidential election

events.enhanced_description: The Icelandic presidential election held in June 2020 resulted in the reelection of incumbent president Guðni Th. Jóhannesson. His continued leadership was seen as a stabilizing factor for Iceland during a time of global uncertainty.
events.name: Icelandic presidential election

events.enhanced_description: The first round of voting for the 2020 Polish presidential election took place in June 2020, setting the stage for a highly contested race. This election was critical in determining the future political direction of Poland amidst various domestic and international challenges.
events.name: First round of voting in the 2020 Polish presidential election

events.enhanced_description: On June 2, 2020, a class action lawsuit was filed against Alphabet Inc. and its subsidiary Google, alleging violations of user privacy rights by tracking users in Chrome's incognito mode. This lawsuit highlighted growing concerns over digital privacy and the responsibilities of tech giants in safeguarding user data.
events.name: Class action lawsuit against Alphabet Inc.

events.enhanced_description: On June 3, 2020, UK Prime Minister Boris Johnson announced plans to amend immigration laws to provide a pathway to citizenship for Hong Kong citizens eligible for British National (Overseas) status. This decision was a direct response to China's imposition of new security laws in Hong Kong, reflecting the UK's commitment to support its former colony.
events.name: UK immigration law changes for Hong Kong citizens

events.enhanced_description: On June 4, 2020, Libya's Government of National Accord (GNA) announced it had regained full control of Tripoli following the retreat of the Libyan National Army (LNA) after months of intense conflict. This marked a significant turning point in the ongoing Libyan civil war, which has seen various factions vying for power since the fall of Muammar Gaddafi in 2011.
events.name: GNA claims control of Tripoli

events.enhanced_description: On June 7, 2020, the global death toll from the COVID-19 pandemic surpassed 400,000, highlighting the severe impact of the virus worldwide. This grim milestone underscored the urgent need for effective public health measures and vaccine development to combat the pandemic.
events.name: COVID-19 global death toll exceeds 400,000

events.enhanced_description: On June 8, 2020, the number of confirmed COVID-19 cases worldwide exceeded 7 million, reflecting the rapid spread of the virus across the globe. This surge in cases prompted renewed discussions on public health strategies and the importance of social distancing and hygiene practices.
events.name: COVID-19 confirmed cases surpass 7 million

events.enhanced_description: On June 9, 2020, a study conducted by Harvard University suggested that COVID-19 may have been spreading in China as early as August 2019, based on analysis of hospital car park usage and web search trends. This research raised questions about the timeline of the outbreak and the global response to the pandemic.

locations.name: Harvard University, Cambridge, Massachusetts, United States

events.name: Harvard study on COVID-19 spread in China

events.enhanced_description: On June 15, 2020, a violent skirmish in the disputed Galwan Valley resulted in the deaths and injuries of at least 20 Indian soldiers and over 40 Chinese forces. This incident marked the largest escalation along the Sino-Indian border in five decades, heightening tensions between the two nuclear-armed neighbors.
events.name: Galwan Valley skirmishes

events.enhanced_description: On June 16, 2020, the number of confirmed COVID-19 cases worldwide surpassed 8 million, indicating the ongoing severity of the pandemic. This milestone prompted further discussions on the effectiveness of containment measures and the need for global cooperation in health responses.
events.name: COVID-19 confirmed cases surpass 8 million

events.enhanced_description: On June 22, 2020, the number of confirmed COVID-19 cases worldwide exceeded 9 million, further illustrating the pandemic's relentless spread. This alarming statistic underscored the critical need for continued public health efforts and vaccine development.
events.name: COVID-19 confirmed cases surpass 9 million

events.enhanced_description: On June 24, 2020, Mongolia held its legislative election, resulting in the ruling Mongolian People's Party winning 62 out of 76 seats in the State Great Khural. This election reinforced the party's dominance in Mongolian politics amidst ongoing economic challenges.
events.name: Mongolian legislative election

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2020, Micheál Martin succeeded Leo Varadkar as Taoiseach of Ireland, marking a significant political transition within a historic three-party coalition government. This change in leadership was crucial for addressing Ireland's challenges, including Brexit and the COVID-19 pandemic.
events.name: Micheál Martin becomes Taoiseach

events.enhanced_description: On June 30, 2020, China passed the controversial Hong Kong national security law, which allowed the government to crack down on dissent both locally and internationally. This legislation was met with widespread criticism and protests, as it was seen as a significant erosion of the freedoms promised to Hong Kong under the 'one country, two systems' principle.

locations.name: Hong Kong, Special Administrative Region, China

events.name: Hong Kong national security law passed

events.enhanced_description: By July 2020, the number of confirmed COVID-19 cases worldwide surpassed 10 million, with the United States reporting the highest number of cases. This milestone underscored the pandemic's extensive reach and the urgent need for effective public health measures.
events.name: COVID-19 pandemic: Global cases surpass 10 million

events.enhanced_description: In July 2020, the global death toll from the COVID-19 pandemic exceeded 500,000, marking a tragic milestone in the ongoing health crisis. This statistic highlighted the severe impact of the virus on global health systems and communities.
events.name: Global death toll from COVID-19 exceeds 500,000

events.enhanced_description: In July 2020, Russian voters approved a constitutional amendment that allows President Vladimir Putin to potentially remain in power until 2036. This vote was seen as a pivotal moment in Russian politics, raising concerns about the future of democracy in the country.
events.name: Russian constitutional amendment vote

events.enhanced_description: In July 2020, former Prime Minister of Malaysia Najib Razak was found guilty of all charges in the first of five trials related to the 1MDB scandal, resulting in a 12-year prison sentence and a fine of RM210 million. This verdict was a landmark moment in Malaysia's fight against corruption.
events.name: Najib Razak found guilty in 1MDB scandal

events.enhanced_description: In July 2020, the Dominican Republic held its general election, resulting in the election of Luis Abinader from the Modern Revolutionary Party as president. This election was pivotal for the country's political landscape and governance.

events.enhanced_description: Beginning in July 2020, widespread protests erupted across Bulgaria aimed at removing Prime Minister Boyko Borisov's cabinet and Chief Prosecutor Ivan Geshev from office. These protests reflected deep-seated public dissatisfaction with corruption and governance issues.
events.name: Protests in Bulgaria

events.enhanced_description: In July 2020, at least 180 bodies were discovered in mass graves in Djibo, Burkina Faso, amid ongoing conflicts with jihadist groups. The findings raised serious concerns about human rights violations and the conduct of government forces in the region.
events.name: Mass graves found in Djibo, Burkina Faso

events.enhanced_description: In July 2020, the European Central Bank accepted Bulgaria and Croatia into the Exchange Rate Mechanism II (ERM II), a crucial step for both countries on their path to adopting the euro. This decision marked a significant milestone in the economic integration of these nations into the European Union.
events.name: ECB accepts Bulgaria and Croatia into ERM II

events.enhanced_description: The second round of voting for the 2020 Polish presidential election took place in July 2020, resulting in the reelection of incumbent president Andrzej Duda. This election was pivotal in determining Poland's political future amidst rising tensions and challenges.
events.name: Second round of voting in the 2020 Polish presidential election

events.enhanced_description: In July 2020, a significant security breach occurred when the Twitter accounts of prominent political figures, CEOs, and celebrities were hacked to promote a bitcoin scam. This incident raised alarms about cybersecurity and the vulnerabilities of social media platforms.
events.name: Twitter accounts hacked for bitcoin scam

events.enhanced_description: In July 2020, severe flooding of the Brahmaputra River resulted in the deaths of 189 people and left 4 million homeless across India and Nepal. This disaster highlighted the ongoing challenges posed by climate change and natural disasters in the region.
events.name: Flooding of the Brahmaputra River

events.enhanced_description: In July 2020, European leaders reached an agreement to create a €750 billion recovery fund aimed at rebuilding EU economies impacted by the COVID-19 pandemic. This landmark decision was seen as a crucial step towards economic recovery and solidarity within the European Union.
events.name: EU recovery fund agreement

events.enhanced_description: By late July 2020, the number of confirmed COVID-19 cases worldwide surpassed 15 million, reflecting the ongoing severity of the pandemic. This milestone underscored the need for continued public health efforts and international cooperation.
